==> packages/db/sql/035_copy_eligibility_policy.sql <==
-- 035_copy_eligibility_policy.sql
-- Durable record of why a signal was refused at the canonical copy-execution
-- claim boundary, one row per (account, signal).
--
-- The reason has to outlive the process that decided it: `signals.status` alone
-- says a signal was rejected but not which gate rejected it, so an operator
-- reading the table after the fact cannot tell a paused source wallet from a
-- dormant one. The primary key is (account, signal_id) because eligibility is
-- account-scoped (Standing Rule 2) — the same signal can be copyable for one
-- account and not another.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only, no data rewrite.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_eligibility_rejections (
  account        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'operator',
  signal_id      UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES signals(id),
  chain          VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
  wallet_address VARCHAR(100),
  reasons        TEXT[]       NOT NULL,
  rejected_at    TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (account, signal_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_eligibility_rejections_rejected
  ON copy_eligibility_rejections(rejected_at DESC);

==> packages/db/sql/036_transactions_brin.sql <==
-- 036_transactions_brin.sql
-- BRIN index on the append-ordered `transactions.timestamp`.
--
-- Rows arrive in near-timestamp order, so each block range holds a narrow
-- min/max — the access pattern BRIN is built for. It is a fraction of a btree's
-- size at this table's growth rate, and range scans over recent activity are
-- the dominant read.
--
-- The existing btrees in 001_init.sql are kept: they cover
-- (wallet_address, timestamp DESC) and (target_token, timestamp DESC), which
-- BRIN cannot serve because it has no per-row pointers to filter a single
-- wallet by.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_timestamp_brin
  ON transactions USING BRIN (timestamp);

==> packages/db/sql/037_pg_stat_statements.sql <==
-- 037_pg_stat_statements.sql
-- Query-level visibility, so a slow query can be found before per-user volume
-- multiplies it.
--
-- The extension needs the library preloaded at server start
-- (`shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements`, set in docker-compose.yml).
-- A database without it — a managed instance that has not enabled the library,
-- or the ephemeral CI Postgres — would otherwise fail this migration and every
-- one after it, so the CREATE is wrapped and downgraded to a notice. Losing
-- observability must not block a schema change.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS.

DO $$
BEGIN
  CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;
EXCEPTION
  WHEN insufficient_privilege OR undefined_file OR feature_not_supported THEN
    RAISE NOTICE
      'pg_stat_statements unavailable (%); set shared_preload_libraries and re-run.',
      SQLERRM;
END $$;

==> packages/db/sql/038_venue_settlement_status.sql <==
-- Distinct settlement state for a venue order whose trades have not reached
-- finality. `venue_status` carries the ORDER status (live/matched/delayed);
-- this carries the SETTLEMENT status of the associated trades, which the venue
-- advances independently: MATCHED -> MINED -> CONFIRMED, with RETRYING when a
-- submitted transaction failed and is being resubmitted.
--
-- Collapsing those into one "pending" bucket loses the operational distinction
-- an operator needs during an incident: "matched, not yet onchain" and
-- "mined, awaiting finality" and "onchain attempt failed, retrying" are three
-- very different positions to be holding.
--
-- Only CONFIRMED ever creates a fill quantity; this column is diagnostic and
-- never a substitute for confirmed evidence.
ALTER TABLE trades
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS venue_settlement_status VARCHAR(32);

==> packages/db/sql/039_users.sql <==
-- 039_users.sql
-- Tenant root. One row per account; every per-user table references this id.
--
-- CITEXT rather than a lowercased VARCHAR: case-insensitive uniqueness is a
-- property of the column, so `Alice@x.com` and `alice@x.com` cannot both
-- register regardless of which call site writes them. A functional index would
-- leave the raw column able to hold either form.
--
-- password_hash is TEXT, not VARCHAR(n): an argon2id encoded hash carries its
-- own parameters, so its length changes whenever those are tuned.
--
-- tier_expires_at IS NULL means LIFETIME (the USDC lifetime tier), not expired.
-- Stage 5's nightly downgrade sweep must read it that way.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only, no data rewrite. Seeds nothing --
-- the admin user is created by a separate step so this file stays deployable
-- on its own.

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citext;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id              UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email           CITEXT       NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  password_hash   TEXT         NOT NULL,
  display_name    VARCHAR(64),
  role            VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',
  tier            VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',
  tier_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  status          VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CONSTRAINT chk_users_role   CHECK (role IN ('user','admin')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_users_tier   CHECK (tier IN ('free','operator','ultra')),
  -- 'deleted' is a soft delete. A user with trades cannot be hard-deleted
  -- without breaking the immutable financial trail (D13).
  CONSTRAINT chk_users_status CHECK (status IN ('active','suspended','deleted'))
);

-- Partial: only rows that can expire are of interest to the downgrade sweep.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_tier_expiry
  ON users(tier_expires_at) WHERE tier_expires_at IS NOT NULL;

==> packages/db/sql/040_user_sessions.sql <==
-- 040_user_sessions.sql
-- Opaque, revocable sessions. The raw token lives in an httpOnly cookie and
-- nowhere else -- only its SHA-256 digest is stored, so a database dump cannot
-- be replayed as a login.
--
-- SHA-256 rather than argon2 is correct HERE and only here: the token is 32
-- bytes of CSPRNG output, so there is no low-entropy secret for a slow hash to
-- protect. Passwords (039) use argon2id for the opposite reason.
--
-- ON DELETE CASCADE is safe on sessions specifically -- a session carries no
-- financial meaning. It is deliberately NOT used on trades/copy_executions,
-- where the row must outlive the account (D13, ADR-0001).
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_sessions (
  id           UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id      UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  token_hash   BYTEA        NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  issued_at    TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,
  -- Set rather than deleted, so logout-everywhere and forced revocation on
  -- password change leave a trail instead of erasing one.
  revoked_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  ip           INET,
  user_agent   VARCHAR(256)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_user
  ON user_sessions(user_id);

-- Drives both the idle/absolute expiry sweep and the revoke-all-for-user path.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_sessions_expiry
  ON user_sessions(expires_at);

==> packages/db/sql/041_user_auth_wallets.sql <==
-- 041_user_auth_wallets.sql
-- Identity wallets: an address the user has proven control of via SIWE
-- (EIP-4361) or SIWS. These are NOT tracked wallets -- they authenticate a
-- person and, from Stage 4, are the only permitted withdrawal destinations.
--
-- UNIQUE is (chain_kind, address) GLOBALLY, not per user. One wallet proves one
-- identity. Without this, two accounts could each claim the same address and
-- Stage 4's withdraw-to-linked-wallet-only control would have no single answer
-- to "whose address is this?" -- which is the control's entire premise.
--
-- chain_kind, not chain: an EVM signature proves control of that address on
-- every EVM chain at once, so pinning a linked wallet to `polygon` rather than
-- `robinhood-chain` would be arbitrary and wrong.
--
-- Addresses here are NOT chain-prefixed. The repo-wide `${chain}:${address}`
-- invariant governs tracked wallets and transactions; chain_kind already
-- carries the discriminator for identity. Write EVM lowercased and Solana
-- case-preserved, matching resolveChainAddress semantics.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_auth_wallets (
  id          UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id     UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chain_kind  VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,
  address     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CONSTRAINT chk_auth_wallet_kind CHECK (chain_kind IN ('evm','solana')),
  CONSTRAINT uq_auth_wallet UNIQUE (chain_kind, address)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_auth_wallets_user
  ON user_auth_wallets(user_id);

==> packages/db/sql/042_user_api_keys.sql <==
-- 042_user_api_keys.sql
-- Per-user programmatic credentials, replacing the single shared API_KEY for
-- user-facing routes. Key format: swat_<prefix>_<secret>.
--
-- key_prefix is stored, indexed and UNIQUE so that verifying a presented key is
-- one indexed equality followed by one constant-time hash compare. The naive
-- alternative -- scan every key row and compare hashes -- degrades linearly
-- with key count and turns verification into a timing oracle.
--
-- Only the SHA-256 digest of the full key is stored; the secret is displayed
-- once at creation and is unrecoverable afterwards. Same reasoning as
-- user_sessions.token_hash: high-entropy credential, so a fast hash is right.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_api_keys (
  id           UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id      UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name         VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
  key_prefix   VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  key_hash     BYTEA        NOT NULL,
  last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_api_keys_user
  ON user_api_keys(user_id);

==> packages/db/sql/043_audit_log.sql <==
-- 043_audit_log.sql
-- Append-only record of auth, custody, billing, and admin events.
--
-- Built now, before there is anything to log, on purpose (D10/D13): it is cheap
-- today and impossible to reconstruct retroactively. It is also the D13
-- compliance trail, so it must be the most durable table here.
--
-- NO foreign key on actor_id, deliberately:
--   * the log must outlive the user row it describes (soft delete, and later
--     hard deletion of a user with no financial rows), and
--   * a failed login for an email that does not exist has no user to reference
--     -- and that is precisely the event worth keeping when investigating
--     credential stuffing.
-- An FK here would either lose those rows or block the delete.
--
-- Append-only is convention in Stage 1 and becomes enforced when the app
-- database role is split out in Stage 0's D10 hardening (revoke UPDATE/DELETE).
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
  id          BIGSERIAL    PRIMARY KEY,
  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  actor_type  VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,
  actor_id    UUID,
  event       VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
  target_type VARCHAR(32),
  target_id   VARCHAR(128),
  ip          INET,
  user_agent  VARCHAR(256),
  metadata    JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  -- 'anonymous' covers pre-authentication events (failed logins, nonce
  -- requests) where no actor is yet established.
  CONSTRAINT chk_audit_actor CHECK (actor_type IN ('user','admin','service','anonymous'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_occurred
  ON audit_log(occurred_at DESC);

-- "What did this actor do?" -- the account-investigation query.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_actor
  ON audit_log(actor_id, occurred_at DESC);

-- "Who is failing logins right now?" -- the abuse-detection query.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_log_event
  ON audit_log(event, occurred_at DESC);

==> packages/db/sql/044_user_wallet_subscriptions.sql <==
-- 044_user_wallet_subscriptions.sql
-- Per-user tracking, on a global-dedup model (D9).
--
-- `wallets`, `transactions`, clusters, and scoring stay GLOBAL: one wallet is
-- indexed once no matter how many users track it. Subscription is a join, never
-- a copy — that is what keeps indexing cost sublinear in user count.
--
-- The primary key is (user_id, wallet_address) rather than a surrogate id
-- because the pair IS the fact; there is no such thing as two distinct
-- subscriptions by one user to one wallet.
--
-- ON DELETE CASCADE on both sides is safe HERE because a subscription is a
-- preference, not a financial record. The same is emphatically not true of
-- trades/copy_executions, which must outlive the account (D13, ADR-0001).
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_wallet_subscriptions (
  user_id        UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)      ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- wallets.address is the table's own primary key and is chain-prefixed
  -- (`${chain}:${raw}`). Never store a bare address here.
  wallet_address VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES wallets(address) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  label          VARCHAR(64),
  source         VARCHAR(24)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',
  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, wallet_address),
  CONSTRAINT chk_subscription_source
    CHECK (source IN ('manual','platform-signal','discovered'))
);

-- Reverse lookup: "does this wallet have any subscribers?" The nightly pause
-- sweep asks that for every wallet, so it must not be a sequential scan.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_uws_wallet
  ON user_wallet_subscriptions(wallet_address);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_uws_user_created
  ON user_wallet_subscriptions(user_id, created_at DESC);

==> packages/db/sql/045_user_token_watches.sql <==
-- 045_user_token_watches.sql
-- Per-user token-contract backfills. Feeds the existing swat-token-discovery
-- queue; wallets discovered as early/large buyers are auto-subscribed for the
-- requesting user with source 'discovered'.
--
-- Surrogate primary key here, unlike 044: a watch carries lifecycle state that
-- outlives its identity, and the daily-quota query counts rows by created_at.
--
-- UNIQUE (user_id, chain, token_mint) makes re-requesting the same backfill
-- idempotent rather than burning a day's quota on a duplicate.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_token_watches (
  id         UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chain      VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
  -- Chain-prefixed, like every other mint in the schema.
  token_mint VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  status     VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
  error      TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CONSTRAINT chk_token_watch_status
    CHECK (status IN ('pending','running','complete','failed')),
  CONSTRAINT uq_token_watch UNIQUE (user_id, chain, token_mint)
);

-- Serves the rolling-24h quota count directly.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_utw_user_created
  ON user_token_watches(user_id, created_at DESC);

==> packages/db/sql/046_polymarket_redemptions.sql <==
-- 046_polymarket_redemptions.sql
--
-- Redemption ledger for resolved Polymarket positions (checklist S3-18).
--
-- Why this table exists at all. A resolved Polymarket market stops accepting
-- orders, so a winning position cannot be *sold* — it must be redeemed, which
-- converts each winning outcome token into 1 pUSD and each losing token into 0.
-- Until this landed, `assertPolymarketMarketTradable` correctly refused to trade
-- a resolving market but nothing ever claimed the proceeds, so a winning
-- position stayed open in the ledger forever and its collateral was stranded.
--
-- Why a ledger rather than an idempotent re-read. `redeemPositions()` takes no
-- amount and redeems the wallet's whole balance for both outcomes, so a second
-- call after a successful first one is a no-op on-chain but still costs gas and
-- still produces a transaction hash the reconciler would treat as a new fill.
-- The unique constraint below is what makes the sweep safe to run on a timer.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS polymarket_redemptions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

  -- Tenancy key per ADR 0001. Nullable during Stage 3 because the executor
  -- still runs as the single 'operator' account; Stage 4 backfills and tightens.
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  condition_id TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- Claim/confirm lifecycle, mirroring how copy_executions separates a claimed
  -- intent from a confirmed on-chain fact. A crash between claim and confirm
  -- must not look like a completed redemption.
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claimed'
    CHECK (status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed', 'failed')),

  transaction_hash TEXT,

  -- Recorded so P&L can attribute the proceeds without re-deriving them from
  -- chain state. Units are pUSD, 6dp, stored as NUMERIC to avoid float drift.
  redeemed_collateral NUMERIC(38, 6),
  winning_token_id TEXT,

  failure_reason TEXT,

  claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

  -- A confirmed redemption must carry its evidence, and a claimed one must not
  -- pretend to. Without this, a failed confirm could leave a row that reads as
  -- settled with no hash to verify against.
  CONSTRAINT chk_polymarket_redemption_confirmed_evidence CHECK (
    status <> 'confirmed'
    OR (transaction_hash IS NOT NULL AND confirmed_at IS NOT NULL)
  )
);

-- The exactly-once guard. One live claim per (user, market): a second sweep
-- while the first is still claimed or already confirmed cannot insert.
-- Partial, so a 'failed' attempt does not permanently poison the market.
--
-- NULLS NOT DISTINCT is load-bearing, not decoration. `user_id` is NULL for the
-- whole of Stage 3 (single 'operator' account), and by default NULL never
-- conflicts with NULL — so without this the index is silently INERT and two
-- concurrent sweeps both claim the same market. Verified by probe: with plain
-- NULLS DISTINCT a second claim inserts happily; with this clause it raises a
-- unique violation, while a 'failed' row is still free to be retried.
--
-- Requires PostgreSQL 15+. CI and production both run 16.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uq_polymarket_redemption_live_claim;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_polymarket_redemption_live_claim
  ON polymarket_redemptions (user_id, condition_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT
  WHERE status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed');

-- Covers the sweep's own lookup: "which markets have I not yet redeemed?"
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_polymarket_redemptions_condition_status
  ON polymarket_redemptions (condition_id, status);

-- Stuck-claim recovery scan: claimed rows older than the confirm timeout.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_polymarket_redemptions_claimed_at
  ON polymarket_redemptions (claimed_at)
  WHERE status = 'claimed';

COMMENT ON TABLE polymarket_redemptions IS
  'Exactly-once ledger for redeeming resolved Polymarket positions into pUSD. '
  'A resolved market cannot be sold, so redemption is the only exit path.';

==> packages/db/sql/047_user_execution_grants.sql <==
-- 047_user_execution_grants.sql
-- Scoped delegated authority to trade on a user's behalf (checklist S4-7,
-- ADR-0003). Renamed from the earlier `user_trading_wallets` shape, which
-- assumed one custodial keypair per user per chain.
--
-- Why the rename matters: the three venues store three DIFFERENT kinds of thing.
--
--   Solana     -> the user's vault PDA address.  No secret exists to store.
--   EVM        -> a session key plus its argument-level scope policy. Secret,
--                 but bounded-loss by the on-chain policy.
--   Polymarket -> the user's signer key. Secret, and funds-loss if it leaks.
--
-- So `sealed_secret` cannot be NOT NULL: a Solana vault has nothing to seal, and
-- a NOT NULL here would force a placeholder — which is exactly how a keyless
-- design quietly acquires a key. `chk_ueg_secret_matches_kind` below makes the
-- absence structural instead.
--
-- `chain`, not `chain_kind` — unlike 041_user_auth_wallets.sql. An EVM *auth*
-- wallet is one signature valid across every EVM chain, so `chain_kind` is right
-- there. An execution *grant* is per-venue: a Polymarket signer key is useless on
-- Robinhood Chain, and polygon/robinhood-chain are both EVM, so keying on
-- `chain_kind` would let one user's two EVM grants collide on a single row.
--
-- ON DELETE RESTRICT, not CASCADE. Stage 1 and 2 used CASCADE because sessions
-- and subscriptions are preferences. A Polymarket row is the only pointer to
-- funds and a Solana row is the only pointer to a vault the user can still
-- withdraw from; a cascade destroys both from one `DELETE FROM users`.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_execution_grants (
  id              UUID         PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id         UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chain           VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
  grant_kind      VARCHAR(24)  NOT NULL,
  -- The account the trade settles from. The user's OWN address on Solana/EVM;
  -- their Polymarket Deposit Wallet on Polymarket. We no longer mint addresses.
  --
  -- NOT chain-prefixed, for the same reason as user_auth_wallets.address: the
  -- repo-wide `${chain}:${raw}` invariant governs *tracked* wallets and
  -- transactions, and `chain` already carries the discriminator here. Write EVM
  -- lowercased and Solana case-preserved, matching resolveChainAddress. Any join
  -- to copy_positions.target_account must prefix on the way.
  account_address VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  -- The versioned envelope from S4-3: `v1.<wrapperId>.<b64 fields...>`. TEXT, not
  -- VARCHAR(n), because the length depends on the wrapper — an env-wrapped data
  -- key is 32 bytes and a Vault/KMS ciphertext blob is a few hundred, so a width
  -- sized for the env wrapper would reject rows during the very migration that
  -- touches every user's key.
  --
  -- NULL for keyless kinds. See chk_ueg_secret_matches_kind.
  sealed_secret   TEXT,
  key_version     INTEGER,
  -- Argument-level allowlist (S4-P10). Required in practice for EVM session keys;
  -- the Solana equivalent lives on-chain in the vault program, not here.
  --
  -- Deliberately JSONB and not typed columns: the policy is a list of
  -- (target, selector, argument constraint) triples whose shape differs per venue,
  -- so a normalised table would need a migration per policy feature. It is
  -- validated in application code on write and never read as authority — the
  -- on-chain policy is the enforcement point. This column records what we asked
  -- for, not what protects the funds.
  scope_policy    JSONB,
  expires_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  status          VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

  CONSTRAINT chk_ueg_chain CHECK (chain IN ('solana','polygon','robinhood-chain')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_ueg_kind CHECK (grant_kind IN
    ('solana_vault','eip7702','session_key_4337','polymarket_signer')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_ueg_status CHECK (status IN ('active','retired','revoked','compromised')),

  -- A keyless grant must carry no secret; a keyed grant must carry one, versioned.
  --
  -- Enforced in SQL rather than in application code because this is the invariant
  -- that "the API can never decrypt" ultimately rests on. The API holds no wrapper
  -- key, so a keyed row is openable only inside trade-executor and a keyless row
  -- has nothing to open at all. If a code path could write a bare key into
  -- `sealed_secret`, or write a secret onto a row the API is allowed to read as
  -- keyless, that guarantee would be a convention rather than a fact.
  --
  -- Written against a SET of keyless kinds rather than by naming `solana_vault`
  -- twice. The invariant is "keyless kinds carry no secret", not "Solana is
  -- special": adding a second PDA-style venue later is then a one-line edit to the
  -- array instead of a DROP + ADD on a load-bearing constraint, which is the kind
  -- of change that gets deferred and then forgotten.
  --
  -- The `LIKE 'v%'` half is a cheap tripwire for the envelope format: it rejects
  -- any write that is not a versioned envelope, so a path that ever stores a raw
  -- or base64-only key fails at the database rather than at the next signing
  -- attempt. It cannot detect a plaintext key that happens to start with `v` — it
  -- is a guardrail, not a proof, and the envelope round-trip tests carry the real
  -- assertion.
  CONSTRAINT chk_ueg_secret_matches_kind CHECK (
    CASE WHEN grant_kind = ANY (ARRAY['solana_vault']) THEN
      sealed_secret IS NULL AND key_version IS NULL
    ELSE
      sealed_secret IS NOT NULL
      AND key_version IS NOT NULL
      AND sealed_secret LIKE 'v%'
    END
  ),

  -- A session key with no expiry is not a scoped grant.
  CONSTRAINT chk_ueg_session_expires CHECK (
    grant_kind NOT IN ('eip7702','session_key_4337') OR expires_at IS NOT NULL
  ),

  -- Global, mirroring uq_auth_wallet. Two users cannot share an execution
  -- account; if a restore bug produced one, two users' funds would settle to a
  -- single address with two ledger balances and no way to say whose is whose.
  CONSTRAINT uq_ueg_account UNIQUE (chain, account_address)
);

-- Exactly one active grant per (user, chain, kind).
--
-- Keyed on `chain`, NOT `chain_kind`: polygon and robinhood-chain are both EVM,
-- so keying on chain_kind would let one user's Polymarket grant collide with
-- their Robinhood Chain grant.
--
-- Partial rather than a plain UNIQUE so that rotation stays possible without
-- deleting the old row — deleting the row that holds the sealed secret for an
-- account that may still hold dust. Retired rows stay forever and stay openable.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_ueg_active_per_user_chain_kind
  ON user_execution_grants(user_id, chain, grant_kind)
  WHERE status = 'active';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ueg_user ON user_execution_grants(user_id);

-- S4-P9 sweeps for lapsing grants. Partial, because only session keys expire, so
-- the index stays proportional to the EVM grant count rather than the table.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ueg_expiring
  ON user_execution_grants(expires_at)
  WHERE status = 'active' AND expires_at IS NOT NULL;

==> packages/db/sql/048_user_balances.sql <==
-- 048_user_balances.sql
-- Cached per-user, per-chain, per-asset balances (checklist S4-8). Refreshed by a
-- poller and after each trade; read by the fan-out sizing path.
--
-- This table is a CACHE OF AN ON-CHAIN FACT, not a ledger. That single sentence
-- drives most of what follows, starting with ON DELETE CASCADE: deleting these
-- rows loses nothing, because the poller rebuilds them from the chain. Compare
-- 047, where RESTRICT is right because the row is the only pointer to funds.
--
-- PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chain, asset) with no surrogate id: the triple IS the
-- fact, matching the reasoning in 044_user_wallet_subscriptions.sql. Nothing
-- references a balance row, so there is nothing for an id to be referenced by.
--
-- Staleness is a hard gate in the reader, not a warning. Sizing a live trade off
-- a stale balance is how a user ends up with more exposure than they hold: the
-- previous trade's debit has not been observed yet, so the next trade sizes off
-- pre-trade funds. Fan-out makes it acute — N jobs for one user across chains can
-- all read the same pre-trade snapshot inside one poll interval.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_balances (
  user_id       UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chain         VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
  -- The asset identifier as the venue names it: a chain-prefixed mint/contract
  -- for a token, or the chain's native symbol. VARCHAR(128) rather than 100
  -- because a Polymarket CTF position id is longer than an address.
  asset         VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  -- Human-scale amount. NUMERIC, never a float: a float64 cannot hold 18-decimal
  -- base units without drift, and this number is multiplied into position sizes.
  amount        NUMERIC      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (amount >= 0),
  -- Stored alongside `amount` rather than looked up at read time. A SELL needs an
  -- exact base-unit quantity (S3-7), which means reconstructing the integer from
  -- `amount`, which needs `decimals`. Deriving it from token metadata on read
  -- would make the sizing path depend on a second network call that can fail.
  decimals      SMALLINT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (decimals BETWEEN 0 AND 36),
  -- Nullable, and carrying its own timestamp, because a price fetch can fail
  -- independently of a balance fetch. Encoding "we know the amount but not the
  -- price" as `usd = 0` would make a funded user look empty to the sizing path,
  -- which then sizes to zero — a silent failure that looks like a working system.
  -- NULL forces the reader to say "unknown" and refuse.
  usd           NUMERIC      CHECK (usd IS NULL OR usd >= 0),
  usd_priced_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  fetched_at    TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  -- Distinguishes a scheduled poll from a post-trade refresh. When a balance
  -- looks wrong the first question is always "when and why did we last write
  -- this", and reconstructing the why from timestamps alone is guesswork.
  source        VARCHAR(24)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'poller',

  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chain, asset),
  -- Same three-value union as every other chain column in the schema.
  CONSTRAINT chk_ub_chain CHECK (chain IN ('solana','polygon','robinhood-chain')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_ub_source CHECK (source IN ('poller','post-trade','manual-refresh')),
  -- A priced balance must say WHEN it was priced, otherwise the staleness gate
  -- cannot tell a fresh valuation from one carried over from an old poll. Stated
  -- one-directionally on purpose: the converse is allowed, so a poller may record
  -- "priced at T, price unavailable" as (usd NULL, usd_priced_at T) rather than
  -- having to discard the attempt.
  CONSTRAINT chk_ub_usd_priced_at CHECK (usd IS NULL OR usd_priced_at IS NOT NULL)
);

-- Serves both the poller's "what is oldest" scan and the sizing path's staleness
-- check. Not composite with user_id: the poller's question is global.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_balances_stale ON user_balances(fetched_at);

==> packages/db/sql/049_user_execution_settings.sql <==
-- 049_user_execution_settings.sql
-- Per-user risk and execution preferences (checklist S4-9), plus the per-chain
-- mode and slippage tolerance that S4-P4 depends on.
--
-- Two tables, not one. Per-chain mode and slippage live in a second table rather
-- than a JSONB column on the first because a JSONB `{"solana":"live"}` cannot
-- carry a CHECK on its values, cannot be joined to the certification gate, and
-- needs application-side parsing inside the fan-out enumeration query — which is
-- the hot path. The (user, chain) pair IS the fact, same argument as 044.
--
-- Defaults duplicate DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/constants.ts) as
-- literals because a migration cannot import TypeScript. The values must match,
-- and user-execution-settings.test.ts asserts this file's defaults against the
-- constant so drift fails CI instead of silently giving new users different risk
-- than the docs claim.
--
-- No row is created at signup. Absence means "all defaults, nothing opted in",
-- and the resolver returns defaults for a missing row. Creating a row at signup
-- would require Stage 1's signup path to know about Stage 4's schema.
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_execution_settings (
  user_id                  UUID         PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- FALSE, and per-chain `mode` defaults to 'off'. A user who creates an account
  -- and deposits does not begin trading; opting in is an explicit act, and the
  -- disclosure obligations attach to that act.
  auto_execute             BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  -- 80 matches the seeded signals.auto_execute_min_score in 001_init.sql.
  min_signal_score         SMALLINT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 80
                             CHECK (min_signal_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  -- DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.maxPositionPct
  max_position_pct         NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 5
                             CHECK (max_position_pct > 0 AND max_position_pct <= 100),
  -- DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.maxDailyExposurePct
  max_daily_exposure_pct   NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 25
                             CHECK (max_daily_exposure_pct > 0 AND max_daily_exposure_pct <= 100),
  -- DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.stopLossPct
  stop_loss_pct            NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 20
                             CHECK (stop_loss_pct > 0 AND stop_loss_pct <= 100),
  -- 3600s == the 60-minute REBUY_COOLDOWN_MINUTES default the operator path uses.
  rebuy_cooldown_seconds   INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 3600
                             CHECK (rebuy_cooldown_seconds >= 0),
  -- Lives here rather than in a constant because D11 requires a daily cap and a
  -- per-user cap must be adjustable by an admin without a deploy. 1000 is
  -- deliberately low; raising it is an audited admin action.
  max_daily_withdrawal_usd NUMERIC      NOT NULL DEFAULT 1000
                             CHECK (max_daily_withdrawal_usd >= 0),
  -- The per-user kill switch. On the settings row rather than derived from setting
  -- every chain to 'off', because those are different intents: "stop everything
  -- now" must be one atomic write that survives the user later re-enabling one
  -- chain, and it must be greppable in the audit log as one event.
  killed                   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at               TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at               TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

  -- Rejects a single-position cap larger than the daily cap. Without it one trade
  -- can exhaust and exceed the daily limit, which makes the daily limit
  -- decorative. The checklist lists both fields and does not say they must be
  -- ordered; they must.
  CONSTRAINT chk_ues_position_within_daily
    CHECK (max_position_pct <= max_daily_exposure_pct)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_chain_execution_settings (
  user_id          UUID        NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  chain            VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  -- 'off' by default. The platform gates (chain_certifications and
  -- LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS) still clamp on top of whatever this says — resolveChainMode
  -- downgrades to paper when either is missing, so 'live' here is a request, not
  -- a grant.
  mode             VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'off',
  -- Per-chain because tolerable slippage is a property of the venue, not the
  -- person: 3% is loose on a Polymarket CLOB book and tight on a thin Solana
  -- memecoin. One global value would force a user to accept the loosest chain's
  -- risk everywhere.
  --
  -- NULL means "use the chain default" and is deliberately distinct from a
  -- user-chosen value. That distinction is what lets DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS be
  -- retuned later for users who never expressed a preference, without silently
  -- overwriting anyone who did — resolveSlippageBps(chain, null) in
  -- packages/shared/src/slippage.ts accepts NULL for exactly this.
  --
  -- Bounds mirror that module: MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS = 1 (zero makes every order
  -- unfillable, which is a footgun rather than a policy) and MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS =
  -- 5000 (without a ceiling a user could set 90% and the executor would fill at a
  -- tenth of the quoted price — technically their stated limit, but not a risk
  -- anyone chooses knowingly). Hard prerequisite of S4-P4.
  max_slippage_bps INTEGER     NULL,
  updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chain),
  CONSTRAINT chk_uces_chain CHECK (chain IN ('solana','polygon','robinhood-chain')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_uces_mode CHECK (mode IN ('off','paper','live')),
  CONSTRAINT chk_uces_max_slippage_bps CHECK (
    max_slippage_bps IS NULL
    OR (max_slippage_bps >= 1 AND max_slippage_bps <= 5000)
  )
);


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- Per-user concurrent-position cap (S4-M4), added 2026-08-21
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--
-- Added by ALTER rather than as a column in the CREATE TABLE above, and that is
-- not a style choice. This file is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and migrate.ts
-- replays every file on every invocation with no applied-migrations table. On
-- any database where 049 has already run the table exists, so the CREATE is
-- skipped in full -- a column added inside its body would be created on fresh
-- databases only and would never appear on an existing one. The two would then
-- disagree, and the disagreement would surface as a 42703 in production while
-- CI (which builds from empty) stayed green.
--
-- Stating the column once, in an ALTER ... IF NOT EXISTS, makes fresh and
-- existing databases converge on the same shape. Same idiom as 043 and 050.
--
-- It lands in 049 rather than in a new file because the cap is a per-user
-- execution setting and this is the per-user execution settings table. The
-- ledger reserves 052-053 for S6-17 and S4-M6, so taking a number here would
-- either collide or push reserved work along for no gain.

ALTER TABLE user_execution_settings
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_concurrent_positions SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 5;

-- The CHECK is added separately, under an existence guard, for the same reason
-- the column is: an inline CHECK inside the CREATE TABLE body would only ever
-- exist on fresh databases. Guarded by name here rather than by conkey shape --
-- unlike the keys 050 rewrites, this name is chosen (not generated), is well
-- under the 63-byte truncation limit, and no other constraint on this table will
-- ever be given it, so the name IS the identity.
--
-- Bounds:
--   * Floor 1, not 0. A cap of 0 means "never open a position", which this row
--     already says twice and more legibly -- `killed`, and a per-chain `mode` of
--     'off'. A third spelling that reads to a skimming operator as "unlimited"
--     rather than "halted" is a footgun, and MIN_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS in
--     packages/db/src/position-cap.ts says the same 1.
--   * Ceiling 50 == PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS in that same module, whose
--     doc comment carries the derivation and is explicit that the shape of the
--     argument is sound and the exact number is a judgement. Restated as a
--     literal because a migration cannot import TypeScript; position-cap.test.ts
--     asserts the constant against this literal so the two cannot drift, the
--     same guard 049's risk defaults already use against DEFAULT_RISK_CONFIG.
--
-- Deliberately NOT cross-checked against max_position_pct. It is tempting to
-- reject max_concurrent_positions * max_position_pct > 100 the way
-- chk_ues_position_within_daily rejects an unordered pair, but that would be
-- wrong: a cap of 20 with 5% per position is a coherent, fully-invested
-- portfolio, and a cap higher than 100/max_position_pct is not incoherent
-- either -- it just means the per-position size binds before the cap does. That
-- interaction is what the derived warning explains at the slider; it is not a
-- representable-state violation, so it does not belong in a CHECK.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'user_execution_settings'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_ues_max_concurrent_positions'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE user_execution_settings
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_ues_max_concurrent_positions
      CHECK (max_concurrent_positions BETWEEN 1 AND 50);
  END IF;
END $$;

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_execution_settings.max_concurrent_positions IS
  'Per-user cap on simultaneously open copied positions (S4-M4). Clamped to the '
  'platform ceiling PLATFORM_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS = 50 by '
  'chk_ues_max_concurrent_positions. Stored and exposed by this release; '
  'ENFORCEMENT belongs to the fan-out eligibility predicate (S4-13), which does '
  'not exist yet, so nothing reads this column to refuse a trade today.';

==> packages/db/sql/050_copy_tenancy.sql <==
-- 050_copy_tenancy.sql
--
-- Tenancy key (`user_id`) on the three execution-ledger tables (checklist
-- S4-10): `trades`, `copy_executions`, `copy_positions`.
--
-- ── The bug this closes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `copy_positions` was keyed `PRIMARY KEY (target_account, chain, token_mint)`
-- (028_copy_execution_lifecycle.sql). In LIVE mode each user trades from a
-- distinct address, so that key separated users by accident. In PAPER mode
-- `resolvePaperCopyTargetAccount(chain)` returns ONE synthetic address per
-- chain with no user dimension, so every paper user on a chain shared a single
-- `copy_positions` row: user A's buy inflated user B's `confirmed_quantity`,
-- and B's exit computed P&L against A's cost basis. Paper is the default mode
-- for every free-tier user, so this was the common path, not an edge case.
--
-- The fix is the key, not the address. A shared synthetic paper target is
-- correct and honest once `user_id` is part of the uniqueness key: it reflects
-- that paper mode has no real counterparty. Minting a per-user fake address
-- would instead invent a counterparty that does not exist.
--
-- ── Expand-and-contract ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Legacy operator rows keep `user_id NULL` by design. Nothing is backfilled
-- destructively in this release and no column becomes NOT NULL. NULL means
-- "the single pre-multi-tenant operator account".
--
-- ── Idempotency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `migrate.ts` has NO applied-migrations tracking table: it replays EVERY file
-- in `packages/db/sql/` on EVERY invocation, in filename order, one
-- transaction per file. So a bare `DROP CONSTRAINT` / `ADD PRIMARY KEY` pair
-- would succeed once and then break `pnpm db:migrate` for every developer and
-- for CI on the second run.
--
-- Every statement below is therefore replay-safe. Three idioms, all already
-- established in this directory:
--   * `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` (043).
--   * `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS x; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS x ...` — 046
--     uses exactly this pair, because `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` alone will
--     NOT change the definition of an index that already exists, so widening
--     an existing index requires dropping it first.
--   * `DO $$ ... IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint ...) ... $$` (028, 030).
--
-- The constraint guards below match on `pg_constraint.conkey` shape rather
-- than on constraint NAME, for two reasons. First, PostgreSQL truncates
-- generated constraint names to 63 bytes, and
-- `copy_executions_source_trade_id_target_account_execution_mode_key` is 67 —
-- so its real name on disk is truncated and hardcoding it is a guess. Second,
-- the new primary key on `copy_positions` is *also* called
-- `copy_positions_pkey`, so a name-only `DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS
-- copy_positions_pkey` would drop the NEW key on replay and then fail, because
-- `copy_position_applications` now references it. Matching on column count
-- distinguishes the old 3-column key from the new 1-column one.
--
-- ── ON DELETE RESTRICT, not CASCADE ───────────────────────────────────────
--
-- 041/044/045 use CASCADE because auth wallets, subscriptions and watches are
-- *preferences*: deleting the user should delete them. These three tables are
-- not preferences, they are financial history:
--
--   * `trades` is the P&L and tax record. It has to outlive the account it
--     describes; a `DELETE FROM users` must not silently destroy it.
--   * `copy_executions` and `copy_positions` are the ledger that `trades` is
--     derived from, and the whole copy lifecycle already uses ON DELETE
--     RESTRICT internally (028, 030) so that evidence can never be orphaned.
--     CASCADE here would be inconsistent with that graph and would delete the
--     evidence chain behind a retained trade.
--
-- This follows 047_user_execution_grants.sql, which made the same call for the
-- same reason ("a cascade destroys both from one DELETE FROM users"). A user
-- with financial rows is soft-deleted; hard deletion is a separate,
-- deliberate operation that has to deal with these rows explicitly.


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 1. copy_positions: surrogate key + tenancy dimension
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- A surrogate key is needed because the natural key is about to gain a
-- NULLable column, and a NULLable column cannot participate in a primary key.
-- `pgcrypto` is enabled in 001_init.sql:1, so gen_random_uuid() is available.
--
-- The default is volatile, so PostgreSQL rewrites the table and evaluates it
-- per row: every pre-existing position gets its own id rather than all sharing
-- one. (The PG11+ "fast default" optimisation deliberately does not apply to
-- volatile defaults.)
ALTER TABLE copy_positions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid();

-- `copy_position_applications` carries a composite foreign key onto the exact
-- three columns of the primary key we are about to drop (028, lines 431-433).
-- PostgreSQL will refuse `DROP CONSTRAINT copy_positions_pkey` while that FK
-- depends on it ("cannot drop constraint ... because other objects depend on
-- it"), so it has to go first. Dropped explicitly by lookup rather than with
-- CASCADE, so this cannot take out an object we did not know about.
--
-- `cardinality(confkey) = 3` targets the OLD composite FK specifically and
-- never the new single-column one added at the end of this section, which is
-- what makes the replay idempotent instead of a drop/recreate churn.
DO $$
DECLARE
  legacy_fk RECORD;
BEGIN
  FOR legacy_fk IN
    SELECT conname
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_position_applications'::regclass
       AND contype = 'f'
       AND confrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass
       AND cardinality(confkey) = 3
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format(
      'ALTER TABLE copy_position_applications DROP CONSTRAINT %I',
      legacy_fk.conname
    );
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- Drop the old three-column primary key, and ONLY the old one. See the
-- name-vs-shape note in the header: the replacement key below reuses the name
-- `copy_positions_pkey`, so the guard has to be on column count.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'p'
       AND cardinality(conkey) = 3
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_positions DROP CONSTRAINT copy_positions_pkey;
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'p'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_positions
      ADD CONSTRAINT copy_positions_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id);
  END IF;
END $$;

ALTER TABLE copy_positions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;

-- The tenancy-aware replacement for the dropped natural key.
--
-- NULLS NOT DISTINCT is load-bearing, not decoration — the same reasoning as
-- 046_polymarket_redemptions.sql. Under the default NULLS DISTINCT, two rows
-- that agree on (target_account, chain, token_mint) but both have
-- `user_id NULL` would NOT collide. Since every legacy operator row has
-- `user_id NULL`, this migration would then *remove* the uniqueness that
-- exists today while appearing to add a dimension: `ensureCopyPosition` would
-- insert a fresh duplicate operator position on every single call, and the
-- position ledger would fragment silently.
--
-- Requires PostgreSQL 15+. CI and production both run 16.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uq_copy_positions_account_chain_token_user;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_copy_positions_account_chain_token_user
  ON copy_positions (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_positions_user
  ON copy_positions (user_id, chain, token_mint);

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_positions.user_id IS
  'Owning tenant. NULL means the pre-multi-tenant operator account. Part of '
  'the uniqueness key so that paper users sharing one synthetic target_account '
  'still hold independent quantities and cost bases (S4-10).';


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 2. copy_position_applications: follow copy_positions
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--
-- NOT in the S4-10 brief, but the fix does not work without it. This table is
-- what `rebuildCopyPosition` aggregates a position from
-- (packages/db/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.ts), and it filters
-- `WHERE application.target_account = $1 AND chain = $2 AND token_mint = $3`.
-- With a shared paper target and no user dimension here, BOTH users' evidence
-- rows land in EACH user's ledger — so splitting `copy_positions` alone would
-- produce two rows holding identical, doubled quantities. Threading the
-- tenancy key onto the applications rows is what makes the split real.
--
-- Mirroring the tenancy column here matches how this table already works: it
-- redundantly carries target_account/chain/token_mint rather than joining for
-- them.
ALTER TABLE copy_position_applications
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;

-- Restores the referential integrity that dropping the composite FK above
-- gave up. It points at the surrogate `copy_positions.id` rather than at the
-- new four-column unique index, deliberately:
--
--   * a composite FK onto (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) would
--     be MATCH SIMPLE, which treats a row with ANY null referencing column as
--     automatically satisfying the constraint — so every legacy `user_id NULL`
--     row (i.e. all of them today) would lose FK enforcement entirely; and
--   * whether PostgreSQL accepts a NULLS NOT DISTINCT index as a foreign-key
--     target at all is not something this migration should be betting on.
--
-- A single-column FK onto a plain primary key has neither problem.
--
-- Left NULLable for the expand phase: tightening it to NOT NULL now would
-- break any old executor process still writing application rows without it.
-- The contract phase does that once all writers are on this version.
ALTER TABLE copy_position_applications
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS position_id UUID;

-- Backfill: only fills NULLs, so replaying it is a no-op.
--
-- `position.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM application.user_id` makes the join key
-- exactly mirror `uq_copy_positions_account_chain_token_user`, which is what
-- keeps this correct on replay. Without it the join is
-- (target_account, chain, token_mint) only, which is unambiguous *today* —
-- every position still has user_id NULL — but stops being so the moment real
-- tenants exist: several positions would then match, and `UPDATE ... FROM`
-- picks one of them nondeterministically, silently attaching one tenant's
-- evidence row to another tenant's position. That is reachable rather than
-- theoretical, because the expand phase deliberately tolerates an old executor
-- still writing application rows without `position_id` (see the note above).
--
-- `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` treats NULL as a value, so a legacy application row
-- matches the legacy position and a tenant's row matches that tenant's
-- position. Since the unique index guarantees at most one position per
-- (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id) with NULLS NOT DISTINCT, there
-- can never be more than one match.
UPDATE copy_position_applications application
   SET position_id = position.id
  FROM copy_positions position
 WHERE application.position_id IS NULL
   AND position.target_account = application.target_account
   AND position.chain = application.chain
   AND position.token_mint = application.token_mint
   AND position.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM application.user_id;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_position_applications'::regclass
       AND conname = 'fk_copy_position_applications_position'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_position_applications
      ADD CONSTRAINT fk_copy_position_applications_position
      FOREIGN KEY (position_id)
      REFERENCES copy_positions (id)
      ON DELETE RESTRICT;
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Complements 028's `idx_copy_position_applications_position` (left in place),
-- which is the index the rebuild's `ordered_events` CTE scans. Without user_id
-- that index no longer covers the predicate.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_position_applications_position_user
  ON copy_position_applications (target_account, chain, token_mint, user_id)
  WHERE active;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 3. copy_executions: tenancy on the identity keys
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--
-- ADR-0001 already flagged a tenancy collision here. Verified against the
-- schema as it stands: `user_id` was NOT present, and three of the identity
-- keys collide between two paper users sharing a synthetic target_account.
ALTER TABLE copy_executions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;

-- 028 declared `UNIQUE (source_trade_id, target_account, execution_mode)` as a
-- table constraint. Two paper users copying the same source trade in the same
-- mode agree on all three columns, so the second user's execution could never
-- be inserted — one user's claim silently blocked everyone else's.
--
-- Matched on column set rather than name: the generated name is 67 bytes and
-- so is truncated on disk (see header).
DO $$
DECLARE
  legacy_unique RECORD;
BEGIN
  FOR legacy_unique IN
    SELECT con.conname
      FROM pg_constraint con
     WHERE con.conrelid = 'copy_executions'::regclass
       AND con.contype = 'u'
       -- `attname` is of type `name`, and there is no `name[] = text[]`
       -- operator, so the cast to text is required rather than cosmetic.
       AND (
         SELECT array_agg(att.attname::text ORDER BY att.attname::text)
           FROM unnest(con.conkey) AS conkey_entry(attnum)
           JOIN pg_attribute att
             ON att.attrelid = con.conrelid
            AND att.attnum = conkey_entry.attnum
       ) = ARRAY['execution_mode', 'source_trade_id', 'target_account']
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format(
      'ALTER TABLE copy_executions DROP CONSTRAINT %I',
      legacy_unique.conname
    );
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- NULLS NOT DISTINCT for the same reason as above: without it the legacy
-- operator rows (user_id NULL) stop colliding with each other, which would
-- turn this from "one execution per source trade per target per mode per
-- tenant" into no guard at all for the operator — the exact duplicate-copy
-- defect 023's `unq_trades_source_trade_mode` was added to prevent.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uq_copy_executions_source_target_mode_user;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_copy_executions_source_target_mode_user
  ON copy_executions (source_trade_id, target_account, execution_mode, user_id)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT
  WHERE source_trade_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Same collision on the signal-scoped key from 030.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS unq_copy_executions_signal_target_mode;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unq_copy_executions_signal_target_mode
  ON copy_executions (signal_id, target_account, execution_mode, user_id)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT
  WHERE signal_id IS NOT NULL AND source_trade_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Deliberately NOT widened:
--
--   * `UNIQUE (chain, target_account, client_order_id)` — a client order id is
--     a hash that now includes the acting user (see
--     `buildCopyExecutionClientOrderId`), so it is already per-tenant
--     distinct. Adding user_id would be redundant, and would additionally
--     stop the index from catching a genuine cross-tenant id collision.
--   * `unq_copy_executions_submission_identity` (chain, submission_type,
--     submission_id) — a venue- or chain-assigned identity is globally unique
--     by construction. Adding a tenancy column would WEAKEN it: two tenants
--     claiming the same on-chain submission is precisely the corruption this
--     index exists to reject.
--   * `unq_copy_executions_id_signal_source` — a composite FK target, not a
--     tenancy guard.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_executions_user
  ON copy_executions (user_id, requested_at DESC);

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_executions.user_id IS
  'Owning tenant. NULL means the pre-multi-tenant operator account (S4-10).';


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 4. trades: tenancy on the reporting/idempotency key
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ALTER TABLE trades
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;

-- 023 added `unq_trades_source_trade_mode (source_trade_id, execution_mode)`
-- to stop duplicate executor runs copying one source trade twice. With more
-- than one tenant that guard is too strong: the SECOND tenant's legitimate
-- paper copy of the same source trade is indistinguishable from a duplicate
-- run and is rejected. Widening by user_id keeps the anti-duplicate guarantee
-- per tenant while letting distinct tenants each hold their own copy.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS unq_trades_source_trade_mode;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unq_trades_source_trade_mode
  ON trades (source_trade_id, execution_mode, user_id)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT
  WHERE source_trade_id IS NOT NULL;

-- Deliberately NOT widened:
--
--   * `unq_trades_copy_execution (copy_execution_id)` — already 1:1 with a
--     `copy_executions` row, which is itself now tenant-scoped. The tenancy
--     comes through the reference; adding user_id would let two trades share
--     one execution.
--   * `idx_trades_live_venue_order_id (executor, venue_order_id)` — a venue
--     order id is globally unique per executor. Adding a tenancy column would
--     WEAKEN it, letting two tenants both claim one real venue order.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_trades_user
  ON trades (user_id, executed_at DESC);

COMMENT ON COLUMN trades.user_id IS
  'Owning tenant. NULL means the pre-multi-tenant operator account. '
  'ON DELETE RESTRICT: a trade is financial history and must outlive the '
  'account it belongs to (S4-10).';

==> packages/db/sql/051_subscription_states.sql <==
-- 051_subscription_states.sql
--
-- Subscription lifecycle states `active` / `winding_down` / `ended`
-- (checklist S4-M3, ADR-0005 §3.7).
--
-- ── What this encodes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Unsubscribe is an **exits-only wind-down**, not a liquidation and not an
-- abandonment. Auto-selling on unsubscribe is a market action the user never
-- asked for — taxable, fee-bearing, slippage-bearing, and at scale 500 users
-- leaving one master at once is a coordinated sell *we* caused. Simply
-- stopping is equally wrong: the exit for an already-open position was going
-- to arrive as the master's sell mirror, so dropping the link orphans it.
--
-- So the three states mean, precisely:
--
--   active        mirror the master's buys AND sells.
--   winding_down  mirror the master's sells ONLY. No new entries, ever.
--                 Positions opened while active keep their exit path.
--   ended         mirror nothing. Reached when the last position opened under
--                 this subscription has closed, or immediately on unsubscribe
--                 when there was nothing open to wind down.
--
-- `packages/db/src/subscriptions.ts` holds the matching state machine and is
-- the only place that decides which transitions are legal. This file's job is
-- to make an incoherent row unrepresentable, not to duplicate that logic.
--
-- ── Why now and not after fan-out ─────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Retrofitting means reconstructing which open position came from which
-- subscription, and that information is not recoverable once positions exist.
-- Today no fan-out has run, so every existing row is unambiguously `active`
-- and the default is exact rather than a guess. That is why the column is
-- landing while the table is still, in effect, empty of history.
--
-- ── Decision 1: a column here, not a separate lifecycle table ─────────────
--
-- The state is an attribute of the subscription, and 044 already settled that
-- there is exactly one subscription per (user, wallet): "the pair IS the fact;
-- there is no such thing as two distinct subscriptions by one user to one
-- wallet." Nothing in `packages/db/sql/` carries a foreign key onto this table
-- (grepped), so there is no dependency forcing a surrogate key either.
--
-- A separate `user_wallet_subscription_states` table would buy transition
-- *history*, which nothing in the checklist asks to read, at the cost of every
-- reader needing a lateral join to answer "is this subscription live?" — the
-- single question the fan-out path asks per master wallet per signal. Where
-- transition history is genuinely wanted it belongs in `audit_log` (043),
-- which already exists and already records per-actor events.
--
-- ── Decision 2: re-subscribe after `ended`, and why `active_since` exists ─
--
-- The primary key is still `(user_id, wallet_address)`, so a second row for
-- the same pair is impossible. A re-subscribe therefore CANNOT be a new row:
-- it is an `ended → active` transition on the row that is already there. That
-- is representable, which is what the state model needed to guarantee.
--
-- But it makes `created_at` unusable as the forward-only mirror boundary
-- (S4-M2: "mirrors only trades from subscription onward"). A row created in
-- January, ended in March and revived in August still reads
-- `created_at = January`, so a forward-only filter written against
-- `created_at` would let the revived subscriber catch up on eight months of
-- the master's trades — entering existing positions at an unknown cost basis,
-- which is precisely how followers become exit liquidity.
--
-- `active_since` is therefore set on EVERY entry into `active`, and it is the
-- column S4-M2 must filter on. Backfilled from `created_at` because for rows
-- that exist today the two are the same fact.
--
-- ── Decision 3: per-transition timestamps ────────────────────────────────
--
-- `wound_down_at` and `ended_at` are not decoration. A subscription that has
-- been winding down for sixty days is an operational alert — either the master
-- has gone quiet and never sold, or an exit is failing (S4-M17) — and that is
-- undetectable without knowing when the wind-down started. `ended_at` is what
-- makes "closed cleanly" distinguishable from "still waiting" in support
-- traffic and in the wind-down UI (S6-32).
--
-- They describe the CURRENT lifecycle instance, not history: entering `active`
-- clears them, which is what lets the coherence CHECK below be a real
-- invariant instead of advice. History is `audit_log`'s job, per Decision 1.
--
-- `close_all_requested_at` is the durable record of the explicit "close all
-- now" the item requires us to offer. It is a timestamp rather than a fourth
-- state because the subscription's mirroring posture does not change when the
-- user asks — it is already sells-only; only the *urgency* changes, from
-- "wait for the master's exit" to "exit now". Making it a state would force
-- every eligibility reader to learn a value that means the same thing as
-- `winding_down` for its purposes. It must be durable rather than an in-flight
-- command so that a request survives an executor restart and so that a second
-- click is a no-op instead of a second round of sells.
--
-- ── Idempotency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `migrate.ts` has NO applied-migrations table: it replays EVERY file in
-- `packages/db/sql/` on EVERY invocation, in filename order, one transaction
-- per file. Every statement below is replay-safe.
--
-- The two CHECK constraints are guarded by NAME rather than by
-- `pg_constraint.conkey` shape, which is the opposite of what 050 does. That
-- is deliberate and the reasoning does not carry over: 050 had to drop keys
-- whose generated names exceed the 63-byte identifier limit and whose
-- replacements reuse the old name. Here both names are explicit, 24 and 25
-- bytes, newly introduced by this file, and never reused by a replacement —
-- so the name IS the identity and a name guard cannot mis-fire. It is also
-- the idiom 050 itself uses for the constraint it ADDS
-- (`fk_copy_position_applications_position`).


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 1. Columns
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- VARCHAR + CHECK rather than a PostgreSQL ENUM, matching every other status
-- column in this schema (`wallets.status`, `user_token_watches.status`,
-- `user_wallet_subscriptions.source` in 044). An ENUM would need
-- `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`, which cannot run inside the transaction
-- `migrate.ts` wraps each file in.
--
-- DEFAULT 'active' is exact for the rows that exist today, not a fallback:
-- every one of them was written by `subscribeToWallet`, no fan-out has ever
-- run, so no row can be mid-wind-down. It also keeps any writer still running
-- the previous release correct — an insert without `state` means active, which
-- is what that writer intends.
ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active';

-- Added NULLable, backfilled, then made NOT NULL with a default. Adding it
-- NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() in one step would stamp every existing row with the
-- migration's own clock instead of its real subscription time. `SET NOT NULL`
-- and `SET DEFAULT` are both no-ops on replay.
ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS active_since TIMESTAMPTZ;

UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
   SET active_since = created_at
 WHERE active_since IS NULL;

ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ALTER COLUMN active_since SET DEFAULT NOW();

ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ALTER COLUMN active_since SET NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wound_down_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ended_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS close_all_requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 2. Constraints
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_subscription_state'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_subscription_state
      CHECK (state IN ('active', 'winding_down', 'ended'));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- The coherence invariant. Without it `state = 'winding_down'` with a NULL
-- `wound_down_at` is representable, and then "how long has this been winding
-- down?" — the one operational question the timestamp exists to answer — has
-- no answer for exactly the rows that need it.
--
-- Note the asymmetry, which is intentional: an `ended` row may have a NULL
-- `wound_down_at`, because `active → ended` is a legal direct transition for a
-- subscription that never opened a position. Requiring `wound_down_at` there
-- would force a fictitious wind-down through a state the subscription never
-- occupied.
--
-- `ELSE FALSE` fails closed. If a fourth state is ever added to
-- `chk_subscription_state` without being given a branch here, every write of
-- it is rejected loudly rather than silently escaping the invariant.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_subscription_state_stamps'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_subscription_state_stamps
      CHECK (
        CASE state
          WHEN 'active' THEN
            wound_down_at IS NULL
            AND ended_at IS NULL
            AND close_all_requested_at IS NULL
          WHEN 'winding_down' THEN
            wound_down_at IS NOT NULL
            AND ended_at IS NULL
          WHEN 'ended' THEN
            ended_at IS NOT NULL
          ELSE FALSE
        END
      );
  END IF;
END $$;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 3. Indexes
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- The fan-out hot path (S4-13): given a master wallet on a `source_trade`
-- signal, find its live subscribers and split them into buy-eligible
-- (`active`) and sell-only (`winding_down`). 044's `idx_uws_wallet` covers the
-- lookup but not the split, and `ended` rows are retained forever for
-- attribution, so without the partial predicate every mirror would scan the
-- accumulated history of everyone who ever left this master.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_uws_wallet_live
  ON user_wallet_subscriptions (wallet_address, state)
  WHERE state <> 'ended';

-- Wind-downs that are not finishing: the operational sweep behind S4-M17
-- (an unfilled sell leaves a user holding a position their master has left).
-- Partial, because this is a small set by construction and a full-table index
-- on a nullable timestamp would be mostly dead entries.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_uws_winding_down
  ON user_wallet_subscriptions (wound_down_at)
  WHERE state = 'winding_down';


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 4. Documentation
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.state IS
  'Mirroring lifecycle (S4-M3, ADR-0005 §3.7). active = mirror buys and '
  'sells; winding_down = mirror SELLS ONLY, no new entries; ended = mirror '
  'nothing. Legal transitions live in packages/db/src/subscriptions.ts '
  '(evaluateSubscriptionTransition) — do not UPDATE this column directly.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.active_since IS
  'When the CURRENT active period began; reset on every entry into active. '
  'This — not created_at — is the forward-only mirror boundary (S4-M2), '
  'because a revived subscription keeps its original created_at and filtering '
  'on that would let it catch up on trades from before it was revived.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.wound_down_at IS
  'When the current wind-down began. NULL for active rows, and also for rows '
  'that went active -> ended directly with nothing open to wind down.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.ended_at IS
  'When mirroring stopped entirely: the last position opened under this '
  'subscription closed, or unsubscribe found nothing open.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.close_all_requested_at IS
  'When the user asked to exit every open position now rather than waiting '
  'for the master to sell (S4-M3 "close all now"). Durable so the request '
  'survives an executor restart and so a second click is a no-op. Not a '
  'fourth state: the mirroring posture is already sells-only, only the '
  'urgency changes.';
