==> packages/db/sql/053_master_capacity.sql <==
-- 053_master_capacity.sql
--
-- Per-master capacity accounting, denominated in price impact
-- (checklist S4-M6, ADR-0005 §4.1-4.4).
--
-- ── What this encodes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Our own cohort is the adverse selection. One master's trade fans out to
-- hundreds of followers as a single directional order on the same pair within
-- minutes: user #900 buys at a price users #1-899 created. A master who notices
-- can farm it deliberately — buy small, wait for the copy flow to lift the
-- price, sell into their own followers.
--
-- The quantity that describes that harm is **aggregate copy notional as a
-- fraction of usable liquidity**, not follower count: 500 followers buying a
-- deep pair move it by basis points, 50 buying a fresh memecoin move it by tens
-- of percent. This file stores the numerator. The denominator (liquidity) is
-- NOT stored here, and the reason is the most important note in this file — see
-- "The liquidity gap" below.
--
-- `packages/db/src/master-capacity.ts` holds the decision, and it is the only
-- place that decides whether a cohort is admitted or skipped. This file's job is
-- to make the accounting honest and an incoherent row unrepresentable.
--
-- ── The liquidity gap, stated rather than papered over ────────────────────
--
-- A price-impact cap needs a usable-liquidity figure per (chain, token) at
-- fan-out time. What exists today, verified:
--
--   * `fetchDexScreenerLiquidity` (`packages/shared/src/prices.ts`) returns
--     DexScreener's `liquidity.usd` for the deepest pair, and is already called
--     at decision time by `apps/signal-engine/src/safety.ts`. It is a reported
--     both-sided pool TVL, not depth and not a quote, and it is not persisted
--     anywhere in this schema.
--   * Jupiter's quote carries a real per-trade `priceImpactPct`
--     (`packages/shared/src/jupiter.ts`, persisted to `trades.price_impact_pct`
--     by `007`) — Solana only, per order, obtained inside the executor at
--     simulation time, i.e. after fan-out was already decided.
--   * Polymarket's order book gives genuine depth and the executor already
--     walks it against a bps bound (`apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket.ts`) —
--     again at submission time. Polymarket outcome tokens trade on Polymarket's
--     own CLOB rather than on a DEX pair, so the DexScreener route is not
--     expected to cover them; that is a property of the venue and is NOT
--     verified anywhere in this repo, so treat it as reasoning to confirm
--     rather than a measured fact.
--
-- So there is an approximate figure for AMM pairs and NOTHING for Polymarket
-- before fan-out. Liquidity is therefore an injected input to the decision, with
-- its basis attached, and an unknown figure produces an explicit "unassessed"
-- result rather than a pass. **No liquidity column is added here on purpose:** a
-- column nothing populates reads as 0 or NULL, and either would turn this cap
-- into a control that blocks everything or permits everything while looking
-- like it works.
--
-- ── Decision 1: a cohort-level ledger, with no user id ───────────────────
--
-- `master_capacity_ledger` records ONE row per fan-out event per execution mode
-- — the whole cohort's notional, not one row per follower. Two reasons:
--
--   * Follower counts are never displayed (`S4-M9`), and a per-user ledger
--     would make a headcount trivially derivable from capacity data. There is
--     no `user_id` on this table and there must never be one.
--   * Capacity binds uniformly on every user (`S4-M7`): the decision is a
--     property of (master, token, window). A table that cannot see users cannot
--     be used to prioritise between them.
--
-- ── Decision 2: why not sum `copy_executions` ────────────────────────────
--
-- Because there is no USD notional there to sum. `028` stores
-- `requested_/confirmed_base_quantity` and `..._quote_quantity` in TOKEN units;
-- the quote token is USDC on Polymarket and on Solana stablecoin routes, but a
-- Uniswap V3 route on robinhood-chain may quote in WETH, so a quote quantity is
-- not a USD figure. `source_trades.amount_usd` is nullable and absent on two of
-- three chains by design (robinhood-chain never records one, Solana omits it off
-- USDC/USDT routes — see `S4-M23`). Summing either would produce a confident
-- wrong number, which for a cap is worse than an honest gap.
--
-- Hence `notional_usd NUMERIC NULL` plus `notional_basis`: an unpriced leg is
-- recorded as unpriced, the reader counts those legs, and the decision reports
-- its impact figure as a LOWER BOUND instead of a pass.
--
-- ── Decision 3: the window is not stored ─────────────────────────────────
--
-- Rows carry `committed_at` and the reader sums over an injected window, rather
-- than the writer bucketing into a fixed window. Bucketing would freeze one
-- window length into the data, and the two candidate windows have different
-- jobs: about 5 minutes is one fan-out's drain through a single concurrency-1
-- worker, about an hour is how long repeated buys still ride the same displaced
-- price. Both are judgements, neither is measured, and either can be changed
-- later without a backfill only if the raw timestamps are what is stored.
--
-- ── Decision 4: the per-master budget share ──────────────────────────────
--
-- `master_capacity_policy.daily_budget_share_bps` is the per-master allocation
-- inside the platform daily relayer budget that `S4-P15` depends on. Without it
-- one master doing 400 trades a day copied by 25 users consumes the whole budget
-- and blanks the venue for users copying OTHER masters — the uniform skip,
-- applied naively, would let one master's followers deny service to everyone
-- else's. NULL means "no explicit share": those masters split what is left
-- equally (`allocateMasterBudget`), because there is no defensible basis for
-- giving one master more of a shared quota and any basis we invented would be
-- the priority rule the uniform-skip decision exists to avoid.
--
-- ── Idempotency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `migrate.ts` has NO applied-migrations table: it replays EVERY file in
-- `packages/db/sql/` on EVERY invocation, in filename order, one transaction per
-- file. Every statement below is replay-safe.
--
-- Both tables are created with their key columns only, and every remaining
-- column is stated ONCE in an `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`. That
-- is deliberate and it is the fix for the trap found in `049`: a
-- `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` body is skipped entirely on any database where
-- the file has already run, so a column later added inside that body never
-- reaches those databases. Columns added to this file in future MUST be
-- nullable or defaulted, since `ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL` without a default
-- fails on a populated table.
--
-- Constraints are guarded by name in `pg_constraint`, as `051` does: every name
-- below is explicit, newly introduced by this file, well inside the 63-byte
-- identifier limit, and never reused by a replacement, so the name is the
-- identity and a name guard cannot mis-fire.


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 1. master_capacity_ledger — the numerator
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS master_capacity_ledger (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY
);

-- Chain-prefixed, per the repo-wide address invariant (`solana:ABC...`,
-- `polygon:0x...`). `chain` is stored alongside it for filter parity with
-- `source_trades` and `copy_executions`, and the two are held in agreement by
-- `chk_master_capacity_ledger_prefix` below.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS master_wallet_address VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS chain VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS token_mint VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL;

-- The fan-out event this cohort notional belongs to. RESTRICT rather than
-- CASCADE: deleting a source trade would silently free capacity that was really
-- consumed, and capacity accounting that can be rewritten by a delete is not
-- accounting.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_trade_id UUID NOT NULL
    REFERENCES source_trades(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;

-- Paper and shadow flow does not move a market, so a capacity check that mixed
-- modes would skip live users because of paper volume. The mode is recorded and
-- the reader filters on it.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS execution_mode VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL;

-- NULL means "this leg could not be priced" — never zero. See Decision 2.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS notional_usd NUMERIC;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS notional_basis VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS committed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_ledger'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_ledger_chain'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_ledger_chain
      CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain'));
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_ledger'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_ledger_mode'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_ledger_mode
      CHECK (execution_mode IN ('paper', 'live', 'shadow'));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- The address invariant, enforced rather than trusted. A bare `0x...` written
-- into a prefixed column is the defect class CLAUDE.md calls out, and here it
-- would silently split one master's capacity across two identities.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_ledger'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_ledger_prefix'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_ledger_prefix
      CHECK (master_wallet_address LIKE chain || ':%');
  END IF;
END $$;

-- The invariant that makes "silently zero" unrepresentable: an unpriced leg has
-- a NULL notional and a NULL notional is an unpriced leg. Without this, a writer
-- that could not price a leg could record 0 with a priced basis, and the cap
-- would read real flow as no flow.
--
-- `ELSE FALSE` is not needed because the equality covers every case, but the
-- basis list IS fail-closed: a basis not in the list is rejected loudly rather
-- than being admitted with unknown meaning.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_ledger'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_ledger
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis
      CHECK (
        notional_basis IN (
          'quote-stablecoin', 'source-amount-usd', 'marked-to-price', 'unpriced'
        )
        AND (notional_basis = 'unpriced') = (notional_usd IS NULL)
        AND (notional_usd IS NULL OR notional_usd >= 0)
      );
  END IF;
END $$;

-- One row per fan-out event per mode. This is what makes a retried fan-out
-- unable to double-count itself into its own cap, and it is why the writer can
-- be a plain `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unq_master_capacity_ledger_event
  ON master_capacity_ledger (source_trade_id, execution_mode);

-- The one read this table exists to serve: sum a (master, token) window.
-- `committed_at DESC` because every query is a recent window, never history.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_master_capacity_ledger_window
  ON master_capacity_ledger (master_wallet_address, chain, token_mint, committed_at DESC);


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 2. master_capacity_policy — per-master overrides and the budget share
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- Keyed on (master_wallet_address, chain) even though the prefix already carries
-- the chain, so the key shape matches every other per-chain table here and a
-- join needs no string surgery. The prefix CHECK keeps the two in agreement.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS master_capacity_policy (
  master_wallet_address VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  chain VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (master_wallet_address, chain)
);

-- NULL means "platform default", which is the common case: an override is an
-- operator action, not a setting every master carries. The platform defaults
-- live in `master-capacity.ts` and are DERIVED from `DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS`
-- (`S4-P4`), so they are deliberately not duplicated into `config` here — a
-- second copy would drift from the tolerance it is a fraction of.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS max_aggregate_impact_bps INTEGER;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS follower_soft_cap INTEGER;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS daily_budget_share_bps INTEGER;

-- Why an override exists at all, for whoever reads the row later.
ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS note TEXT;

ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_policy'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_policy_chain'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_policy_chain
      CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain'));
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_policy'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_policy_prefix'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_policy_prefix
      CHECK (master_wallet_address LIKE chain || ':%');
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Ranges, mirroring the guards in `master-capacity.ts` so a value written by
-- hand cannot be one the decision function would throw on. 10000 bps = 100%:
-- an impact cap of 100% is already absurd and anything above it is a typo, and
-- a budget share above 100% cannot be honoured by definition. A soft cap of 0
-- is excluded because "copy nobody" is already expressible, and more legibly,
-- by not being a selectable master at all.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'master_capacity_policy'::regclass
       AND conname = 'chk_master_capacity_policy_ranges'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE master_capacity_policy
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_master_capacity_policy_ranges
      CHECK (
        (max_aggregate_impact_bps IS NULL
          OR (max_aggregate_impact_bps > 0 AND max_aggregate_impact_bps <= 10000))
        AND (follower_soft_cap IS NULL OR follower_soft_cap >= 1)
        AND (daily_budget_share_bps IS NULL
          OR (daily_budget_share_bps >= 0 AND daily_budget_share_bps <= 10000))
      );
  END IF;
END $$;

-- The budget allocator reads every explicit share at once (`S4-P15`), so the
-- partial index is over exactly the rows it wants.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_master_capacity_policy_budget
  ON master_capacity_policy (chain, daily_budget_share_bps)
  WHERE daily_budget_share_bps IS NOT NULL;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 3. Documentation
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

COMMENT ON TABLE master_capacity_ledger IS
  'Cohort-level copy notional per fan-out event (S4-M6). ONE row per '
  '(source_trade_id, execution_mode) covering the WHOLE cohort — there is no '
  'user_id and there must never be one: follower counts are never displayed '
  '(S4-M9) and capacity binds uniformly on every user (S4-M7), so a table that '
  'cannot see users cannot be used to prioritise between them. Summed over an '
  'injected window by fetchMasterWindowNotional in '
  'packages/db/src/master-capacity.ts.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_ledger.notional_usd IS
  'Cohort USD notional for this fan-out event, or NULL when the legs could not '
  'be priced. NULL means unknown, NEVER zero: copy_executions stores token '
  'quantities and no USD figure, and source_trades.amount_usd is NULL on '
  'robinhood-chain and on non-stablecoin Solana routes. A window containing '
  'NULLs is reported as a LOWER BOUND rather than as a pass.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_ledger.notional_basis IS
  'How notional_usd was obtained: quote-stablecoin (quote token is USD-pegged), '
  'source-amount-usd (from source_trades.amount_usd), marked-to-price (quantity '
  'times a fetched price), or unpriced (notional_usd IS NULL, enforced by '
  'chk_master_capacity_ledger_basis).';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_ledger.execution_mode IS
  'Paper and shadow flow does not move a market. Recorded so the capacity read '
  'can filter to live flow instead of skipping live users over paper volume.';

COMMENT ON TABLE master_capacity_policy IS
  'Per-master capacity overrides and the per-master share of the daily relayer '
  'budget (S4-M6, consumed by S4-P15). An absent row means platform defaults, '
  'which are derived in packages/db/src/master-capacity.ts from '
  'DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS (S4-P4) rather than duplicated here.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_policy.daily_budget_share_bps IS
  'This master''s reserved share of the platform daily relayer/venue budget, in '
  'bps. NULL means no explicit share: those masters split the remainder equally '
  '(allocateMasterBudget). Exists so one master doing 400 trades a day cannot '
  'consume the whole budget and blank the venue for users copying OTHER '
  'masters — the uniform skip applied naively would let one master''s followers '
  'deny service to everyone else''s.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_policy.max_aggregate_impact_bps IS
  'Override for the aggregate cohort price-impact ceiling per (master, token, '
  'window). NULL uses PLATFORM_MAX_AGGREGATE_IMPACT_BPS, which is a fraction of '
  'the chain default slippage tolerance — the cohort must not spend the whole '
  'budget that protects the last copier from a bad fill.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN master_capacity_policy.follower_soft_cap IS
  'Override for the CRUDE secondary cap on followers per master per chain. '
  'Venue-blind by construction; the price-impact cap is the primary control. It '
  'exists because the primary cap cannot see the per-chain concurrency-1 trade '
  'worker: 500 tiny copies of a deep pair pass the impact test and still put '
  '500 orders behind one worker.';

==> packages/db/sql/054_copy_evidence_quote_units.sql <==
-- 054_copy_evidence_quote_units.sql
--
-- Give `copy_execution_evidence.quote_quantity` a unit (checklist S4-M35).
--
-- ── The bug ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `quote_quantity` was a mixed-unit column. Each executor path wrote whatever
-- its venue settled in, and nothing recorded which that was:
--
--   * Polymarket live wrote `spendAmountUsd`              -- USD
--   * paper simulation wrote `simAmountUsd`               -- USD
--   * Solana live wrote `nativeLamportsDelta / 1e9`       -- SOL
--   * robinhood-chain live wrote `result.amountEth`       -- ETH
--
-- `rebuildCopyPosition` then folded that column into `copy_positions.cost_basis_usd`
-- with `COALESCE(quote_quantity, base_quantity * price_usd, 0)` -- PREFERRING
-- `quote_quantity`, so on the two live paths the USD fallback never fired and a
-- column named `_usd` accumulated SOL and ETH.
--
-- ── What this migration does ──────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Decided 2026-08-23: record BOTH, not either/or.
--
--   1. `quote_quantity` becomes USD, always, for every row written from here on.
--      The conversion happens at write time through the one conversion rule in
--      `packages/db/src/quote-valuation.ts`, which `persistTrade` now shares.
--   2. `quote_native_quantity` + `quote_currency` + `quote_native_usd_price`
--      preserve what was actually settled and the rate used, because a USD
--      figure alone cannot be re-derived if the rate was wrong, cannot be
--      audited, and cannot answer "how much SOL did this position cost".
--
-- ── The historical rows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- The unit of an existing row is NOT recoverable from `chain` alone -- the
-- Solana paper path settles in USD while the Solana live path settles in SOL.
-- It IS recoverable from (`evidence_type`, `chain`), because that pair is what
-- identifies the executor path:
--
--   * `venue_fill`        -> Polymarket only             -> USD
--   * `paper_simulation`  -> `simAmountUsd`              -> USD
--   * `chain_receipt`     -> solana live                 -> SOL
--   * `chain_receipt`     -> robinhood-chain live        -> ETH
--   * `chain_receipt`     -> polygon                     -> USD (no writer exists;
--                            polygon settles in USDC, so if such a row is ever
--                            found its amount is USD)
--
-- (`balance_reconciliation` has no writer in the codebase, so no such row can
-- exist; any that somehow does is left with a NULL currency, i.e. unknown.)
--
-- So the backfill below moves each legacy amount into `quote_native_quantity`,
-- stamps its currency, and -- for the SOL and ETH rows only -- NULLs
-- `quote_quantity`, because that value never was USD and no historical rate is
-- available to convert it. NULL here means *unknown*, which is the honest
-- reading: `rebuildCopyPosition` then falls back to `base_quantity * price_usd`,
-- which is USD by construction, exactly as it should have done all along.
--
-- Nothing invents a price. A row whose USD value is unknown stays unknown.
--
-- `copy_positions.cost_basis_usd` rows written before this migration keep their
-- wrong value until the position's next fill: `rebuildCopyPosition` is a full
-- recompute over the whole evidence ledger, so the first rebuild after this
-- migration repairs the basis from the repaired evidence. No separate position
-- backfill is needed and none is attempted here.
--
-- ── Idempotency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- `migrate.ts` re-runs every file on every invocation. Every statement here is
-- `IF NOT EXISTS`/additive, the backfill is guarded on `quote_currency IS NULL`
-- so a replay is a no-op, and the CHECK constraints are guarded on
-- `pg_constraint.conkey` SHAPE rather than on a name (Postgres truncates
-- identifiers at 63 bytes, so a name guard can silently fail to match).

-- ── 1. Evidence: the native record ───────────────────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE copy_execution_evidence
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quote_native_quantity NUMERIC,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quote_currency VARCHAR(8),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quote_native_usd_price NUMERIC;

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_execution_evidence.quote_quantity IS
  'USD value of the quote leg. Always USD, never a native token amount (S4-M35). '
  'NULL means the USD value is unknown -- never zero standing in for unknown.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_execution_evidence.quote_native_quantity IS
  'Amount the venue actually settled, in quote_currency. The observed figure; '
  'quote_quantity is derived from it.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_execution_evidence.quote_currency IS
  'Unit of quote_native_quantity: USD, SOL or ETH. NULL only on a row with no '
  'quote leg at all, or a pre-S4-M35 row whose executor path is unidentifiable.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_execution_evidence.quote_native_usd_price IS
  'USD per unit of quote_currency used for the conversion, so quote_quantity is '
  're-derivable and auditable. 1 for USD.';

-- ── 2. Backfill the historical rows ──────────────────────────────────────
--
-- The payload-immutability trigger (028) raises on any UPDATE that changes
-- quote_quantity, so it comes off for the duration of the backfill and goes back
-- on below, re-created to cover the three new columns as well.

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_copy_evidence_payload_immutable ON copy_execution_evidence;

UPDATE copy_execution_evidence evidence
   SET quote_native_quantity = evidence.quote_quantity,
       quote_currency = resolved.currency,
       quote_native_usd_price = CASE WHEN resolved.currency = 'USD' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END,
       quote_quantity = CASE WHEN resolved.currency = 'USD' THEN evidence.quote_quantity ELSE NULL END
  FROM (
    SELECT
      inner_evidence.id,
      CASE
        WHEN inner_evidence.evidence_type IN ('venue_fill', 'paper_simulation') THEN 'USD'
        WHEN inner_evidence.evidence_type = 'chain_receipt' AND execution.chain = 'solana' THEN 'SOL'
        WHEN inner_evidence.evidence_type = 'chain_receipt' AND execution.chain = 'robinhood-chain' THEN 'ETH'
        WHEN inner_evidence.evidence_type = 'chain_receipt' AND execution.chain = 'polygon' THEN 'USD'
        ELSE NULL
      END AS currency
    FROM copy_execution_evidence inner_evidence
    JOIN copy_executions execution ON execution.id = inner_evidence.execution_id
  ) resolved
 WHERE resolved.id = evidence.id
   AND resolved.currency IS NOT NULL
   AND evidence.quote_currency IS NULL
   AND evidence.quote_quantity IS NOT NULL;

-- ── 3. Evidence: constraints and the widened immutable payload ───────────
--
-- Pairing rule: an amount without its unit is the bug this migration exists to
-- fix, so it is made unrepresentable. A unit without an amount is equally
-- incoherent. Both or neither.
DO $$
DECLARE
  pairing_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum ORDER BY attnum)
    INTO pairing_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
     AND attname IN ('quote_native_quantity', 'quote_currency');

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> pairing_shape
       AND conkey <@ pairing_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_execution_evidence
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_evidence_quote_unit_paired
      CHECK ((quote_native_quantity IS NULL) = (quote_currency IS NULL));
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
DECLARE
  currency_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO currency_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
     AND attname = 'quote_currency';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> currency_shape
       AND conkey <@ currency_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_execution_evidence
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_evidence_quote_currency
      CHECK (quote_currency IS NULL OR quote_currency IN ('USD', 'SOL', 'ETH'));
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
DECLARE
  native_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO native_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
     AND attname = 'quote_native_quantity';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> native_shape
       AND conkey <@ native_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_execution_evidence
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_evidence_quote_native_nonneg
      CHECK (quote_native_quantity IS NULL OR quote_native_quantity >= 0);
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
DECLARE
  rate_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO rate_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
     AND attname = 'quote_native_usd_price';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_execution_evidence'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> rate_shape
       AND conkey <@ rate_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_execution_evidence
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_evidence_quote_rate_nonneg
      CHECK (quote_native_usd_price IS NULL OR quote_native_usd_price >= 0);
  END IF;
END $$;

-- The immutable payload now includes the unit. Recording an amount and later
-- relabelling its currency would rewrite history exactly as silently as the
-- original bug did.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION reject_copy_evidence_payload_mutation()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.execution_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.execution_id
    OR NEW.evidence_type IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.evidence_type
    OR NEW.evidence_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.evidence_id
    OR NEW.base_quantity IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.base_quantity
    OR NEW.quote_quantity IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.quote_quantity
    OR NEW.quote_native_quantity IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.quote_native_quantity
    OR NEW.quote_currency IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.quote_currency
    OR NEW.quote_native_usd_price IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.quote_native_usd_price
    OR NEW.price_usd IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.price_usd
    OR NEW.completes_execution IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.completes_execution
    OR NEW.occurred_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.occurred_at
    OR NEW.observed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.observed_at
  THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'copy execution evidence payload is immutable';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_copy_evidence_payload_immutable
  BEFORE UPDATE ON copy_execution_evidence
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION reject_copy_evidence_payload_mutation();

-- ── 4. Executions: unknown must not read as zero ─────────────────────────
--
-- `COALESCE(SUM(quote_quantity), 0)` reported the same complete-looking number
-- whether every fill was valued, some were, or none were, because SUM skips
-- NULLs. Two changes make the three cases distinguishable:
--
--   * `confirmed_quote_quantity` becomes nullable, and is NULL when at least one
--     confirmed fill exists and none of them carries a USD value. Zero now means
--     zero.
--   * `quote_unassessed_fill_count` says how many confirmed fills the sum omits,
--     so a partial total can be read as the lower bound it is.

ALTER TABLE copy_executions
  ALTER COLUMN confirmed_quote_quantity DROP NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE copy_executions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quote_unassessed_fill_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

DO $$
DECLARE
  unassessed_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO unassessed_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_executions'::regclass
     AND attname = 'quote_unassessed_fill_count';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_executions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> unassessed_shape
       AND conkey <@ unassessed_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_executions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_executions_quote_unassessed_nonneg
      CHECK (quote_unassessed_fill_count >= 0);
  END IF;
END $$;

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_executions.confirmed_quote_quantity IS
  'USD sum over confirmed fills that have a known USD value. NULL means no '
  'confirmed fill has one -- distinct from 0, which means no fills or a genuine '
  'zero. Read together with quote_unassessed_fill_count.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_executions.quote_unassessed_fill_count IS
  'Confirmed fills omitted from confirmed_quote_quantity because their USD value '
  'is unknown. Non-zero means that sum is a lower bound, not a settled total.';

-- ── 5. Positions: the same honesty for cost basis ─────────────────────────

ALTER TABLE copy_positions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

DO $$
DECLARE
  basis_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO basis_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass
     AND attname = 'cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'copy_positions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> basis_shape
       AND conkey <@ basis_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_positions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_positions_unvalued_fill_nonneg
      CHECK (cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count >= 0);
  END IF;
END $$;

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_positions.cost_basis_usd IS
  'USD cost basis rebuilt from the evidence ledger. Only fills with a known USD '
  'value contribute; see cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count before treating this as '
  'the whole basis.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_positions.cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count IS
  'Applied buy fills that contributed nothing to cost_basis_usd because neither a '
  'USD quote value nor a USD price was recorded. Non-zero means the basis is a '
  'lower bound.';

-- Native cost basis is deliberately NOT summarised onto copy_positions: one
-- position can mix a USD paper fill with a SOL live fill, so a single native
-- total would itself be a mixed-unit column -- the exact defect this migration
-- removes. The per-fill native record on copy_execution_evidence is the
-- auditable answer to "how much SOL did this cost", and this index makes that
-- question cheap to ask.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_evidence_quote_currency
  ON copy_execution_evidence (execution_id, quote_currency)
  WHERE quote_currency IS NOT NULL;

==> packages/db/sql/055_polymarket_position_exits.sql <==
-- 055_polymarket_position_exits.sql
--
-- Single-shot exit claim per Polymarket outcome position (checklist S4-M19).
--
-- Why this table exists. Our copy has two independent ways to exit a Polymarket
-- position and they race: (1) the master closes their position, which mirrors as
-- a sell, and (2) the market resolves, which redeems. Neither alone is
-- sufficient — waiting only for the master's sell strands every hold-to-
-- resolution position, and waiting only for resolution exits late on every
-- position the master actually traded out of. So both are tracked and the
-- earlier one acts.
--
-- Why the existing claim cannot be reused. `polymarket_redemptions` (046) is
-- keyed `(user_id, condition_id)`, which is correct for the on-chain call —
-- `redeemPositions({conditionId})` takes no amount and redeems the wallet's
-- balances for BOTH outcomes of the condition. But a condition holds two outcome
-- positions, and the race needs one winner PER POSITION, not one per condition
-- and not one per trigger. A condition-keyed guard would let a mirrored sell of
-- YES suppress the redemption of NO on the same condition, which is exactly the
-- outcome-collapsing mistake S4-M20 forbids.
--
-- Why the two triggers can genuinely collide. A master selling moments before
-- resolution is the ordinary case, not the edge. Without a position-scoped
-- exactly-once guard both triggers fire and the position is exited twice.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS polymarket_position_exits (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

  -- Tenancy key per ADR 0001, and NULLable for the same reason as 046: the
  -- executor still runs as the single pre-multi-tenant operator account.
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  -- The canonical position key from `polymarketPositionKey`: the chain-prefixed
  -- ERC-1155 OUTCOME token, `polygon:<tokenId>`. Deliberately not the condition
  -- id -- a condition holds two outcomes, so a condition-keyed row would merge
  -- YES and NO into one position.
  position_key TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- Carried for reporting and for the redemption fan-out. Not part of any
  -- uniqueness key, so it can never become the identity by accident.
  condition_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  outcome_token_id TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- Which side of the race won. Recorded because "the position exited" and "the
  -- position exited because the master left" are different facts, and P&L
  -- attribution needs the second one.
  exit_trigger TEXT NOT NULL
    CHECK (exit_trigger IN ('mirrored-sell', 'redemption')),

  -- Claim/confirm lifecycle, mirroring 046. A crash between claim and confirm
  -- must not look like a completed exit.
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claimed'
    CHECK (status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed', 'failed')),

  -- Evidence of the exit: a settlement transaction hash for a redemption, or the
  -- copy execution id for a mirrored sell. One of the two, never neither, once
  -- confirmed.
  transaction_hash TEXT,
  copy_execution_id UUID,

  failure_reason TEXT,

  claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

  -- A confirmed exit must carry its evidence and a claimed one must not pretend
  -- to, for the same reason as 046: a row that reads as settled with nothing to
  -- verify against is worse than no row.
  CONSTRAINT chk_polymarket_position_exit_confirmed_evidence CHECK (
    status <> 'confirmed'
    OR (
      confirmed_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (transaction_hash IS NOT NULL OR copy_execution_id IS NOT NULL)
    )
  )
);

-- The exactly-once guard, and the whole point of the table. One live exit per
-- (user, position): whichever trigger inserts first wins, and the loser's insert
-- returns no row rather than raising, so the losing trigger is a no-op instead of
-- an error.
--
-- NULLS NOT DISTINCT is load-bearing, exactly as in 046 and 050. `user_id` is
-- NULL for every operator row, and by default NULL never conflicts with NULL --
-- so without this clause the index is silently INERT and both triggers claim the
-- same position. Partial, so a 'failed' attempt does not poison the position
-- forever: redemption has no deadline and must stay retryable.
--
-- Requires PostgreSQL 15+. CI and production both run 16.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uq_polymarket_position_exit_live_claim;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_polymarket_position_exit_live_claim
  ON polymarket_position_exits (user_id, position_key) NULLS NOT DISTINCT
  WHERE status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed');

-- The redemption fan-out reads every position of one condition at once.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_polymarket_position_exits_condition
  ON polymarket_position_exits (condition_id, status);

-- Stuck-claim recovery scan: claimed rows older than the confirm timeout.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_polymarket_position_exits_claimed_at
  ON polymarket_position_exits (claimed_at)
  WHERE status = 'claimed';

COMMENT ON TABLE polymarket_position_exits IS
  'Single-shot exit claim per Polymarket outcome position. Two exit triggers '
  'race -- the master closing their position (mirrored sell) and the market '
  'resolving (redemption) -- and this table guarantees one winner per position '
  'rather than one per trigger (S4-M19).';

COMMENT ON COLUMN polymarket_position_exits.position_key IS
  'polygon:<outcomeTokenId>. The outcome token, never the condition id: a '
  'condition holds two outcomes and keying on it would merge them (S4-M20).';

==> packages/db/sql/056_master_membership.sql <==
-- 056_master_membership.sql
--
-- Master **membership** cap: 50 members per master, enforced structurally
-- (checklist S4-M43), plus the rule that a copier who leaves does not get their
-- slot back (S4-M44).
--
-- ── What this encodes, and what it deliberately does not ──────────────────
--
-- 053 caps ONE SIGNAL's fan-out, denominated in price impact. This file caps
-- STANDING MEMBERSHIP: how many users may hold a live subscription to one
-- master at all. Both are needed. A master with 5000 members whose fan-out is
-- impact-capped serves 50 people per signal and misleads the other 4950 about
-- what they actually bought.
--
-- Both caps are 50, and the equality is the point rather than a coincidence.
-- One concurrency-1 worker per chain at ~6s/order drains roughly 50 orders per
-- 5-minute window, so 50 members is the largest cohort that can actually be
-- served inside one window. 500 would take ~50 minutes to clear and everyone
-- past roughly #50 would fill materially worse than the master they are paying
-- to copy. The matching TS constant is MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP in
-- packages/db/src/master-membership.ts, and a test asserts the two agree.
--
-- ── Decision 1: an ordinal with a partial unique index, not a COUNT ───────
--
-- The obvious enforcement is "SELECT COUNT(*) ... IF count < 50 THEN INSERT".
-- That is not a cap. migrate.ts and every service run at READ COMMITTED, so N
-- concurrent subscribes all read the state before any of them commits: every
-- one sees 49 < 50 and every one inserts, and the cap is exceeded by exactly
-- the number of racers. subscriptions.ts already carries the same finding for
-- the tracked-wallet quota ("A test firing five concurrent subscribes against a
-- 3-wallet tier granted all five"), and its fix — FOR UPDATE on the USER row —
-- does not help here: it serialises one user's writes, and this cap is about 50
-- DIFFERENT users joining one master at the same moment.
--
-- So membership is a finite set of numbered slots:
--
--   membership_slot SMALLINT      the ordinal a live member holds
--   CHECK 1 <= membership_slot <= 50
--   UNIQUE (wallet_address, membership_slot) WHERE membership_slot IS NOT NULL
--
-- Range plus uniqueness is a pigeonhole argument. There are 50 ordinals a
-- master can hand out and no two members may hold the same one, so a 51st
-- slot-holder is UNREPRESENTABLE. That holds against concurrent writers,
-- against a future service that never read this file, and against a hand-typed
-- INSERT in psql. No application code has to be trusted for the cap to be true.
--
-- claimMasterMembershipSlot additionally takes pg_advisory_xact_lock on the
-- master while it picks an ordinal. That is for LIVENESS, not correctness:
-- without it two racers pick the same lowest free ordinal and the index rejects
-- one of them with a unique violation instead of giving it a different slot or a
-- clean refusal. The constraint is the cap; the lock is the manners.
--
-- ── Decision 2: winding_down and ended hold NO slot ──────────────────────
--
-- A winding-down user is leaving, so they must not occupy a slot. But they
-- still hold open positions and still need the master's sells mirrored, so they
-- must still be ENUMERATED for exits. Conflating the two breaks one or the
-- other: count them and the cap under-serves; drop them from enumeration and
-- their positions strand with no exit path.
--
-- The two facts are kept apart by construction. Mirror eligibility is derived
-- from `state` alone (mirrorEligibilityForState, consumed by
-- fanout-eligibility.ts) and nothing on the fan-out path reads membership_slot.
-- Occupancy is derived from membership_slot alone. Neither can drift into the
-- other.
--
-- chk_uws_membership_slot_state is what makes "a leaver holds no slot" an
-- invariant rather than a convention: a non-active row with a non-null
-- membership_slot is rejected by the database, so an UPDATE that forgets to
-- release the ordinal fails loudly instead of quietly holding a slot hostage.
--
-- ── Decision 3: S4-M44 expressed as a constraint, not a code path ─────────
--
-- A dropped copier does not get their slot back. Any reservation mechanism is a
-- queue, and a queue holding a slot for an absent user makes the cap dishonest
-- — the master shows 50 members of whom some cannot trade — while creating an
-- incentive to churn a subscription to hold position.
--
-- The ELSE branch of chk_uws_membership_slot_state clears BOTH columns for a
-- non-active row, so leaving `active` provably releases the ordinal and cannot
-- carry a grandfathering exemption out of the state either. Re-subscribing is
-- therefore an ordinary allocation: a free ordinal, or a refusal.
--
-- ── Decision 4: an over-subscribed master GRANDFATHERS, it never evicts ───
--
-- Existing masters may already have more than 50 active members. Nothing here
-- deletes a row or forces a state transition. Evicting the excess would be far
-- worse than the problem: it does not close anyone's positions, so it strands
-- exactly the open positions whose exit path is the master's sell mirror, and it
-- does it silently to users who did nothing wrong.
--
-- So the backfill hands out ordinals 1..50 oldest-member-first, and flags every
-- remaining active member `membership_grandfathered`. A grandfathered member
-- holds NO ordinal: they keep mirroring (fan-out reads `state`), they neither
-- block a join nor free one, and the cap applies to new joins only. The set can
-- only shrink — the flag is cleared the moment they leave `active` and can
-- never be reacquired, because DEFAULT FALSE is the only way a new row gets a
-- value for it. An over-subscribed master therefore converges to 50 by
-- attrition rather than by eviction.
--
-- The flag also closes the hole that a one-directional CHECK would leave open.
-- Without it, "an active row may have a NULL slot" would have to be permitted
-- forever to accommodate the legacy rows, and then any future writer could
-- insert unlimited active members with NULL slots and the cap would silently
-- stop being a cap. With it, an active row may skip the slot only when it
-- carries an explicit flag that no INSERT can set.
--
-- ── Idempotency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- migrate.ts has NO applied-migrations table: it replays EVERY file in
-- packages/db/sql/ on EVERY invocation, in filename order, one transaction per
-- file. Every statement below is replay-safe.
--
-- The backfill deserves the specific argument, because a naive one is NOT
-- replay-safe. Re-deriving ordinals from a ROW_NUMBER() over current members
-- would, after any churn, try to give an already-taken ordinal to a
-- grandfathered row and abort the migration with a unique violation. Instead
-- the backfill only ever writes ordinals that are demonstrably FREE for that
-- master, and — the stronger argument — once the constraints below exist its
-- WHERE clause selects rows the CHECK has made unrepresentable, so on every
-- replay it matches nothing at all. It is a first-run-only statement enforced
-- by a constraint rather than by a flag.
--
-- Constraint adds are guarded on pg_constraint.conkey SHAPE rather than on
-- conname, following 054. A name guard is only safe when the name is explicit,
-- short and never reused; shape is safe unconditionally, and neither shape here
-- collides with 044's chk_subscription_source ({source}) or 051's
-- chk_subscription_state ({state}) / chk_subscription_state_stamps
-- ({state, wound_down_at, ended_at, close_all_requested_at}).


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 1. Columns
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- SMALLINT, not INTEGER: the domain is 1..50 and the cap exists precisely
-- because a larger cohort cannot be served.
--
-- NULLable, and NULL is meaningful in two distinct ways that the coherence
-- CHECK below tells apart: a non-active row holds no slot because it is not a
-- member, and a grandfathered active row holds no slot because migration time
-- found the master already over the cap.
ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS membership_slot SMALLINT;

-- The only way an active row may hold no ordinal. DEFAULT FALSE with no writer
-- that ever sets it TRUE except the backfill below, so the grandfathered set is
-- fixed at migration time and monotonically shrinking.
ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS membership_grandfathered BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 2. The uniqueness half of the cap
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- Created BEFORE the backfill on purpose: the backfill's writes are then
-- checked as they happen, so a bug in it aborts this migration instead of
-- committing two members onto one ordinal.
--
-- Partial on `membership_slot IS NOT NULL` because NULLs are the common case
-- (every ended row, forever, is retained for attribution) and because a
-- multi-column unique index would treat them as distinct anyway — the partial
-- predicate makes the intent explicit and keeps the index small.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unq_uws_membership_slot
  ON user_wallet_subscriptions (wallet_address, membership_slot)
  WHERE membership_slot IS NOT NULL;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 3. Backfill
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- Assigns ordinals to existing active members, oldest first.
--
-- Ordered by active_since then created_at then user_id: active_since is the
-- forward-only boundary 051 introduced and is the honest answer to "who has
-- been copying this master longest"; created_at breaks ties from a common
-- backfill clock; user_id makes the result deterministic so a replay cannot
-- reorder anyone.
--
-- Only ordinals that are currently FREE for that master are written, and each
-- free ordinal is consumed once. That is what makes the statement safe to
-- replay against a table that has since churned.
WITH unslotted AS (
  SELECT user_id,
         wallet_address,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY wallet_address
           ORDER BY active_since, created_at, user_id
         ) AS seq
    FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
   WHERE state = 'active'
     AND membership_slot IS NULL
     AND NOT membership_grandfathered
),
masters AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT wallet_address FROM unslotted
),
free_slots AS (
  SELECT masters.wallet_address,
         candidate.slot,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY masters.wallet_address
           ORDER BY candidate.slot
         ) AS seq
    FROM masters
    CROSS JOIN generate_series(1, 50) AS candidate(slot)
   WHERE NOT EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
             FROM user_wallet_subscriptions taken
            WHERE taken.wallet_address = masters.wallet_address
              AND taken.membership_slot = candidate.slot
         )
)
UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions AS target
   SET membership_slot = free_slots.slot
  FROM unslotted
  JOIN free_slots
    ON free_slots.wallet_address = unslotted.wallet_address
   AND free_slots.seq = unslotted.seq
 WHERE target.user_id = unslotted.user_id
   AND target.wallet_address = unslotted.wallet_address;

-- Whatever is left is a master that was already over the cap. Grandfathered,
-- never deleted and never transitioned: see Decision 4. After the constraints
-- below exist, this statement's WHERE clause describes a row the CHECK forbids,
-- so every replay matches nothing.
UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions
   SET membership_grandfathered = TRUE
 WHERE state = 'active'
   AND membership_slot IS NULL
   AND NOT membership_grandfathered;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 4. The range half of the cap
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- 50 is written as a literal rather than derived, because a CHECK cannot read a
-- configuration table. packages/db/src/master-membership.test.ts asserts this
-- literal equals MASTER_MEMBERSHIP_CAP, so drift between the two is a red suite
-- rather than a cap that binds at a different number than the code believes.
DO $$
DECLARE
  slot_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum)
    INTO slot_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
     AND attname = 'membership_slot';

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> slot_shape
       AND conkey <@ slot_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_uws_membership_slot_range
      CHECK (membership_slot IS NULL OR (membership_slot >= 1 AND membership_slot <= 50));
  END IF;
END $$;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 5. The coherence invariant
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

-- Reads: an ACTIVE row is a member, so it holds an ordinal unless it was
-- grandfathered; ANY OTHER row holds neither an ordinal nor an exemption.
--
-- The ELSE branch is doing three separate jobs and each one matters:
--
--   * a winding_down or ended row cannot occupy a slot, so an UPDATE that
--     forgets to release the ordinal fails loudly instead of holding a slot for
--     a user who has left;
--   * a grandfathering exemption cannot survive a departure, which is S4-M44
--     expressed as an invariant: a returning member must take a real ordinal or
--     be refused;
--   * a state this build has never seen falls into ELSE and therefore holds no
--     slot, which is the fail-closed direction.
--
-- membership_grandfathered is NOT NULL, so `NOT membership_grandfathered` has no
-- three-valued-logic hazard and the CHECK cannot be satisfied by a NULL.
DO $$
DECLARE
  coherence_shape smallint[];
BEGIN
  SELECT array_agg(attnum ORDER BY attnum)
    INTO coherence_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
     AND attname IN ('state', 'membership_slot', 'membership_grandfathered');

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'user_wallet_subscriptions'::regclass
       AND contype = 'c'
       AND conkey @> coherence_shape
       AND conkey <@ coherence_shape
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE user_wallet_subscriptions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_uws_membership_slot_state
      CHECK (
        CASE state
          WHEN 'active' THEN membership_slot IS NOT NULL OR membership_grandfathered
          ELSE membership_slot IS NULL AND NOT membership_grandfathered
        END
      );
  END IF;
END $$;


-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- 6. Documentation
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.membership_slot IS
  'Membership ordinal 1..50 held by an active member of this master (S4-M43). '
  'The cap is enforced by this range plus unq_uws_membership_slot, which '
  'together make a 51st slot-holder unrepresentable — a COUNT(*) check would '
  'be exceeded by exactly the number of concurrent racers. NULL for every '
  'non-active row, and for active rows grandfathered by migration 056. '
  'NEVER expose this to a user: an ordinal is a rank, and a rank discloses the '
  'follower count S4-M9 forbids showing.';

COMMENT ON COLUMN user_wallet_subscriptions.membership_grandfathered IS
  'TRUE only for active members that migration 056 found on a master already '
  'over the cap. They hold no ordinal, keep mirroring, and neither block nor '
  'free a join; the cap applies to new joins only. Set exclusively by 056 — '
  'DEFAULT FALSE and no writer sets it — and cleared on leaving active by '
  'chk_uws_membership_slot_state, so the set can only shrink and an '
  'over-subscribed master converges to the cap by attrition, never eviction.';

==> packages/db/sql/057_polymarket_manual_exit_trigger.sql <==
-- 057 — allow 'manual' as a Polymarket exit trigger (S4-M45).
--
-- `055` created `polymarket_position_exits` with a CHECK admitting only
-- 'mirrored-sell' and 'redemption', the two entrants `S4-M19` raced. `S4-M45`
-- adds a third: the user exiting their own position.
--
-- The third entrant joins the SAME race rather than getting its own path,
-- because a user tapping "exit" moments before the master sells is the ordinary
-- case, not the edge — and two paths would sell one position twice. That is why
-- this is a one-value widening of an existing CHECK rather than a new table.
--
-- Idempotent: the guard matches on the constraint's `conkey` SHAPE and its
-- current definition, not on its name. Postgres truncates identifiers at 63
-- bytes, so a name comparison is unreliable on generated names — the trap
-- `028` fell into and `054` documents.
DO $$
DECLARE
  trigger_shape smallint[];
  existing_name text;
  admits_manual boolean;
BEGIN
  IF to_regclass('polymarket_position_exits') IS NULL THEN
    RAISE NOTICE '057: polymarket_position_exits absent; 055 has not run yet';
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  SELECT ARRAY[attnum] INTO trigger_shape
    FROM pg_attribute
   WHERE attrelid = 'polymarket_position_exits'::regclass
     AND attname = 'exit_trigger'
     AND NOT attisdropped;
  IF trigger_shape IS NULL THEN
    RAISE NOTICE '057: exit_trigger column absent; nothing to widen';
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  -- Find the single-column CHECK on exit_trigger, whatever it is called, and ask
  -- whether it already admits 'manual'. Checking the definition rather than
  -- assuming makes the replay a no-op instead of a needless constraint churn.
  SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE '%manual%'
    INTO existing_name, admits_manual
    FROM pg_constraint
   WHERE conrelid = 'polymarket_position_exits'::regclass
     AND contype = 'c'
     AND conkey @> trigger_shape
     AND conkey <@ trigger_shape
   LIMIT 1;

  IF existing_name IS NOT NULL AND admits_manual THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  IF existing_name IS NOT NULL THEN
    EXECUTE format(
      'ALTER TABLE polymarket_position_exits DROP CONSTRAINT %I', existing_name
    );
  END IF;

  ALTER TABLE polymarket_position_exits
    ADD CONSTRAINT chk_polymarket_exit_trigger
    CHECK (exit_trigger IN ('mirrored-sell', 'redemption', 'manual'));
END $$;

==> packages/db/sql/058_copy_position_lots.sql <==
-- 058_copy_position_lots.sql
--
-- Master-attributed inventory for downstream exits (S4-M3 / ADR-0007).
-- A copy position is an aggregate tenant/token ledger; these rows preserve which
-- source master and signal supplied each open quantity. All statements are replay-safe
-- because db:migrate replays every SQL file on every invocation.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_position_master_lots (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  position_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_positions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  master_wallet_address VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  chain VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain')),
  token_mint VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  signal_id UUID REFERENCES signals(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  source_trade_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES source_trades(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  acquisition_execution_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_executions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  acquisition_evidence_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_execution_evidence(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  acquired_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (acquired_quantity > 0),
  reduced_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reduced_quantity >= 0),
  remaining_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (remaining_quantity >= 0),
  acquired_cost_basis_usd NUMERIC,
  remaining_cost_basis_usd NUMERIC,
  acquired_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CONSTRAINT chk_copy_position_lot_quantity_bounds
    CHECK (reduced_quantity <= acquired_quantity AND remaining_quantity <= acquired_quantity),
  CONSTRAINT chk_copy_position_lot_cost_bounds
    CHECK (
      acquired_cost_basis_usd IS NULL
      OR (acquired_cost_basis_usd >= 0 AND remaining_cost_basis_usd IS NOT NULL AND remaining_cost_basis_usd >= 0)
    )
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_copy_position_master_lots_evidence
  ON copy_position_master_lots (acquisition_evidence_id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_position_master_lots_open
  ON copy_position_master_lots (position_id, master_wallet_address, acquired_at, id)
  WHERE remaining_quantity > 0;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_position_master_lots_signal
  ON copy_position_master_lots (user_id, master_wallet_address, signal_id)
  WHERE remaining_quantity > 0;

-- Every reduction is durable and idempotent per sell evidence and source lot.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_position_master_lot_reductions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  lot_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_position_master_lots(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  sell_execution_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_executions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  sell_evidence_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_execution_evidence(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),
  proceeds_usd NUMERIC,
  reduced_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE (lot_id, sell_evidence_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_position_master_lot_reductions_evidence
  ON copy_position_master_lot_reductions (sell_evidence_id);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce_copy_position_lot_parent()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
  position_user_id UUID;
  position_chain VARCHAR(64);
  position_token_mint VARCHAR(128);
BEGIN
  SELECT user_id, chain, token_mint
    INTO position_user_id, position_chain, position_token_mint
    FROM copy_positions
   WHERE id = NEW.position_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'copy position lot references missing position %', NEW.position_id;
  END IF;
  IF position_user_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.user_id
     OR position_chain IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.chain
     OR position_token_mint IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.token_mint THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'copy position lot ownership does not match parent position %', NEW.position_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_copy_position_lot_parent ON copy_position_master_lots;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_copy_position_lot_parent
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF position_id, user_id, chain, token_mint
  ON copy_position_master_lots
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce_copy_position_lot_parent();

COMMENT ON TABLE copy_position_master_lots IS
  'Master/signal-attributed inventory lots under a tenant copy position. '
  'Open quantity is never borrowed across masters (ADR-0007, S4-M3).';

COMMENT ON COLUMN copy_position_master_lots.user_id IS
  'Tenant copied by this lot. NULL is the legacy operator account.';

-- 059_stop_loss_lot_identity.sql
-- Add the master-lot dimension to stop-loss claims. LP migrations use their
-- separate sql-lp/059 namespace and are never loaded by the core profile.

ALTER TABLE signal_stop_losses
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS position_key VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL DEFAULT '';

DO $$
DECLARE
  primary_key_name text;
BEGIN
  SELECT conname INTO primary_key_name
    FROM pg_constraint
   WHERE conrelid = 'signal_stop_losses'::regclass
     AND contype = 'p'
     AND cardinality(conkey) = 2;
  IF primary_key_name IS NOT NULL THEN
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE signal_stop_losses DROP CONSTRAINT %I', primary_key_name);
  END IF;
END $$;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
     WHERE conrelid = 'signal_stop_losses'::regclass
       AND contype = 'p'
       AND cardinality(conkey) = 3
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE signal_stop_losses
      ADD CONSTRAINT signal_stop_losses_pkey PRIMARY KEY (account, signal_id, position_key);
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_signal_stop_losses_position
  ON signal_stop_losses (account, position_key, triggered_at DESC);

-- 060_close_all_claims.sql
-- Durable exactly-once claims for explicit tenant close-all sells.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_position_close_all_claims (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  lot_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_position_master_lots(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  wallet_address VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  requested_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL CHECK (requested_quantity > 0),
  status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claimed'
    CHECK (status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed', 'released')),
  execution_id UUID REFERENCES copy_executions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  evidence_id UUID REFERENCES copy_execution_evidence(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  released_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  CHECK (
    (status = 'claimed' AND confirmed_at IS NULL AND released_at IS NULL)
    OR (status = 'confirmed' AND confirmed_at IS NOT NULL AND released_at IS NULL)
    OR (status = 'released' AND released_at IS NOT NULL AND confirmed_at IS NULL)
  ),
  UNIQUE (lot_id, status) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_close_all_claim_active_lot
  ON copy_position_close_all_claims (lot_id)
  WHERE status IN ('claimed', 'confirmed');

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_close_all_claims_pending
  ON copy_position_close_all_claims (status, claimed_at)
  WHERE status = 'claimed';

-- 061_copy_position_lot_exits.sql
-- User/risk initiated exits have evidence but no master source event.

ALTER TABLE copy_executions
  ALTER COLUMN source_trade_id DROP NOT NULL,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS exit_lot_id UUID REFERENCES copy_position_master_lots(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS exit_trigger TEXT CHECK (exit_trigger IN ('close-all', 'stop-loss', 'manual', 'redemption'));

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'copy_executions'::regclass AND conname = 'chk_copy_execution_origin') THEN
    ALTER TABLE copy_executions ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_execution_origin CHECK (
      (source_trade_id IS NOT NULL AND exit_lot_id IS NULL AND exit_trigger IS NULL)
      OR (source_trade_id IS NULL AND exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL AND exit_trigger IS NOT NULL AND direction = 'sell')
    );
  END IF;
END $$;

ALTER TABLE copy_executions DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_copy_executions_source_snapshot;
ALTER TABLE copy_executions ADD CONSTRAINT chk_copy_executions_source_snapshot CHECK (
  (exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL AND direction = 'sell'
    AND source_position_before_quantity IS NULL AND source_sell_fraction IS NULL)
  OR (exit_lot_id IS NULL AND (
    signal_id IS NULL
    OR (direction = 'buy' AND source_position_before_quantity IS NULL AND source_sell_fraction IS NULL)
    OR (direction = 'sell' AND source_position_before_quantity IS NOT NULL
      AND source_sell_fraction IS NOT NULL AND source_position_before_quantity > 0
      AND source_sell_fraction > 0 AND source_sell_fraction <= 1)
  ))
);

DROP INDEX IF EXISTS uq_copy_executions_source_target_mode_user;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_copy_executions_source_target_mode_user
  ON copy_executions (source_trade_id, target_account, execution_mode, user_id)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE source_trade_id IS NOT NULL;
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS unq_copy_executions_signal_target_mode;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX unq_copy_executions_signal_target_mode
  ON copy_executions (signal_id, target_account, execution_mode, user_id)
  NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE signal_id IS NOT NULL AND source_trade_id IS NOT NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_copy_execution_open_lot_exit
  ON copy_executions (exit_lot_id)
  WHERE exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL AND state NOT IN ('failed', 'cancelled', 'confirmed');

ALTER TABLE trades
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS exit_lot_id UUID REFERENCES copy_position_master_lots(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE trades DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS chk_trades_copy_execution_identity_complete;
ALTER TABLE trades ADD CONSTRAINT chk_trades_copy_execution_identity_complete CHECK (
  copy_execution_id IS NULL OR
  (signal_id IS NOT NULL AND source_trade_id IS NOT NULL AND exit_lot_id IS NULL) OR
  (signal_id IS NOT NULL AND source_trade_id IS NULL AND exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce_copy_lot_exit_identity()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM copy_position_master_lots lot
    JOIN copy_positions position ON position.id = lot.position_id
    WHERE lot.id = NEW.exit_lot_id
      AND lot.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.user_id
      AND lot.chain = NEW.chain AND lot.token_mint = NEW.token_mint
      AND lot.signal_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.signal_id
      AND position.target_account = NEW.target_account
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'lot exit identity does not match its owning position';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_copy_lot_exit_identity ON copy_executions;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_copy_lot_exit_identity BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF exit_lot_id, user_id, chain, token_mint, signal_id, target_account
  ON copy_executions FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce_copy_lot_exit_identity();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce_trade_lot_exit_identity()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.exit_lot_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM copy_executions execution
    WHERE execution.id = NEW.copy_execution_id AND execution.exit_lot_id = NEW.exit_lot_id
      AND execution.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.user_id
      AND execution.signal_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NEW.signal_id
      AND execution.chain = NEW.chain AND execution.token_mint = NEW.token_mint
      AND execution.execution_mode = NEW.execution_mode
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'trade lot exit identity does not match execution';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_trade_lot_exit_identity ON trades;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_trade_lot_exit_identity BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON trades
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce_trade_lot_exit_identity();

-- 063_crypto_billing.sql
--
-- Pure crypto-native billing ledger in USDC for Solana and Polygon (checklist Stage 5).
--
-- Replaces fiat/Stripe payment infrastructure to eliminate banking bottlenecks,
-- chargeback risk, and fiat de-platforming. Supports:
--   - Operator Tier: 35 USDC / 30 Days (Stackable)
--   - Ultra Tier: 150 USDC / 30 Days (Stackable)
--   - Lifetime Pass: 1999 USDC (Permanent access; tier_expires_at = NULL per 039)
--
-- Idempotent: CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS only. Replays cleanly on migrate.ts.

-- 1. Crypto payments ledger (audit trail and replay-attack guard)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crypto_payments (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chain VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon')),
  tx_hash VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  amount_usdc NUMERIC(16, 6) NOT NULL CHECK (amount_usdc > 0),
  tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('operator', 'ultra')),
  plan_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (plan_id IN ('operator_monthly', 'ultra_monthly', 'lifetime')),
  duration_days INT CHECK (duration_days IS NULL OR duration_days > 0),
  payer_address VARCHAR(128),
  treasury_address VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  memo VARCHAR(64),
  status VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'confirmed'
    CHECK (status IN ('confirmed', 'underpaid', 'refund_requested')),
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Crucial security constraint: a blockchain transaction hash on a given chain
-- can NEVER be credited more than once across the entire system.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_crypto_payments_chain_tx
  ON crypto_payments(chain, tx_hash);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_crypto_payments_user
  ON crypto_payments(user_id, confirmed_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_crypto_payments_memo
  ON crypto_payments(memo)
  WHERE memo IS NOT NULL;


-- 2. User payment intents (tracks reference memos for external / exchange deposits)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_payment_intents (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  reference_memo VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  plan_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL CHECK (plan_id IN ('operator_monthly', 'ultra_monthly', 'lifetime')),
  tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (tier IN ('operator', 'ultra')),
  expected_amount_usdc NUMERIC(16, 6) NOT NULL CHECK (expected_amount_usdc > 0),
  status VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'completed', 'expired')),
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_user_payment_intents_memo
  ON user_payment_intents(reference_memo);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_payment_intents_user
  ON user_payment_intents(user_id, status);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_payment_intents_expiry
  ON user_payment_intents(expires_at)
  WHERE status = 'pending';

==> packages/db/sql/064_row_level_security.sql <==
-- 064_row_level_security.sql
--
-- Row-Level Security (RLS) for tenant isolation across all user-scoped tables.
--
-- Defense-in-depth security model:
--   1. Functions:
--      - current_app_user_id(): Extracts 'app.current_user_id' setting as UUID (returns NULL if unset/invalid).
--      - is_rls_bypassed(): Checks 'app.bypass_rls' = 'on' OR 'app.current_user_id' = '*'.
--        Crucially, untrusted/app role 'swat_app' is forbidden from bypassing RLS under any condition.
--   2. Policies:
--      - 'tenant_isolation_policy' on all 17 user-scoped tables.
--      - Evaluates USING and WITH CHECK to guarantee no cross-tenant reads, updates, deletes, or inserts.
--   3. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY:
--      - Ensures table owners are bound by RLS policies.
--   4. Role 'swat_app':
--      - Least-privilege application role with NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS for production application pools.
--
-- Idempotent: Replays cleanly on migrate.ts.

-- 1. Helper Functions
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION current_app_user_id() RETURNS uuid STABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '')::uuid;
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_rls_bypassed() RETURNS boolean STABLE AS $$
BEGIN
  -- An unprivileged app role can NEVER bypass RLS even if it attempts to set session flags
  IF CURRENT_USER = 'swat_app' THEN
    RETURN false;
  END IF;

  RETURN (
    current_setting('app.bypass_rls', true) = 'on'
    OR current_setting('app.current_user_id', true) = '*'
    OR (
      current_setting('app.bypass_rls', true) IS DISTINCT FROM 'off'
      AND NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_user_id', true), '') IS NULL
    )
  );
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- 2. Create swat_app role if it doesn't already exist
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'swat_app') THEN
    CREATE ROLE swat_app WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'swat_app' NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS;
  END IF;
END $$;

GRANT swat_app TO swat WITH SET TRUE;
DO $$
BEGIN
  EXECUTE format('GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %I TO swat_app', current_database());
END $$;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO swat_app;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO swat_app;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO swat_app;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO swat_app;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO swat_app;

-- 3. Configure RLS Policies on all 17 User-Scoped Tables
DO $$
DECLARE
  tbl text;
  tables text[] := ARRAY[
    'user_sessions',
    'user_auth_wallets',
    'user_api_keys',
    'user_balances',
    'user_wallet_subscriptions',
    'user_token_watches',
    'user_execution_grants',
    'user_execution_settings',
    'user_chain_execution_settings',
    'user_payment_intents',
    'crypto_payments',
    'copy_positions',
    'copy_executions',
    'copy_position_master_lots',
    'copy_position_applications',
    'copy_position_close_all_claims'
  ];
BEGIN
  -- 3a. Table 'users' (identity column is 'id')
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'users') THEN
    EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY';
    EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE users FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY';
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies 
      WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'users' AND policyname = 'tenant_isolation_policy'
    ) THEN
      EXECUTE 'CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_policy ON users FOR ALL USING (is_rls_bypassed() OR id = current_app_user_id()) WITH CHECK (is_rls_bypassed() OR id = current_app_user_id())';
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- 3b. Tables where tenant discriminator column is 'user_id'
  FOREACH tbl IN ARRAY tables LOOP
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = tbl) THEN
      EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', tbl);
      EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', tbl);
      IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies 
        WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = tbl AND policyname = 'tenant_isolation_policy'
      ) THEN
        EXECUTE format(
          'CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation_policy ON %I FOR ALL USING (is_rls_bypassed() OR user_id = current_app_user_id()) WITH CHECK (is_rls_bypassed() OR user_id = current_app_user_id())',
          tbl
        );
      END IF;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- Row Level Security for Perps tables
DO $$
DECLARE
  tbl text;
  tables text[] := ARRAY[
    'polymarket_perps_accounts',
    'polymarket_perps_positions',
    'polymarket_perps_orders'
  ];
