  query: mocks.query
}));

import {
  claimCircuitBreakerProbe,
  CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError,
  readCircuitBreakerState,
  recordCircuitBreakerFailure,
  recordCircuitBreakerSuccess
} from './circuit-breaker.js';

describe('database circuit breaker', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 0, trippedAt: null } }]
        : []
    }));
  });

  it('reads the chain-specific persisted state without process-local caching', async () => {
    mocks.query
      .mockResolvedValueOnce([{
        value: { consecutiveFailures: 2, trippedAt: null }
      }])
      .mockResolvedValueOnce([{
        value: { consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: '2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z' }
      }]);

    await expect(readCircuitBreakerState('operator', 'polygon')).resolves.toEqual({
      consecutiveFailures: 2,
      trippedAt: null
    });
    await expect(readCircuitBreakerState('operator', 'polygon')).resolves.toEqual({
      consecutiveFailures: 3,
      trippedAt: '2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z'
    });
    expect(mocks.query).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(mocks.query).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.any(String), ['breaker:operator:polygon']);
  });

  it.each([
    null,
    [],
    { consecutiveFailures: -1, trippedAt: null },
    { consecutiveFailures: 1.5, trippedAt: null },
    { consecutiveFailures: 1, trippedAt: 'not-a-date' },
    { consecutiveFailures: 1, trippedAt: null, open: true }
  ])('fails closed when stored state is malformed: %j', async (value) => {
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([{ value }]);

    await expect(readCircuitBreakerState('operator', 'solana')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError
    );
  });

  it('fails closed when the migrated chain key is missing', async () => {
    mocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);

    await expect(readCircuitBreakerState('operator', 'robinhood-chain')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError
    );
  });

  it('increments under a row lock and trips at the exact threshold', async () => {
    const failedAt = new Date('2026-07-27T12:34:56.789Z');
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 2, trippedAt: null } }]
        : []
    }));

    await expect(
      recordCircuitBreakerFailure('operator', 'robinhood-chain', 3, failedAt)
    ).resolves.toEqual({
      consecutiveFailures: 3,
      trippedAt: failedAt.toISOString()
    });

    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.map(([sql]) => sql)).toEqual([
      'BEGIN',
      expect.stringContaining('FOR UPDATE'),
      expect.stringContaining('UPDATE config'),
      'COMMIT'
    ]);
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(
      3,
      expect.any(String),
      [
        'breaker:operator:robinhood-chain',
        JSON.stringify({ consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: failedAt.toISOString() })
      ]
    );
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('rolls back a failure when the migrated chain key is missing', async () => {
    mocks.clientQuery.mockResolvedValue({ rows: [] });

    await expect(recordCircuitBreakerFailure('operator', 'polygon', 3)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError
    );
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('ROLLBACK');
    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.some(([sql]) => String(sql).includes('UPDATE config')))
      .toBe(false);
  });

  it('preserves the original trip time after additional failures', async () => {
    const trippedAt = '2026-07-27T09:00:00.000Z';
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt } }]
        : []
    }));

    await expect(
      recordCircuitBreakerFailure('operator', 'solana', 3, new Date('2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z'))
    ).resolves.toEqual({ consecutiveFailures: 4, trippedAt });
  });

  it.each([0, 101, 1.5, Number.NaN])(
    'rejects invalid threshold %s before opening a transaction',
    async (threshold) => {
      await expect(recordCircuitBreakerFailure('operator', 'solana', threshold)).rejects.toThrow(
        /integer from 1 through 100/
      );
      expect(mocks.connect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    }
  );

  it('rolls back and leaves malformed persisted state closed', async () => {
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: '2', trippedAt: null } }]
        : []
    }));

    await expect(recordCircuitBreakerFailure('operator', 'polygon', 3)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError
    );
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('ROLLBACK');
    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.some(([sql]) => String(sql).includes('UPDATE config')))
      .toBe(false);
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('resets exactly one chain to the canonical success state', async () => {
    await expect(recordCircuitBreakerSuccess('operator', 'polygon')).resolves.toEqual({
      consecutiveFailures: 0,
      trippedAt: null
    });

    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.map(([sql]) => sql)).toEqual([
      'BEGIN',
      expect.stringContaining('FOR UPDATE'),
      expect.stringContaining('UPDATE config'),
      'COMMIT'
    ]);
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(
      3,
      expect.any(String),
      [
        'breaker:operator:polygon',
        JSON.stringify({ consecutiveFailures: 0, trippedAt: null })
      ]
    );
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('rolls back success without hiding malformed persisted state', async () => {
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: false } }]
        : []
    }));

    await expect(recordCircuitBreakerSuccess('operator', 'solana')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(
      CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError
    );
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('ROLLBACK');
    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.some(([sql]) => String(sql).includes('UPDATE config')))
      .toBe(false);
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('leases one half-open probe after the persisted cooldown', async () => {
    const now = new Date('2026-07-27T10:05:00.000Z');
    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: '2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z' } }]
        : []
    }));

    await expect(claimCircuitBreakerProbe('operator', 'solana', 300_000, now)).resolves.toBe(true);
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(3, expect.any(String), [
      'breaker:operator:solana',
      JSON.stringify({ consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: now.toISOString() })
    ]);
  });

  it('does not lease a closed or cooling-down breaker', async () => {
    mocks.clientQuery
      .mockImplementationOnce(async () => ({ rows: [] }))
      .mockImplementationOnce(async () => ({
        rows: [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 0, trippedAt: null } }]
      }))
      .mockImplementationOnce(async () => ({ rows: [] }));
    await expect(claimCircuitBreakerProbe(
      'operator',
      'polygon',
      300_000,
      new Date('2026-07-27T10:01:00.000Z')
    )).resolves.toBe(false);

    mocks.clientQuery.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => ({
      rows: sql.includes('SELECT value')
        ? [{ value: { consecutiveFailures: 3, trippedAt: '2026-07-27T10:00:00.000Z' } }]
        : []
    }));
    await expect(claimCircuitBreakerProbe(
      'operator',
      'polygon',
      300_000,
      new Date('2026-07-27T10:04:59.999Z')
    )).resolves.toBe(false);
    expect(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.some(([sql]) => String(sql).includes('UPDATE config')))
      .toBe(false);
  });

  it.each([0, -1, 1.5, Number.NaN])(
    'rejects an invalid probe cooldown before opening a transaction: %s',
    async (cooldownMs) => {
      await expect(claimCircuitBreakerProbe('operator', 'solana', cooldownMs)).rejects.toThrow(
        'positive safe integer'
      );
      expect(mocks.connect).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    }
  );

  it('seeds every chain idempotently without overwriting operator state', async () => {
    const sql = await readFile(
      resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../sql/032_circuit_breaker_state.sql'),
      'utf8'
    );

    expect(sql).toContain("'breaker:solana'");
    expect(sql).toContain("'breaker:polygon'");
    expect(sql).toContain("'breaker:robinhood-chain'");
    expect(sql).toContain('ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING');
    expect(sql).not.toMatch(/DO UPDATE/i);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/circuit-breaker.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import type { QueryResultRow } from 'pg';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { withTransaction } from './transaction.js';

export interface CircuitBreakerState {
  consecutiveFailures: number;
  trippedAt: string | null;
}

type CircuitBreakerRow = QueryResultRow & { value: unknown };

const chains = new Set<Chain>(['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain']);
const initialState: CircuitBreakerState = {
  consecutiveFailures: 0,
  trippedAt: null
};

export class CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError extends Error {
  constructor(account: string, chain: Chain) {
    super(`Circuit breaker state for ${account}:${chain} is malformed; refusing to continue`);
    this.name = 'CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError';
  }
}

function assertChain(chain: Chain): void {
  if (!chains.has(chain)) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported circuit breaker chain: ${chain}`);
  }
}

function breakerKey(account: string, chain: Chain): string {
  assertChain(chain);
  if (!account || typeof account !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Account must be a non-empty string for circuit breaker keys');
  }
  return `breaker:${account}:${chain}`;
}

function serializeState(state: CircuitBreakerState): string {
  return JSON.stringify(state);
}

function parseState(account: string, chain: Chain, value: unknown): CircuitBreakerState {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {
    throw new CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError(account, chain);
  }

  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const keys = Object.keys(record).sort();
  const hasExactShape = keys.length === 2
    && keys[0] === 'consecutiveFailures'
    && keys[1] === 'trippedAt';
  const failures = record.consecutiveFailures;
  const trippedAt = record.trippedAt;
  const hasValidFailures = Number.isSafeInteger(failures) && Number(failures) >= 0;
  const hasValidTripTime = trippedAt === null || (
    typeof trippedAt === 'string'
    && trippedAt.length > 0
    && Number.isFinite(Date.parse(trippedAt))
  );

  if (!hasExactShape || !hasValidFailures || !hasValidTripTime) {
    throw new CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError(account, chain);
  }

  return {
    consecutiveFailures: failures as number,
    trippedAt: trippedAt as string | null
  };
}

function validateThreshold(threshold: number): void {
  if (!Number.isInteger(threshold) || threshold < 1 || threshold > 100) {
    throw new Error('Circuit breaker threshold must be an integer from 1 through 100');
  }
}

function validateFailureTime(failedAt: Date): void {
  if (!(failedAt instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(failedAt.getTime())) {
    throw new Error('Circuit breaker failure time must be a valid date');
  }
}

function validateCooldown(cooldownMs: number): void {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cooldownMs) || cooldownMs <= 0) {
    throw new Error('Circuit breaker cooldown must be a positive safe integer');
  }
}

/** Reads directly from PostgreSQL on every call so state is shared across processes and restarts. */
export async function readCircuitBreakerState(account: string, chain: Chain): Promise<CircuitBreakerState> {
  const key = breakerKey(account, chain);
  const rows = await query<CircuitBreakerRow>(
    'SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = $1',
    [key]
  );

  if (rows.length === 0) throw new CircuitBreakerStateCorruptionError(account, chain);
  return parseState(account, chain, rows[0]?.value);
}

/** Atomically increments one chain and records the first threshold-crossing timestamp. */
export async function recordCircuitBreakerFailure(
  account: string,
  chain: Chain,
  threshold: number,
  failedAt = new Date()
): Promise<CircuitBreakerState> {
  const key = breakerKey(account, chain);
  validateThreshold(threshold);
  validateFailureTime(failedAt);

  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    const result = await client.query<CircuitBreakerRow>(
      'SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = $1 FOR UPDATE',
      [key]
    );
    const current = parseState(account, chain, result.rows[0]?.value);
    const consecutiveFailures = Math.min(
      current.consecutiveFailures + 1,
      Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
    );
    const next: CircuitBreakerState = {
      consecutiveFailures,
      trippedAt: current.trippedAt
        ?? (consecutiveFailures >= threshold ? failedAt.toISOString() : null)
    };

    await client.query(
      `UPDATE config
          SET value = $2::jsonb,
              updated_at = NOW()
        WHERE key = $1`,
      [key, serializeState(next)]
    );
    return next;
  });
}

/** Atomically clears one chain after validating and locking its persisted state. */
export async function recordCircuitBreakerSuccess(account: string, chain: Chain): Promise<CircuitBreakerState> {
  const key = breakerKey(account, chain);
  const reset = { ...initialState };
  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    const result = await client.query<CircuitBreakerRow>(
      'SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = $1 FOR UPDATE',
      [key]
    );
    parseState(account, chain, result.rows[0]?.value);
    await client.query(
      `UPDATE config
          SET value = $2::jsonb,
              updated_at = NOW()
        WHERE key = $1`,
      [key, serializeState(reset)]
    );
    return reset;
  });
}

/**
 * Claims one half-open recovery probe after the cooldown. Updating `trippedAt`
 * acts as a cross-process lease so concurrent workers continue delaying.
 */
export async function claimCircuitBreakerProbe(
  account: string,
  chain: Chain,
  cooldownMs: number,
  now = new Date()
): Promise<boolean> {
  const key = breakerKey(account, chain);
  validateCooldown(cooldownMs);
  validateFailureTime(now);
  return withTransaction(async (client) => {
    const result = await client.query<CircuitBreakerRow>(
      'SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = $1 FOR UPDATE',
      [key]
    );
    const current = parseState(account, chain, result.rows[0]?.value);
    // Returning commits the (read-only) transaction and releases the row lock,
    // which is what the explicit COMMIT on these paths did.
    if (current.trippedAt === null) return false;

    const elapsedMs = now.getTime() - Date.parse(current.trippedAt);
    if (!Number.isFinite(elapsedMs) || elapsedMs < cooldownMs) return false;

    const leased: CircuitBreakerState = {
      consecutiveFailures: current.consecutiveFailures,
      trippedAt: now.toISOString()
    };
    await client.query(
      `UPDATE config
          SET value = $2::jsonb,
              updated_at = NOW()
        WHERE key = $1`,
      [key, serializeState(leased)]
    );
    return true;
  });
}

==> packages/db/src/client-pools.test.ts <==
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

/**
 * The read/write pool seam. `client.ts` builds its pools at import time, so
 * each case resets the module registry and re-imports under different env.
 */

const constructed: Array<{ connectionString?: string }> = [];

vi.mock('pg', () => {
  class Pool {
    options: { connectionString?: string };
    constructor(options: { connectionString?: string }) {
      this.options = options;
      constructed.push(options);
    }
    on = vi.fn();
    query = vi.fn(async () => ({ rows: [{ pool: this.options.connectionString }] }));
    end = vi.fn(async () => undefined);
  }
  return { Pool, types: { setTypeParser: vi.fn() } };
});

const WRITE_URL = 'postgres://user:pw@primary/swat';
const READ_URL = 'postgres://user:pw@replica/swat';

async function loadClient(env: { read?: string }) {
  vi.resetModules();
  constructed.length = 0;
  process.env.DATABASE_URL = WRITE_URL;
  if (env.read === undefined) {
    delete process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL;
  } else {
    process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL = env.read;
  }
  return import('./client.js');
}

const originalRead = process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL;
const originalWrite = process.env.DATABASE_URL;

beforeEach(() => {
  process.env.NODE_ENV = 'test';
});

afterEach(() => {
  if (originalRead === undefined) delete process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL;
  else process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL = originalRead;
  if (originalWrite === undefined) delete process.env.DATABASE_URL;
  else process.env.DATABASE_URL = originalWrite;
});

describe('read and write pools', () => {
  // The common deployment. A second pool against the same database would double
  // the connection count for no benefit.
  it('shares one pool when no replica is configured', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({});

    expect(client.readPool).toBe(client.writePool);
    expect(constructed).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('keeps `pool` as an alias of the write pool', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({});

    expect(client.pool).toBe(client.writePool);
  });

  it('opens a separate pool for a distinct replica URL', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({ read: READ_URL });

    expect(client.readPool).not.toBe(client.writePool);
    expect(constructed.map((options) => options.connectionString)).toEqual([
      WRITE_URL,
      READ_URL
    ]);
  });

  // A replica URL that resolves to the primary is a config mistake, not a
  // reason to open a redundant pool.
  it('does not open a second pool when the replica URL equals the primary', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({ read: WRITE_URL });

    expect(client.readPool).toBe(client.writePool);
    expect(constructed).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  // This is the guarantee that makes the seam safe: 92 of the ~200 query()
  // calls in this package are writes, so query() must never drift to the
  // replica.
  it('sends query() to the write pool and readQuery() to the read pool', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({ read: READ_URL });

    await expect(client.query('SELECT 1')).resolves.toEqual([{ pool: WRITE_URL }]);
    await expect(client.readQuery('SELECT 1')).resolves.toEqual([{ pool: READ_URL }]);
  });

  it('closes both pools', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({ read: READ_URL });

    await client.closePool();

    expect(client.writePool.end).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(client.readPool.end).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('closes the shared pool exactly once', async () => {
    const client = await loadClient({});

    await client.closePool();
    await client.closePool();

    expect(client.writePool.end).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/client-runtime.test.ts <==
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  attachPoolErrorHandler,
  buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig,
  createPoolCloser,
  installDatabaseShutdownHandlers,
  type DatabaseShutdownProcess
} from './client-runtime.js';

function createFakeProcess() {
  const listeners = new Map<NodeJS.Signals, () => void>();
  const processRef: DatabaseShutdownProcess = {
    once: vi.fn((signal, listener) => {
      listeners.set(signal, listener);
      return processRef;
    }),
    removeListener: vi.fn((signal, listener) => {
      if (listeners.get(signal) === listener) listeners.delete(signal);
      return processRef;
    }),
    exit: vi.fn()
  };
  return { listeners, processRef };
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.useRealTimers();
});

describe('database runtime configuration', () => {
  it('applies bounded defaults for pool and timeout behavior', () => {
    const config = buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db', {});

    expect(config).toEqual({
      pool: {
        connectionString: 'postgresql://db',
        max: 10,
        connectionTimeoutMillis: 5_000,
        idleTimeoutMillis: 30_000,
        query_timeout: 60_000,
        statement_timeout: 60_000,
        idle_in_transaction_session_timeout: 60_000,
        allowExitOnIdle: true,
        keepAlive: true,
        keepAliveInitialDelayMillis: 10_000
      },
      shutdownTimeoutMs: 10_000
    });
  });

  it('accepts valid overrides and rejects invalid values', () => {
    const config = buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db', {
      DB_POOL_MAX: '20',
      DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS: '2500',
      DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS: '45000',
      DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS: '90000',
      DB_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS: '120000',
      DB_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS: '15000'
    });

    expect(config.pool).toMatchObject({
      max: 20,
      connectionTimeoutMillis: 2_500,
      idleTimeoutMillis: 45_000,
      query_timeout: 90_000,
      statement_timeout: 90_000,
      idle_in_transaction_session_timeout: 120_000
    });
    expect(config.shutdownTimeoutMs).toBe(15_000);
    expect(() => buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db', {
      DB_POOL_MAX: '0'
    })).toThrow(/DB_POOL_MAX/);
    expect(() => buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db', {
      DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS: 'not-a-number'
    })).toThrow(/DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS/);
  });

  it('adjusts session timeouts when connecting through PgBouncer', () => {
    const configViaEnv = buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db', {
      DB_PGBOUNCER: 'true'
    });
    expect(configViaEnv.pool.statement_timeout).toBeUndefined();
    expect(configViaEnv.pool.idle_in_transaction_session_timeout).toBeUndefined();

    const configViaPort = buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig('postgresql://db:6432/swat', {});
    expect(configViaPort.pool.statement_timeout).toBeUndefined();
    expect(configViaPort.pool.idle_in_transaction_session_timeout).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe('database pool lifecycle', () => {
  it('handles idle-client errors without throwing from the event source', () => {
    let listener: ((error: Error) => void) | undefined;
    const source = {
      on: vi.fn((_event: 'error', callback: (error: Error) => void) => {
        listener = callback;
      })
    };
    const logError = vi.fn();

    attachPoolErrorHandler(source, logError);
    const error = new Error('connection reset');
    expect(() => listener?.(error)).not.toThrow();
    expect(logError).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      '[db] unexpected error on an idle PostgreSQL client',
      error
    );
  });

  it('closes the pool once across concurrent callers', async () => {
    const end = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    const close = createPoolCloser({ end });
    const first = close();
    const second = close();

    expect(first).toBe(second);
    await Promise.all([first, second]);
    expect(end).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('closes once and exits cleanly on repeated shutdown signals', async () => {
    const close = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    const { listeners, processRef } = createFakeProcess();

    installDatabaseShutdownHandlers({
      close,
      timeoutMs: 5_000,
      processRef
    });
    listeners.get('SIGTERM')?.();
    listeners.get('SIGINT')?.();

    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(close).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(processRef.exit).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    });
    expect(processRef.exit).toHaveBeenCalledWith(0);
  });

  it('logs failed and timed-out shutdowns before exiting non-zero', async () => {
    const failed = createFakeProcess();
    const failure = new Error('close failed');
    const failureLog = vi.fn();

    installDatabaseShutdownHandlers({
      close: vi.fn(() => {
        throw failure;
      }),
      timeoutMs: 5_000,
      processRef: failed.processRef,
      logError: failureLog
    });
    failed.listeners.get('SIGINT')?.();

    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(failureLog).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        '[db] PostgreSQL pool shutdown failed (SIGINT)',
        failure
      );
    });

    const timeoutLog = vi.fn();

==> packages/db/src/client-runtime.ts <==
import type { PoolConfig } from 'pg';

const DEFAULT_POOL_MAX = 10;
const DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;
const DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
const DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
const DEFAULT_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
const DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

type Environment = Record<string, string | undefined>;

export type DatabaseRuntimeConfig = {
  pool: PoolConfig;
  shutdownTimeoutMs: number;
};

type PoolErrorSource = {
  on(event: 'error', listener: (error: Error) => void): unknown;
};

type ClosablePool = {
  end(): Promise<void>;
};

export type DatabaseShutdownProcess = {
  once(signal: NodeJS.Signals, listener: () => void): unknown;
  removeListener(signal: NodeJS.Signals, listener: () => void): unknown;
  exit(code: number): void;
};

type ShutdownOptions = {
  close: () => Promise<void>;
  timeoutMs: number;
  processRef?: DatabaseShutdownProcess;
  logError?: (message: string, error: unknown) => void;
};

function readBoundedInteger(
  env: Environment,
  name: string,
  fallback: number,
  min: number,
  max: number
): number {
  const raw = env[name];
  if (raw === undefined || raw.trim() === '') return fallback;

  const parsed = Number(raw);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(parsed) || parsed < min || parsed > max) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be an integer between ${min} and ${max}`);
  }
  return parsed;
}

export function buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig(
  databaseUrl: string,
  env: Environment = process.env
): DatabaseRuntimeConfig {
  const poolMax = readBoundedInteger(env, 'DB_POOL_MAX', DEFAULT_POOL_MAX, 1, 100);
  const connectionTimeoutMs = readBoundedInteger(
    env,
    'DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS',
    DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS,
    100,
    120_000
  );
  const idleTimeoutMs = readBoundedInteger(
    env,
    'DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS',
    DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS,
    1_000,
    600_000
  );
  const queryTimeoutMs = readBoundedInteger(
    env,
    'DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS',
    DEFAULT_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS,
    1_000,
    900_000
  );
  const idleTransactionTimeoutMs = readBoundedInteger(
    env,
    'DB_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS',
    DEFAULT_IDLE_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS,
    1_000,
    900_000
  );
  const shutdownTimeoutMs = readBoundedInteger(
    env,
    'DB_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS',
    DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS,
    1_000,
    60_000
  );

  const isPgBouncer = env.DB_PGBOUNCER === 'true' || databaseUrl.includes(':6432');

  return {
    pool: {
      connectionString: databaseUrl,
      max: poolMax,
      connectionTimeoutMillis: connectionTimeoutMs,
      idleTimeoutMillis: idleTimeoutMs,
      query_timeout: queryTimeoutMs,
      statement_timeout: isPgBouncer ? undefined : queryTimeoutMs,
      idle_in_transaction_session_timeout: isPgBouncer ? undefined : idleTransactionTimeoutMs,
      allowExitOnIdle: true,
      keepAlive: true,
      keepAliveInitialDelayMillis: 10_000
    },
    shutdownTimeoutMs
  };
}

export function attachPoolErrorHandler(
  source: PoolErrorSource,
  logError: (message: string, error: unknown) => void = console.error
): void {
  source.on('error', (error) => {
    logError('[db] unexpected error on an idle PostgreSQL client', error);
  });
}

export function createPoolCloser(pool: ClosablePool): () => Promise<void> {
  let closePromise: Promise<void> | null = null;

  return () => {
    closePromise ??= Promise.resolve().then(() => pool.end());
    return closePromise;
  };
}

export function installDatabaseShutdownHandlers({
  close,
  timeoutMs,
  processRef = process,
  logError = console.error
}: ShutdownOptions): () => void {
  let shuttingDown = false;

  const startShutdown = (signal: NodeJS.Signals) => {
    if (shuttingDown) return;
    shuttingDown = true;
    let finished = false;

    const finish = (code: number) => {
      if (finished) return;
      finished = true;
      clearTimeout(forceTimer);
      processRef.exit(code);
    };

    const forceTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      logError(
        `[db] PostgreSQL pool shutdown timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms (${signal})`,
        new Error('Database shutdown timeout')
      );
      finish(1);
    }, timeoutMs);
    forceTimer.unref?.();

    void Promise.resolve().then(close).then(
      () => finish(0),
      (error) => {
        logError(`[db] PostgreSQL pool shutdown failed (${signal})`, error);
        finish(1);
      }
    );
  };

  const onSigint = () => startShutdown('SIGINT');
  const onSigterm = () => startShutdown('SIGTERM');
  processRef.once('SIGINT', onSigint);
  processRef.once('SIGTERM', onSigterm);

  return () => {
    processRef.removeListener('SIGINT', onSigint);
    processRef.removeListener('SIGTERM', onSigterm);
  };
}

==> packages/db/src/client.ts <==
import { Pool, types, type QueryResultRow } from 'pg';
import {
  attachPoolErrorHandler,
  buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig,
  createPoolCloser,
  installDatabaseShutdownHandlers
} from './client-runtime.js';
import { configurePostgresNumericParsers } from './numeric.js';

const databaseUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL;

if (!databaseUrl) {
  throw new Error('DATABASE_URL is required');
}

configurePostgresNumericParsers(types);

export const databaseRuntimeConfig = buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig(databaseUrl);

/**
 * Writes, transactions, and any read that must observe them.
 *
 * `pool` is kept as an alias so the ~40 call sites that reach for it directly
 * (`pool.connect()` for transactions, `pool.query()` in tests) keep working.
 */
export const writePool = new Pool(databaseRuntimeConfig.pool);
export const pool = writePool;
attachPoolErrorHandler(writePool);

/**
 * Reads that tolerate replica lag.
 *
 * Points at `DATABASE_READ_URL` when set, otherwise at the same database as
 * `writePool` — in which case it *is* `writePool`, so no second connection pool
 * is opened for a deployment with no replica.
 *
 * The seam is deliberately opt-in via `readQuery()` rather than `query()`
 * silently switching pools: 92 of the ~200 `query()` call sites in this package
 * are INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Routing `query()` at large to a replica would send
 * every one of those to a read-only endpoint the day a replica is configured.
 * A caller has to state that a read is lag-tolerant.
 */
const readUrl = process.env.DATABASE_READ_URL;
export const readPool = readUrl && readUrl !== databaseUrl
  ? new Pool(buildDatabaseRuntimeConfig(readUrl).pool)
  : writePool;
if (readPool !== writePool) {
  attachPoolErrorHandler(readPool);
}

const closeWritePool = createPoolCloser(writePool);
const closeReadPool = readPool === writePool ? null : createPoolCloser(readPool);

export const closePool = async (): Promise<void> => {
  await Promise.all([closeWritePool(), closeReadPool?.()]);
};

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test') {
  installDatabaseShutdownHandlers({
    close: closePool,
    timeoutMs: databaseRuntimeConfig.shutdownTimeoutMs
  });
}

export async function query<T extends QueryResultRow = QueryResultRow>(text: string, values?: unknown[]): Promise<T[]> {
  const result = await writePool.query<T>(text, values);
  return result.rows;
}

/**
 * Run a read that tolerates replica lag. Identical to `query()` until
 * `DATABASE_READ_URL` is set.
 *
 * Do not use for a read that a write in the same logical operation depends on
 * (a read-modify-write, or a read that must see a row just inserted) — those
 * belong on `query()` or inside a transaction.
 */
export async function readQuery<T extends QueryResultRow = QueryResultRow>(
  text: string,
  values?: unknown[]
): Promise<T[]> {
  const result = await readPool.query<T>(text, values);
  return result.rows;
}

==> packages/db/src/close-all.ts <==
import { query } from './client.js';
import { withTransaction } from './transaction.js';
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';

export interface CloseAllLotJob {
  readonly claimId?: string;
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly walletAddress: string;
  readonly lotId: string;
  readonly signalId: string;
  readonly tokenMint: string;
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly sellTokenAmount: number;
  readonly jobId: string;
}

type CloseAllLotRow = {
  user_id: string;
  wallet_address: string;
  lot_id: string;
  signal_id: string;
  token_mint: string;
  chain: Chain;
  remaining_quantity: string;
};

/**
 * Enumerate exact-quantity close-all sells without changing lifecycle state.
 *
 * The lot is the unit of work and the deterministic job id. A repeated poll
 * therefore produces the same BullMQ identity until evidence reduces the lot;
 * only confirmed reductions may make a winding-down subscription eligible for
 * `endSubscription`.
 */
export async function listCloseAllLotJobs(): Promise<CloseAllLotJob[]> {
  const rows = await query<CloseAllLotRow>(
    `SELECT
       subscription.user_id,
       subscription.wallet_address,
       lot.id AS lot_id,
       lot.signal_id,
       lot.token_mint,
       lot.chain,
       lot.remaining_quantity::text
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions subscription
       JOIN copy_position_master_lots lot
         ON lot.user_id = subscription.user_id
        AND lot.master_wallet_address = subscription.wallet_address
        AND lot.remaining_quantity > 0
      WHERE subscription.state = 'winding_down'
        AND subscription.close_all_requested_at IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY subscription.user_id, subscription.wallet_address,
               lot.acquired_at, lot.id`
  );

  return rows.map((row) => {
    const quantity = Number(row.remaining_quantity);
    if (!Number.isFinite(quantity) || quantity <= 0) {
      throw new Error(`Close-all lot ${row.lot_id} has invalid remaining quantity`);
    }
    return {
      userId: row.user_id,
      walletAddress: row.wallet_address,
      lotId: row.lot_id,
      signalId: row.signal_id,
      tokenMint: row.token_mint,
      chain: row.chain,
      sellTokenAmount: quantity,
      jobId: `close-all-${row.user_id}-${row.lot_id}`
    };
  });
}

/**
 * End only subscriptions whose requested close-all has no open lot left.
 *
 * The predicate is evaluated in the UPDATE itself, so a concurrent confirmed
 * reduction wins the race with this sweep rather than being stranded by an
 * in-memory read. This is intentionally separate from enumeration: enqueueing
 * a sell is not evidence that the lot was reduced.
 */
export async function endCompletedCloseAllSubscriptions(): Promise<number> {
  const rows = await query<{ user_id: string }>(
    `UPDATE user_wallet_subscriptions subscription
        SET state = 'ended',
            ended_at = NOW(),
            membership_slot = NULL,
            membership_grandfathered = FALSE
      WHERE subscription.state = 'winding_down'
        AND subscription.close_all_requested_at IS NOT NULL
        AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
            FROM copy_position_master_lots lot
           WHERE lot.user_id = subscription.user_id
             AND lot.master_wallet_address = subscription.wallet_address
             AND lot.remaining_quantity > 0
        )
      RETURNING subscription.user_id`
  );
  return rows.length;
}

import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const clientQuery = vi.fn();
  const release = vi.fn();
  return {
    clientQuery,
    release,
    // `on`/`off`: a real PoolClient is an EventEmitter, and withTransaction
    // attaches an 'error' listener so a mid-transaction socket failure cannot
    // crash the process. transaction.test.ts covers that behaviour itself.
    connect: vi.fn(async () => ({ query: clientQuery, release, on: vi.fn(), off: vi.fn() })),

vi.mock('./client.js', () => ({
  pool: { connect: mocks.connect },
  query: mocks.query

import {
  generateBehavioralClusters,
  generateFundingClusters
} from './clustering-queries.js';
import { MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS } from './independence.js';

/** Collapse whitespace so an assertion is not hostage to SQL indentation. */
function flat(sql: string): string {
  return sql.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
}

describe('cluster membership regeneration', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    mocks.clientQuery.mockResolvedValue({ rows: [] });
  });

  it('reconciles funding memberships inside one repeatable-read transaction', async () => {
    await generateFundingClusters();

    const sqlCalls = mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.map(([sql]) => sql as string);
    expect(sqlCalls[0]).toBe('BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ');
    expect(sqlCalls[1]).toContain("INSERT INTO wallet_clusters");
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain('DELETE FROM cluster_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain("c.cluster_type = 'funding'");
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain('expected_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[3]).toContain('INSERT INTO cluster_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[4]).toContain("WHERE cluster_type = 'funding'");
    expect(sqlCalls[5]).toContain('DELETE FROM wallet_clusters');
    expect(sqlCalls[6]).toBe('COMMIT');
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('reconciles behavioral memberships without touching other cluster types', async () => {
    await generateBehavioralClusters();

    const sqlCalls = mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.map(([sql]) => sql as string);
    expect(sqlCalls[0]).toBe('BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ');
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain('DELETE FROM cluster_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain("c.cluster_type = 'behavioral'");
    expect(sqlCalls[2]).toContain('expected_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[3]).toContain('INSERT INTO cluster_memberships');
    expect(sqlCalls[4]).toContain("WHERE cluster_type = 'behavioral'");
    expect(sqlCalls[5]).toContain('DELETE FROM wallet_clusters');
    expect(sqlCalls[6]).toBe('COMMIT');
  });

  describe('funder degree bound (S4-M11)', () => {
    it('bounds funder degree from above, not only below', async () => {
      await generateFundingClusters();

      const clusterInsert = flat(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls[1]?.[0] as string);
      // The bug: a floor with no ceiling, so a CEX hot wallet that funded millions
      // of addresses became one Funding Group.
      expect(clusterInsert).not.toContain('COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b) >= 2');
      expect(clusterInsert).toContain(
        `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b) BETWEEN ${MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS} `
          + `AND ${MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE}`
      );
    });

    it('excludes blacklisted funders as hubs, on top of the degree band', async () => {
      await generateFundingClusters();

      const clusterInsert = flat(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls[1]?.[0] as string);
      expect(clusterInsert).toContain('JOIN wallets funder ON funder.address = wr.wallet_a');
      expect(clusterInsert).toContain("funder.status <> 'blacklisted'");
    });

    it('applies the identical eligibility rule to clusters and to memberships', async () => {
      await generateFundingClusters();

      // The two must not drift: a membership set computed from a looser rule than
      // the cluster set would delete every member of a cluster just created, and a
      // tighter one would leave hub clusters populated.
      const eligibility = /eligible_funders AS \((.*?)\) *,? *(?:expected_memberships|INSERT)/;
      const fromInsert = eligibility.exec(
        flat(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls[1]?.[0] as string)
      );
      const fromDelete = eligibility.exec(
        flat(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls[2]?.[0] as string)
      );
      const fromMemberInsert = eligibility.exec(
        flat(mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls[3]?.[0] as string)
      );

      // Guard the regex itself: a capture that matched nothing useful would make
      // the equality below vacuously true.
      expect(fromInsert?.[1]).toContain(
        `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b) BETWEEN ${MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS} `
          + `AND ${MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE}`
      );
      expect(fromInsert?.[1]).toContain("funder.status <> 'blacklisted'");
      expect(fromDelete?.[1]).toBe(fromInsert?.[1]);
      expect(fromMemberInsert?.[1]).toBe(fromInsert?.[1]);
    });

    it('still tears down a cluster whose funder crossed the ceiling', async () => {
      await generateFundingClusters();

      const sqlCalls = mocks.clientQuery.mock.calls.map(([sql]) => sql as string);
      // Demotion needs no new statement: the funder drops out of
      // expected_memberships, the DELETE empties the cluster, the recount zeroes
      // wallet_count, and the final DELETE drops the row. Order is what makes that
      // work, so it is asserted.
      expect(flat(sqlCalls[2] ?? '')).toContain('DELETE FROM cluster_memberships');
      expect(flat(sqlCalls[4] ?? '')).toContain('wallet_count =');
      expect(flat(sqlCalls[5] ?? '')).toContain(
        "DELETE FROM wallet_clusters WHERE cluster_type = 'funding' AND wallet_count < 2"
      );
    });
  });

  it('rolls back and releases the client when reconciliation fails', async () => {
    mocks.clientQuery
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ rows: [] })
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ rows: [] })
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('cluster write failed'))
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ rows: [] });

    await expect(generateFundingClusters()).rejects.toThrow('cluster write failed');
    expect(mocks.clientQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('ROLLBACK');
    expect(mocks.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/clustering-queries.ts <==
import { query } from './client.js';
import { withTransaction } from './transaction.js';
import { MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE, MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS } from './independence.js';

/**
 * Funding-cluster eligibility, as one SQL fragment.
 *
 * Single-sourced deliberately. The rule is evaluated twice per run -- once to
 * create/refresh the cluster rows, once to compute the expected membership set
 * -- and the two diverging would delete every member of a cluster it had just
 * created. Both call sites interpolate this same string, so they cannot drift.
 *
 * Two halves, mirroring assessFunderIndependence in ./independence.ts:
 *
 *  1. A DEGREE BAND, not just a floor. The previous rule was
 *     HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b) >= 2 with no ceiling, so an exchange
 *     hot wallet that funded millions of addresses became a single Funding
 *     Group holding a large slice of the chain -- a cluster whose members
 *     co-move with everything trending, which is no evidence at all. See
 *     MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE for how the ceiling was chosen.
 *
 *  2. A HUB EXCLUSION. The band is necessary but not sufficient: the count is
 *     degree as observed in OUR index, so an exchange four of whose recipients
 *     we happen to track has an observed degree of 4 and clears any ceiling.
 *     wallets.status = 'blacklisted' is the one operator-controlled role
 *     channel the schema carries today (there is no wallets.role and no
 *     wallet_labels table), so this half is exactly as complete as that column
 *     -- inert until an operator populates it.
 *
 * A funder that was eligible and has since crossed the ceiling needs no extra
 * cleanup: it drops out of expected_memberships, the DELETE below strips its
 * members, wallet_count falls to 0, and the final DELETE drops the cluster.
 */
const eligibleFundersCte = `
    eligible_funders AS (
      SELECT wr.wallet_a
      FROM wallet_relationships wr
      JOIN wallets funder ON funder.address = wr.wallet_a
      WHERE wr.relationship_type = 'funding'
        AND funder.status <> 'blacklisted'
      GROUP BY wr.wallet_a
      HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b)
             BETWEEN ${MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS} AND ${MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE}
    )`;

export async function generateFundingClusters() {
  const expectedMembershipsCte = `
    WITH ${eligibleFundersCte},
    expected_memberships AS (
      SELECT DISTINCT c.id AS cluster_id, edge.wallet_address
      FROM eligible_funders ef
      JOIN wallet_relationships wr
        ON wr.wallet_a = ef.wallet_a
       AND wr.relationship_type = 'funding'
      JOIN wallet_clusters c
        ON c.name = 'Funding Group ' || ef.wallet_a
       AND c.cluster_type = 'funding'
      CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (wr.wallet_a), (wr.wallet_b)) AS edge(wallet_address)
      JOIN wallets w ON w.address = edge.wallet_address
    )`;

  await withTransaction(async (client) => {

  // Create a cluster per eligible funder (see eligibleFundersCte: a funded-wallet
  // count inside the band, and not an excluded hub). A lone A->B funding pair is
  // too weak to be a "group" and previously produced a constant-0.85 cluster from
  // a single dust transfer. Confidence is derived from the actual edge confidences
  // (which scale with transfer size) plus a small bonus per extra funded wallet.
    await client.query(`
      WITH ${eligibleFundersCte}
      INSERT INTO wallet_clusters (name, cluster_type, confidence, chain)
      SELECT
        'Funding Group ' || wr.wallet_a,
        'funding',
        LEAST(0.95, AVG(wr.confidence) + 0.05 * (COUNT(DISTINCT wr.wallet_b) - 1)),
        MAX(w.chain)
      FROM eligible_funders ef
      JOIN wallet_relationships wr
        ON wr.wallet_a = ef.wallet_a
       AND wr.relationship_type = 'funding'
      JOIN wallets w ON w.address = wr.wallet_a
      GROUP BY wr.wallet_a
      -- Refresh confidence on re-run so it tracks current evidence instead of
      -- being frozen at first-creation (DO NOTHING).
      ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET confidence = EXCLUDED.confidence, updated_at = NOW()
    `);

    // Remove members no longer implied by an eligible funding hub before
    // inserting any newly expected members. Valid existing rows retain joined_at.
    await client.query(`
      ${expectedMembershipsCte}
      DELETE FROM cluster_memberships cm
      USING wallet_clusters c
      WHERE cm.cluster_id = c.id
        AND c.cluster_type = 'funding'
        AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM expected_memberships expected
          WHERE expected.cluster_id = cm.cluster_id
            AND expected.wallet_address = cm.wallet_address
        )
    `);

    // Insert BOTH sides of each current funding edge.
    await client.query(`
      ${expectedMembershipsCte}
      INSERT INTO cluster_memberships (cluster_id, wallet_address)
      SELECT cluster_id, wallet_address
      FROM expected_memberships
      ON CONFLICT (cluster_id, wallet_address) DO NOTHING
    `);

    await client.query(`
      UPDATE wallet_clusters SET
        wallet_count = (
          SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cluster_memberships cm
          WHERE cm.cluster_id = wallet_clusters.id
        ),
        updated_at = NOW()
      WHERE cluster_type = 'funding'
    `);

    // Remove clusters that no longer have enough members. This is also how a
    // funder that grew past MAX_FUNDER_DEGREE, or was newly blacklisted, gets
    // its cluster torn down: it stops appearing in expected_memberships, so the
    // DELETE above empties it and it lands here at wallet_count = 0.
    await client.query(`
      DELETE FROM wallet_clusters
      WHERE cluster_type = 'funding' AND wallet_count < 2
    `);
  }, { isolationLevel: 'REPEATABLE READ' });
}

export async function generateBehavioralClusters() {
  // A synchronized pair = two DISTINCT wallets that bought the same token within
  // 5 minutes of each other, on >3 distinct occasions.
  //
  // The join is constrained to `w_low < w_high` so each unordered pair is
  // produced exactly once. Without that guard the previous version counted every
  // pair twice (A,B and B,A), inflating sync_count ~2x AND creating a duplicate
  // cluster per direction. We also count DISTINCT synchronized buys
  // (COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id)) rather than ordered transaction-pair combinations,
  // so the >3 threshold and the confidence formula reflect real buy events.
  //
  // Clusters are anchored on the lexicographically-smaller wallet of each pair.
  // (A fully transitive connected-components grouping is a future improvement;
  // this already removes the direction-duplication and double-counting.)
  const syncPairsCte = `
    WITH sync_pairs AS (
      SELECT
        t1.wallet_address AS w_low,
        t2.wallet_address AS w_high,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS sync_count,
        MAX(w1.chain) AS chain
      FROM transactions t1
      JOIN transactions t2
        ON t1.target_token = t2.target_token
        AND t1.wallet_address < t2.wallet_address
        AND ABS(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t1.timestamp - t2.timestamp))) < 300
      JOIN wallets w1 ON w1.address = t1.wallet_address
      JOIN wallets w2 ON w2.address = t2.wallet_address
      WHERE t1.direction = 'buy' AND t2.direction = 'buy'
        AND t1.target_token IS NOT NULL
        AND w1.chain = w2.chain
      GROUP BY t1.wallet_address, t2.wallet_address
      HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) > 3
    )`;
  const expectedMembershipsCte = `
    ${syncPairsCte},
    expected_memberships AS (
      SELECT DISTINCT c.id AS cluster_id, edge.wallet_address
      FROM sync_pairs sp
      JOIN wallet_clusters c
        ON c.name = 'Behavioral Group ' || sp.w_low
       AND c.cluster_type = 'behavioral'
      CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (sp.w_low), (sp.w_high)) AS edge(wallet_address)
      JOIN wallets w ON w.address = edge.wallet_address
    )`;

  await withTransaction(async (client) => {

    // Step 1: create one cluster per anchor wallet (w_low).
    await client.query(`
      ${syncPairsCte}
      INSERT INTO wallet_clusters (name, cluster_type, confidence, chain)
      SELECT
        'Behavioral Group ' || w_low,
        'behavioral',
        LEAST(0.95, 0.50 + (MAX(sync_count)::float * 0.05)),
        MAX(chain)
      FROM sync_pairs
      GROUP BY w_low
      ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET confidence = EXCLUDED.confidence, updated_at = NOW()
    `);

    // Step 2: remove members no longer present in the current synchronized-buy
    // graph, scoped strictly to behavioral clusters.
    await client.query(`
      ${expectedMembershipsCte}
      DELETE FROM cluster_memberships cm
      USING wallet_clusters c
      WHERE cm.cluster_id = c.id
        AND c.cluster_type = 'behavioral'
        AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM expected_memberships expected
          WHERE expected.cluster_id = cm.cluster_id
            AND expected.wallet_address = cm.wallet_address
        )
    `);

    // Step 3: add both wallets of every currently synchronized pair.
    await client.query(`
      ${expectedMembershipsCte}
      INSERT INTO cluster_memberships (cluster_id, wallet_address)
      SELECT cluster_id, wallet_address
      FROM expected_memberships
      ON CONFLICT (cluster_id, wallet_address) DO NOTHING
    `);

    await client.query(`
      UPDATE wallet_clusters SET
        wallet_count = (
          SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cluster_memberships cm
          WHERE cm.cluster_id = wallet_clusters.id
        ),
        updated_at = NOW()
      WHERE cluster_type = 'behavioral'
    `);

    // Remove clusters that no longer have enough members
    await client.query(`
      DELETE FROM wallet_clusters
      WHERE cluster_type = 'behavioral' AND wallet_count < 2
    `);
  }, { isolationLevel: 'REPEATABLE READ' });
}

export async function updateClusterPerformance(clusterId: string) {
  await query(`
    UPDATE wallet_clusters SET
      total_realized_roi = (
        SELECT AVG(w.realized_roi) FROM wallets w
        JOIN cluster_memberships cm ON w.address = cm.wallet_address
        WHERE cm.cluster_id = $1
      ),
      avg_composite_score = (
        SELECT AVG(w.composite_score) FROM wallets w
        JOIN cluster_memberships cm ON w.address = cm.wallet_address
        WHERE cm.cluster_id = $1
      ),
      last_active = NOW(),
      updated_at = NOW()
    WHERE id = $1
  `, [clusterId]);
}

export async function listClusters() {
  return query(`
    SELECT id, name, cluster_type, confidence, wallet_count, 
           total_realized_roi, avg_composite_score, status, 
           last_active, created_at, chain
    FROM wallet_clusters
    WHERE status = 'active'
    ORDER BY confidence DESC, wallet_count DESC, id DESC
  `);
}

export async function getClusterWithMembers(clusterId: string) {
  const [cluster] = await query<{ id: string; name: string; confidence: number }>(
    `SELECT * FROM wallet_clusters WHERE id = $1`, [clusterId]
  );
  if (!cluster) return null;

  const members = await query(
    `SELECT w.address, w.tier, w.composite_score, w.win_rate, w.realized_roi, cm.confidence, cm.joined_at
     FROM cluster_memberships cm
     JOIN wallets w ON w.address = cm.wallet_address
     WHERE cm.cluster_id = $1
     ORDER BY w.composite_score DESC NULLS LAST`,
    [clusterId]
  );

  return { cluster, members };
}

==> packages/db/src/copy-eligibility.ts <==
import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { withTransaction } from './transaction.js';

/**
 * Facts the copy-eligibility policy needs about a canonical signal's source,
 * read once at the claim boundary.
 *
 * These are deliberately read fresh rather than carried on the trade job. The
 * signal-engine already filters on `wallets.status = 'active'` when it emits a
 * candidate, but the nightly scorer sweep can pause a wallet in between — so by
 * the time the executor claims, the emit-time snapshot may be hours stale and
 * describe a source we no longer follow.
 */
export interface CopyEligibilityFacts {
  signalId: string;
  signalStatus: string;
  chain: Chain;
  walletAddress: string;
  /** A `wallets` row exists for the source address at all. */
  walletKnown: boolean;
  /** `wallets.status`; empty string when the wallet is unknown. */
  walletStatus: string;
  walletTradeCount: number;
  /** The source wallet belongs to at least one cluster that is still active. */
  clusterSelected: boolean;
  /** Confirmed USD this wallet traded inside the activity lookback window. */
  sourceActivityUsd: number;
  eventAt: Date;
}

export interface CopyEligibilityRejection {
  account: string;
  signalId: string;
  chain: Chain;
  walletAddress: string | null;
  reasons: string[];
  rejectedAt?: Date;
}

interface CopyEligibilityFactsRow {
  signal_id: string;
  signal_status: string;
  chain: Chain;
  wallet_address: string;
  wallet_known: boolean;
  wallet_status: string;
  wallet_trade_count: string;
  cluster_selected: boolean;
  source_activity_usd: string;
  event_at: Date;
}

async function inTransaction<T>(operation: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  return withTransaction(operation);
}

/**
 * Load the source facts for a canonical signal, or `null` when the signal is
 * not linked to a source trade. A `null` result is not "eligible by default":
 * the caller must treat an absent fact set as a rejection, because a signal
 * with no observable source is exactly the case we cannot vouch for.
 */
export async function loadCopyEligibilityFacts(input: {
  signalId: string;
  activityLookbackMs: number;
  now?: Date;
}): Promise<CopyEligibilityFacts | null> {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(input.activityLookbackMs) || input.activityLookbackMs <= 0) {
    throw new Error('activityLookbackMs must be a positive safe integer');
  }
  const now = input.now ?? new Date();
  const rows = await query<CopyEligibilityFactsRow>(
    `SELECT
       signal.id                                  AS signal_id,
       signal.status                              AS signal_status,
       source.chain                               AS chain,
       source.wallet_address                      AS wallet_address,
       source.event_at                            AS event_at,
       (wallet.address IS NOT NULL)               AS wallet_known,
       COALESCE(wallet.status, '')                AS wallet_status,
       COALESCE(wallet.total_trades, 0)::text     AS wallet_trade_count,
       EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM cluster_memberships membership
           JOIN wallet_clusters cluster ON cluster.id = membership.cluster_id
          WHERE membership.wallet_address = source.wallet_address
            AND cluster.status = 'active'
       )                                          AS cluster_selected,
       COALESCE((
         SELECT SUM(activity.amount_usd)
           FROM source_trades activity
          WHERE activity.wallet_address = source.wallet_address
            AND activity.chain = source.chain
            AND activity.confirmation_state IN ('confirmed', 'finalized')
            AND activity.event_at >= $2::timestamptz - ($3::bigint * INTERVAL '1 millisecond')
       ), 0)::text                                AS source_activity_usd
     FROM signals signal
     JOIN source_trades source ON source.id = signal.source_trade_id
     LEFT JOIN wallets wallet ON wallet.address = source.wallet_address
     WHERE signal.id = $1`,
    [input.signalId, now, input.activityLookbackMs]
  );
  const row = rows[0];
  if (!row) return null;
  return {
    signalId: row.signal_id,
    signalStatus: row.signal_status,
    chain: row.chain,
    walletAddress: row.wallet_address,
    walletKnown: row.wallet_known,
    walletStatus: row.wallet_status,
    walletTradeCount: Number(row.wallet_trade_count),
    clusterSelected: row.cluster_selected,
    sourceActivityUsd: Number(row.source_activity_usd),
    eventAt: row.event_at
  };
}

/**
 * Persist why a signal was refused and take it out of the claimable set.
 *
 * Both writes happen in one transaction. Recording the reason without marking
 * the signal would let the next queue retry re-run the same rejected policy,
 * and marking it without recording the reason would leave an operator with a
 * `rejected` row and no way to tell which gate fired.
 *
 * The status update is deliberately narrow: only a signal that is still
 * awaiting a claim is moved. A signal already `executing` or `executed` has
 * money behind it and must not be rewritten by a policy pass.
 */
export async function recordCopyEligibilityRejection(
  input: CopyEligibilityRejection
): Promise<boolean> {
  if (input.reasons.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('recordCopyEligibilityRejection requires at least one reason');
  }
  const rejectedAt = input.rejectedAt ?? new Date();
  return inTransaction(async (client) => {
    await client.query(
      `INSERT INTO copy_eligibility_rejections
         (account, signal_id, chain, wallet_address, reasons, rejected_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6)
       ON CONFLICT (account, signal_id) DO UPDATE
         SET reasons = EXCLUDED.reasons,
             rejected_at = EXCLUDED.rejected_at`,
      [
        input.account,
        input.signalId,
        input.chain,
        input.walletAddress,
        input.reasons,
        rejectedAt
      ]
    );
    const updated = await client.query(
      `UPDATE signals
          SET status = 'rejected'
        WHERE id = $1
          AND status IN ('pending', 'eligible', 'alerted')`,
      [input.signalId]
    );
    return (updated.rowCount ?? 0) === 1;
  });
}

import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  query: vi.fn(),
  withTransaction: vi.fn()
}));

vi.mock('./client.js', () => ({ query: mocks.query }));
vi.mock('./transaction.js', () => ({ withTransaction: mocks.withTransaction }));

import { recordCopyExecutionEvidence } from './copy-trade-lifecycle.js';

/**
 * The `copy_execution_evidence` write path, driven without Postgres (S4-M35).
 *
 * `packages/db` has no database available in this environment, so the transaction
 * boundary is stubbed and a fake client answers each statement by matching its SQL.
 * That is enough to assert the two things this fix turns on, both of which live in
 * the statement text and its parameters rather than in the server:
 *
 *   1. what gets written into `quote_quantity` versus `quote_native_quantity` —
 *      i.e. that a SOL amount is converted and never stored as if it were USD;
 *   2. that an unknown USD total is stored as NULL rather than as `0`.
 *
 * Server-enforced behaviour (the CHECK constraints, the immutability trigger, the
 * recursive ledger's arithmetic) is covered by
 * `tests/integration/copy-trade-lifecycle.integration.test.ts`, which needs a real
 * database and has not been run here.
 */

interface RecordedCall {
  sql: string;
  params: unknown[];
}

const EXECUTION_ID = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111';

function executionRow(overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
  return {
    id: EXECUTION_ID,
    signal_id: null,
    source_trade_id: '22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222',
    chain: 'solana',
    target_account: 'solana:TargetAccount',

    execution_mode: 'live',
    client_order_id: 'copy-1',
    state: 'submitted',
    requested_base_quantity: '100',
    requested_quote_quantity: null,
    confirmed_base_quantity: '0',
    confirmed_quote_quantity: '0',

    reconciliation_attempts: 0,
    max_reconciliation_attempts: 10,
    source_position_before_quantity: null,

  };
}

function positionRow(overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {

    target_account: 'solana:TargetAccount',
    chain: 'solana',

    cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count: 0,
    last_evidence_at: new Date('2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z'),
    ...overrides
  };
}

/**
 * A client that answers by statement shape rather than by call index, so inserting
 * an unrelated statement into the write path does not silently shift every stubbed
 * response by one.
 */
function fakeClient(options: {
  totals: {
    confirmed_base_quantity: string;
    valued_quote_usd_sum: string | null;
    valued_fill_count: string;
    unvalued_fill_count: string;
    completes_execution: boolean;
  };
  evidenceQuoteQuantity?: string | null;
  evidenceNativeQuantity?: string | null;
  evidenceCurrency?: string | null;
  evidenceNativeUsdPrice?: string | null;
}) {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = [];
  const client = {
    query: vi.fn(async (sql: string, params: unknown[] = []) => {
      calls.push({ sql, params });
      if (sql.includes('FROM copy_executions') && sql.includes('FOR UPDATE')) {
        return { rows: [executionRow()] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('INSERT INTO copy_execution_evidence')) {
        return { rows: [] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('FROM copy_execution_evidence') && sql.includes('payload_matches')) {
        return {
          rows: [{
            id: '44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444',
            execution_id: EXECUTION_ID,
            evidence_type: 'chain_receipt',
            evidence_id: 'sig',
            base_quantity: '100',
            quote_quantity: options.evidenceQuoteQuantity ?? null,
            quote_native_quantity: options.evidenceNativeQuantity ?? null,
            quote_currency: options.evidenceCurrency ?? null,
            quote_native_usd_price: options.evidenceNativeUsdPrice ?? null,
            price_usd: null,
            confirmation_state: 'confirmed',
            completes_execution: true,
            occurred_at: new Date('2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z'),
            payload_matches: true
          }]
        };
      }
      if (sql.includes('INSERT INTO copy_positions')) return { rows: [] };
      if (sql.includes('FROM copy_positions') && sql.includes('FOR UPDATE')) {
        return { rows: [{ id: positionRow().id }] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('INSERT INTO copy_position_applications')) return { rows: [] };
      if (sql.includes('SELECT source.wallet_address') && sql.includes('FROM source_trades source')) {
        return { rows: [{ wallet_address: 'master-wallet', direction: 'buy', signal_id: 'signal-id' }] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('INSERT INTO copy_position_master_lots')) return { rows: [] };
      if (sql.includes('valued_quote_usd_sum')) {
        return { rows: [options.totals] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('UPDATE copy_positions position')) {
        return { rows: [positionRow()] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('INSERT INTO copy_execution_state_history')) return { rows: [] };
      if (sql.includes('UPDATE copy_executions')) {
        return { rows: [executionRow({ state: 'confirmed' })] };
      }
      if (sql.includes('UPDATE signals')) return { rows: [] };
      throw new Error(`unstubbed statement: ${sql.slice(0, 120)}`);
    })
  };
  return { client, calls };
}

function findCall(calls: RecordedCall[], needle: string): RecordedCall {
  const call = calls.find((entry) => entry.sql.includes(needle));
  if (!call) throw new Error(`no statement contained ${needle}`);
  return call;
}

describe('recordCopyExecutionEvidence quote units', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    mocks.query.mockReset();
    mocks.withTransaction.mockReset();
  });

  function runWith(
    options: Parameters<typeof fakeClient>[0],
    leg: Parameters<typeof recordCopyExecutionEvidence>[0]['quoteLeg']
  ) {
    const { client, calls } = fakeClient(options);
    mocks.withTransaction.mockImplementation(
      async (operation: (client: unknown) => Promise<unknown>) => operation(client)
    );
    return recordCopyExecutionEvidence({
      executionId: EXECUTION_ID,
      evidenceType: 'chain_receipt',
      evidenceId: 'sig',
      baseQuantity: '100',
      quoteLeg: leg,
      confirmationState: 'confirmed',
      completesExecution: true,
      occurredAt: new Date('2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z')
    }).then((result) => ({ result, calls }));
  }

  it('converts a Solana-live SOL leg to USD and keeps the native amount beside it', async () => {
    const { result, calls } = await runWith(
      {
        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: '187.5',
          valued_fill_count: '1',
          unvalued_fill_count: '0',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: '187.5',
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '1.25',
        evidenceCurrency: 'SOL',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: '150'
      },
      { amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 150 }
    );

    const insert = findCall(calls, 'INSERT INTO copy_execution_evidence');
    // params: [executionId, type, evidenceId, base, quoteUsd, native, currency, rate, ...]
    expect(insert.params[4]).toBe('187.5');
    // The regression this whole item exists to prevent: 1.25 SOL must not land in
    // the column named quote_quantity.
    expect(insert.params[4]).not.toBe('1.25');
    expect(insert.params[5]).toBe('1.25');
    expect(insert.params[6]).toBe('SOL');
    expect(insert.params[7]).toBe('150');
    expect(result.fillValuation).toMatchObject({
      code: 'valued',
      currency: 'SOL',
      nativeAmount: '1.25',
      usdAmount: '187.5'
    });
  });

  it('writes a USD leg unconverted, at a recorded rate of 1', async () => {
    const { calls } = await runWith(
      {
        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: '4.5',
          valued_fill_count: '1',
          unvalued_fill_count: '0',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: '4.5',
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '4.5',
        evidenceCurrency: 'USD',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: '1'
      },
      { amount: '4.5', currency: 'USD' }
    );

    const insert = findCall(calls, 'INSERT INTO copy_execution_evidence');
    expect(insert.params[4]).toBe('4.5');
    expect(insert.params[5]).toBe('4.5');
    expect(insert.params[6]).toBe('USD');
    expect(insert.params[7]).toBe('1');
  });

  it('stores a NULL USD value but keeps the native record when the rate is unknown', async () => {
    const { result, calls } = await runWith(
      {
        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: null,
          valued_fill_count: '0',
          unvalued_fill_count: '1',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: null,
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '1.25',
        evidenceCurrency: 'SOL',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: null
      },
      { amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: null }
    );

    const insert = findCall(calls, 'INSERT INTO copy_execution_evidence');
    expect(insert.params[4]).toBeNull();
    expect(insert.params[5]).toBe('1.25');
    expect(insert.params[6]).toBe('SOL');
    expect(insert.params[7]).toBeNull();
    expect(result.fillValuation.code).toBe('native-price-unknown');

    // Unknown must not be laundered into zero on the execution row either.
    const update = findCall(calls, 'confirmed_quote_quantity = $3::numeric');
    expect(update.params[2]).toBeNull();
    expect(update.params[4]).toBe(1);
    expect(result.confirmedQuoteTotal).toMatchObject({
      code: 'unvalued',
      usdAmount: null,
      complete: false,
      unvaluedFillCount: 1
    });
  });

  it('carries the unvalued fill count so a partial total is not read as settled', async () => {
    const { result, calls } = await runWith(

        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: '187.5',
          valued_fill_count: '1',
          unvalued_fill_count: '2',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: '187.5',
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '1.25',
        evidenceCurrency: 'SOL',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: '150'
      },
      { amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 150 }
    );

    const update = findCall(calls, 'quote_unassessed_fill_count = $5::integer');
    expect(update.params[2]).toBe('187.5');
    expect(update.params[4]).toBe(2);
    expect(result.confirmedQuoteTotal.code).toBe('partially-valued');
    expect(result.confirmedQuoteTotal.complete).toBe(false);
  });

        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: null,
          valued_fill_count: '0',

          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: '187.5',
          valued_fill_count: '1',
          unvalued_fill_count: '0',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: '187.5',
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '1.25',
        evidenceCurrency: 'SOL',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: '150'
      },
      { amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 150 }
    );

    const totals = findCall(calls, 'valued_quote_usd_sum');
    // The old statement was COALESCE(SUM(quote_quantity), 0), which reported the
    // same number whether one fill was unvalued or all of them were.
    expect(totals.sql).not.toContain('COALESCE(SUM(quote_quantity), 0)');
    expect(totals.sql).toContain('COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE quote_quantity IS NOT NULL)');
    expect(totals.sql).toContain('COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE quote_quantity IS NULL)');
  });

  it('refuses a pre-054 amount that never declared its unit when rebuilding a position', async () => {
    const { calls } = await runWith(
      {
        totals: {
          confirmed_base_quantity: '100',
          valued_quote_usd_sum: '187.5',
          valued_fill_count: '1',
          unvalued_fill_count: '0',
          completes_execution: true
        },
        evidenceQuoteQuantity: '187.5',
        evidenceNativeQuantity: '1.25',
        evidenceCurrency: 'SOL',
        evidenceNativeUsdPrice: '150'
      },
      { amount: '1.25', currency: 'SOL', nativeUsdPrice: 150 }
    );

    const rebuild = findCall(calls, 'UPDATE copy_positions position');
    // The unit gate: an amount only enters the cost basis if its row declares a
    // currency, so a legacy SOL amount falls through to base_quantity * price_usd.
    expect(rebuild.sql).toContain('WHEN evidence.quote_currency IS NOT NULL THEN evidence.quote_quantity');
    expect(rebuild.sql).toContain(
      'ledger.cost_basis + COALESCE(event.quote_usd, event.base_quantity * event.price_usd, 0)'
    );
    // And the ledger no longer prefers the raw column.
    expect(rebuild.sql).not.toContain('COALESCE(event.quote_quantity,');
    // Every buy the trailing zero swallowed is counted.
    expect(rebuild.sql).toContain('cost_basis_unvalued_fill_count = final.unvalued');
  });
});

function assertIdentifier(name: string, value: string, maximumLength = 256): string {
  if (!value || value.trim() !== value || value.length > maximumLength) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be non-empty, trimmed, and at most ${maximumLength} characters`);
  }
  return value;
}

function assertDate(name: string, value: Date): Date {
  if (!(value instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(value.getTime())) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be a valid date`);
  }
  return value;
}

const UUID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;

/**
 * Field separator used when hashing a tuple into a stable identity string.
 *
 * MUST stay equal to the separator `buildCopyExecutionClientOrderId` passes to
 * `Array.prototype.join`, or the tenant-scoped digest stops matching the
 * unscoped one for the same tuple. NUL is safe as a separator because no field
 * being joined can contain it: `assertIdentifier` rejects untrimmed input, and
 * the values are UUIDs, chain names, addresses and a fixed mode enum.
 */
const COPY_IDENTITY_SEPARATOR = String.fromCharCode(0);

/**
 * Normalise an acting tenant id to either a canonical UUID or `null`.
 *
 * `null` is a real, load-bearing value here, not a missing one: migration 050
 * gives every legacy operator row `user_id NULL`, and the tenancy-aware unique
 * indexes are declared `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` so those rows still collide with
 * each other. That means a caller that has no user in scope MUST reach `null`
 * and not some placeholder string — a placeholder would be a distinct tenant
 * and would silently fork the operator's position ledger.
 *
 * `users.id` is a UUID (039_users.sql:22), so anything that is not
 * UUID-shaped is a bug in the caller rather than a tenant we have never seen.
 * Rejecting it here keeps a stray account label (`'operator'`, an email, a
 * chain-prefixed address) from being written into the tenancy column, where it
 * would fail the foreign key at a confusing distance from its origin.
 */
export function normalizeTenantId(value: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  if (trimmed === '') return null;
  if (!UUID_PATTERN.test(trimmed)) {
    throw new Error(`userId must be a UUID or null, received ${JSON.stringify(value)}`);
  }
  return trimmed.toLowerCase();
}

function decimal(name: string, value: DecimalInput, allowZero = false): string {
  const normalized = typeof value === 'number' ? String(value) : value;
  if (
    !normalized
    || normalized.trim() !== normalized
    || !/^(?:\d+\.?\d*|\d*\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?$/.test(normalized)
  ) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be an unsigned decimal`);
  }
  const numeric = Number(normalized);
  if (!Number.isFinite(numeric) || (allowZero ? numeric < 0 : numeric <= 0)) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be ${allowZero ? 'non-negative' : 'positive'}`);
  }
  return normalized;
}

function optionalDecimal(name: string, value: DecimalInput | null | undefined): string | null {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? null : decimal(name, value, true);
}

async function inTransaction<T>(operation: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  return withTransaction(operation);
}

function isStaleConfirmation(
  current: SourceConfirmationState,
  proposed: SourceConfirmationState
): boolean {
  if (current === 'reversed') return proposed !== 'reversed';
  if (current === 'finalized') return proposed === 'observed' || proposed === 'confirmed';
  return current === 'confirmed' && proposed === 'observed';
}

async function ensureSourcePosition(client: PoolClient, source: SourceTradeDbRow): Promise<void> {
  await client.query(
    `INSERT INTO wallet_positions (wallet_address, chain, token_mint)
     VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
     ON CONFLICT (wallet_address, chain, token_mint) DO NOTHING`,
    [source.wallet_address, source.chain, source.token_mint]
  );
  await client.query(
    `SELECT wallet_address
       FROM wallet_positions
      WHERE wallet_address = $1 AND chain = $2 AND token_mint = $3
      FOR UPDATE`,
    [source.wallet_address, source.chain, source.token_mint]
  );
}

async function rebuildSourcePosition(
  client: PoolClient,
  source: SourceTradeDbRow
): Promise<PositionRecord> {
  const result = await client.query<QueryResultRow & {
    wallet_address: string;
    chain: Chain;
    token_mint: string;
    confirmed_quantity: string;
    cost_basis_usd: string;
    total_acquired_quantity: string;
    total_reduced_quantity: string;
    unmatched_reduction_quantity: string;
    last_event_at: Date | null;
  }>(
    `WITH RECURSIVE ordered_events AS (
       SELECT
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY st.event_at, st.id)::bigint AS sequence,
         st.direction,
         st.token_amount,
         st.amount_usd,
         st.price_usd,
         st.event_at
       FROM source_position_applications spa
       JOIN source_trades st ON st.id = spa.source_trade_id
       WHERE spa.wallet_address = $1
         AND spa.chain = $2
         AND spa.token_mint = $3
         AND spa.active
     ), ledger AS (
       SELECT
         0::bigint AS sequence,
         wp.opening_balance AS quantity,
         wp.opening_cost_basis_usd AS cost_basis,
         0::numeric AS acquired,
         0::numeric AS reduced,
         0::numeric AS unmatched
       FROM wallet_positions wp
       WHERE wp.wallet_address = $1 AND wp.chain = $2 AND wp.token_mint = $3

       UNION ALL

       SELECT
         event.sequence,
         CASE
           WHEN event.direction IN ('buy', 'transfer_in') THEN ledger.quantity + event.token_amount
           ELSE GREATEST(0, ledger.quantity - event.token_amount)
         END,
         CASE
           WHEN event.direction IN ('buy', 'transfer_in') THEN
             ledger.cost_basis + COALESCE(event.amount_usd, event.token_amount * event.price_usd, 0)
           WHEN ledger.quantity = 0 THEN 0
           ELSE GREATEST(
             0,
             ledger.cost_basis - (ledger.cost_basis / ledger.quantity) * LEAST(ledger.quantity, event.token_amount)
           )
         END,
         ledger.acquired + CASE WHEN event.direction IN ('buy', 'transfer_in') THEN event.token_amount ELSE 0 END,
         ledger.reduced + CASE WHEN event.direction IN ('sell', 'transfer_out') THEN event.token_amount ELSE 0 END,
         ledger.unmatched + CASE
           WHEN event.direction IN ('sell', 'transfer_out') THEN GREATEST(0, event.token_amount - ledger.quantity)
           ELSE 0
         END
       FROM ledger
       JOIN ordered_events event ON event.sequence = ledger.sequence + 1
     ), final AS (
       SELECT * FROM ledger ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 1
     ), last_event AS (
       SELECT MAX(event_at) AS event_at FROM ordered_events
     )
     UPDATE wallet_positions position
        SET balance = final.quantity,
            cost_basis_usd = final.cost_basis,
            total_acquired_quantity = final.acquired,
            total_reduced_quantity = final.reduced,
            unmatched_reduction_quantity = final.unmatched,
            last_event_at = last_event.event_at,
            updated_at = NOW()
       FROM final, last_event
      WHERE position.wallet_address = $1
        AND position.chain = $2
        AND position.token_mint = $3
     RETURNING
       position.wallet_address,
       position.chain,
