         SET active = EXCLUDED.active,
             user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id,
             position_id = EXCLUDED.position_id,
             updated_at = NOW()`,
      [
        evidence.id,
        execution.id,
        execution.target_account,
        execution.chain,
        execution.token_mint,
        isAppliedSourceConfirmation(evidence.confirmation_state),
        evidenceUserId,
        positionId
      ]
    );

    await synchronizePositionLots(client, {
      execution,
      evidence,
      positionId
    });

    // `SUM` skips NULLs, so the old `COALESCE(SUM(quote_quantity), 0)` produced the
    // same confident-looking number whether every confirmed fill was valued in USD,
    // some were, or none were. The two counts alongside the sum are what let
    // `summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal` tell those three cases apart, so an unknown
    // total can be stored as NULL instead of as a zero nobody can question.
    const totalsResult = await client.query<{
      confirmed_base_quantity: string;
      valued_quote_usd_sum: string | null;
      valued_fill_count: string;
      unvalued_fill_count: string;
      completes_execution: boolean;
    }>(
      `SELECT
         COALESCE(SUM(base_quantity), 0)::text AS confirmed_base_quantity,
         SUM(quote_quantity)::text AS valued_quote_usd_sum,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE quote_quantity IS NOT NULL)::text AS valued_fill_count,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE quote_quantity IS NULL)::text AS unvalued_fill_count,
         COALESCE(BOOL_OR(completes_execution), FALSE) AS completes_execution
       FROM copy_execution_evidence
       WHERE execution_id = $1
         AND confirmation_state IN ('confirmed', 'finalized')`,
      [execution.id]
    );
    const totals = totalsResult.rows[0] as {
      confirmed_base_quantity: string;
      valued_quote_usd_sum: string | null;
      valued_fill_count: string;
      unvalued_fill_count: string;
      completes_execution: boolean;
    };
    const confirmedQuoteTotal = summarizeConfirmedQuoteTotal({
      valuedFillCount: Number(totals.valued_fill_count),
      unvaluedFillCount: Number(totals.unvalued_fill_count),
      valuedUsdSum: totals.valued_quote_usd_sum
    });

    const preStatePosition = await rebuildCopyPosition(client, execution);
    const hasConfirmedQuantity = Number(totals.confirmed_base_quantity) > 0;
    const hasLedgerMismatch = Number(preStatePosition.unmatchedReductionQuantity) > 0;
    let desiredState: CopyExecutionState = execution.state;
    if (hasLedgerMismatch || (!hasConfirmedQuantity && evidence.confirmation_state === 'reversed')) {
      desiredState = 'reconciliation_required';
    } else if (hasConfirmedQuantity) {
      desiredState = totals.completes_execution ? 'confirmed' : 'partially_filled';
    }

    if (
      (desiredState === 'partially_filled' || desiredState === 'confirmed')
      && execution.state === 'requested'
    ) {
      execution = await setCopyExecutionState(
        client,
        execution,
        'reconciliation_required',
        'confirmed evidence arrived before submission state was persisted'
      );
    } else if (execution.state === 'confirmed' && desiredState === 'partially_filled') {
      execution = await setCopyExecutionState(
        client,
        execution,
        'reconciliation_required',
        'previously confirmed evidence was reversed'
      );
    }
    execution = await setCopyExecutionState(
      client,
      execution,
      desiredState,
      `${input.evidenceType}:${evidenceId}`
    );

    const updatedExecution = await client.query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
      `UPDATE copy_executions
          SET confirmed_base_quantity = $2::numeric,
              confirmed_quote_quantity = $3::numeric,
              quote_unassessed_fill_count = $5::integer,
              reserved_base_quantity = CASE
                WHEN direction <> 'sell' OR $4 = 'confirmed' THEN 0
                ELSE GREATEST(0, requested_base_quantity - $2::numeric)
              END,
              next_reconciliation_at = CASE
                WHEN $4 = 'reconciliation_required' THEN COALESCE(next_reconciliation_at, NOW())
                WHEN $4 = 'confirmed' THEN NULL
                ELSE next_reconciliation_at
              END,
              reconciliation_claim_id = CASE WHEN $4 = 'confirmed' THEN NULL ELSE reconciliation_claim_id END,
              reconciliation_claimed_at = CASE WHEN $4 = 'confirmed' THEN NULL ELSE reconciliation_claimed_at END,
              updated_at = NOW()
        WHERE id = $1
      RETURNING ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}`,
      [
        execution.id,
        totals.confirmed_base_quantity,
        confirmedQuoteTotal.usdAmount,
        desiredState,
        confirmedQuoteTotal.unvaluedFillCount
      ]
    );
    execution = updatedExecution.rows[0] as CopyExecutionDbRow;
    const position = await rebuildCopyPosition(client, execution);
    if (
      execution.state === 'confirmed'
      && execution.signal_id
      && !execution.exit_lot_id
      && execution.execution_mode !== 'shadow'
    ) {
      await client.query(
        `UPDATE signals
         SET status = 'executed', executed_at = COALESCE(executed_at, NOW())
         WHERE id = $1 AND status IN ('executing', 'eligible', 'alerted')`,
        [execution.signal_id]
      );
    }
    return {
      execution: mapCopyExecution(execution),
      position,
      fillValuation,
      confirmedQuoteTotal
    };
  };
  return operation();
}

export async function getCopyExecutionById(id: string): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord | null> {
  const rows = await query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
    `SELECT ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}
       FROM copy_executions
      WHERE id = $1`,
    [assertIdentifier('id', id, 128)]
  );
  return rows[0] ? mapCopyExecution(rows[0]) : null;
}

export async function getCopyExecutionByClientOrderId(input: {
  chain: Chain;
  targetAccount: string;
  clientOrderId: string;
}): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord | null> {
  const target = resolveChainAddress(input.targetAccount, input.chain);
  const rows = await query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
    `SELECT ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}
       FROM copy_executions
      WHERE chain = $1 AND target_account = $2 AND client_order_id = $3`,
    [input.chain, target.prefixed, assertIdentifier('clientOrderId', input.clientOrderId, 128)]
  );
  return rows[0] ? mapCopyExecution(rows[0]) : null;
}

export async function getCopyExecutionByClientOrderIdentity(input: {
  chain: Chain;
  clientOrderId: string;
}): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord | null> {
  const rows = await query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
    `SELECT ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}
     FROM copy_executions
     WHERE chain = $1 AND client_order_id = $2
     ORDER BY id
     LIMIT 2`,
    [input.chain, assertIdentifier('clientOrderId', input.clientOrderId, 128)]
  );
  if (rows.length > 1) {
    throw new Error('Client order identity is ambiguous across target accounts');
  }
  return rows[0] ? mapCopyExecution(rows[0]) : null;
}

export async function getCopyExecutionBySubmissionIdentity(input: {
  chain: Chain;
  submissionType: 'transaction' | 'order';
  submissionId: string;
}): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord | null> {
  const rows = await query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
    `SELECT ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}
     FROM copy_executions
     WHERE chain = $1 AND submission_type = $2 AND submission_id = $3
     ORDER BY id
     LIMIT 2`,
    [
      input.chain,
      input.submissionType,
      assertIdentifier('submissionId', input.submissionId)
    ]
  );
  if (rows.length > 1) throw new Error('Submission identity is ambiguous');
  return rows[0] ? mapCopyExecution(rows[0]) : null;
}

export async function claimCopyExecutionsForReconciliation(input: {
  chain?: Chain;
  limit?: number;
  staleClaimBefore?: Date;
} = {}): Promise<CopyExecutionRecord[]> {
  const limit = input.limit ?? 20;
  if (!Number.isInteger(limit) || limit < 1 || limit > 100) {
    throw new Error('limit must be an integer between 1 and 100');
  }
  const staleClaimBefore = assertDate(
    'staleClaimBefore',
    input.staleClaimBefore ?? new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000)
  );
  const rows = await query<CopyExecutionDbRow>(
    `WITH candidates AS (
       SELECT id AS candidate_id
       FROM copy_executions
       WHERE state IN ('submitted', 'partially_filled', 'reconciliation_required')
         AND ($1::text IS NULL OR chain = $1)
         AND COALESCE(next_reconciliation_at, submitted_at, requested_at) <= NOW()
         AND reconciliation_attempts < max_reconciliation_attempts
         AND (reconciliation_claimed_at IS NULL OR reconciliation_claimed_at < $2)
       ORDER BY COALESCE(next_reconciliation_at, submitted_at, requested_at), id
       FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
       LIMIT $3
     )
     UPDATE copy_executions execution
        SET reconciliation_claim_id = gen_random_uuid(),
            reconciliation_claimed_at = NOW(),
            reconciliation_attempts = execution.reconciliation_attempts + 1,
            updated_at = NOW()
       FROM candidates
      WHERE execution.id = candidates.candidate_id
     RETURNING ${COPY_EXECUTION_COLUMNS}`,
    [input.chain ?? null, staleClaimBefore, limit]
  );
  return rows.map(mapCopyExecution);
}

export async function releaseCopyExecutionReconciliationClaim(input: {
  executionId: string;
  claimId: string;
  retryAt?: Date | null;
}): Promise<boolean> {
  const retryAt = input.retryAt ? assertDate('retryAt', input.retryAt) : null;
  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
    `UPDATE copy_executions
        SET reconciliation_claim_id = NULL,
            reconciliation_claimed_at = NULL,
            next_reconciliation_at = CASE
              WHEN state IN ('confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled') THEN NULL
              ELSE $3::timestamptz
            END,
            updated_at = NOW()
      WHERE id = $1
        AND reconciliation_claim_id = $2
      RETURNING id`,
    [
      assertIdentifier('executionId', input.executionId, 128),
      assertIdentifier('claimId', input.claimId, 128),
      retryAt
    ]
  );
  return rows.length === 1;
}

==> packages/db/src/credentials.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { hash as argonHash } from '@node-rs/argon2';
import {
  hashPassword,
  verifyPassword,
  verifyPasswordAgainstDummy,
  generateToken,
  hashToken,
  tokenMatches,
  generateApiKey,
  parseApiKeyPrefix
} from './credentials.js';

describe('credentials', () => {
  describe('password hashing', () => {
    it('accepts the correct password', async () => {
      const stored = await hashPassword('correct-horse-battery');
      expect(await verifyPassword(stored, 'correct-horse-battery')).toBe(true);
    });

    it('rejects the wrong password', async () => {
      const stored = await hashPassword('correct-horse-battery');
      expect(await verifyPassword(stored, 'wrong-horse-battery')).toBe(false);
    });

    it('produces a different hash for the same password (salted)', async () => {
      const a = await hashPassword('same-password');
      const b = await hashPassword('same-password');
      expect(a).not.toBe(b);
      expect(await verifyPassword(a, 'same-password')).toBe(true);
      expect(await verifyPassword(b, 'same-password')).toBe(true);
    });

    it('fails closed on a malformed stored hash rather than throwing', async () => {
      // A truncated or corrupted column value must not surface as a 500 that
      // tells the caller their password was at least well-formed.
      expect(await verifyPassword('not-an-argon2-hash', 'password')).toBe(false);
      expect(await verifyPassword('', 'password')).toBe(false);
      expect(await verifyPassword('$argon2id$v=19$truncated', 'password')).toBe(false);
    });

    it('verifies hashes written under different parameters', async () => {
      // The design doc claims argon2 parameters can be retuned without a
      // migration because the encoded hash carries its own parameters. If that
      // is false, changing ARGON2_OPTIONS silently locks every existing user out.
      const legacy = await argonHash('legacy-password', {
        memoryCost: 19456,
        timeCost: 2,
        parallelism: 1
      });
      expect(legacy).toContain('m=19456');
      expect(await verifyPassword(legacy, 'legacy-password')).toBe(true);
      expect(await verifyPassword(legacy, 'wrong')).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('unknown-email timing defence', () => {
    it('always returns false', async () => {
      expect(await verifyPasswordAgainstDummy('anything')).toBe(false);
      expect(await verifyPasswordAgainstDummy('')).toBe(false);
    });

    it('costs about the same as a real verify, so timing does not enumerate users', async () => {
      const stored = await hashPassword('pw');
      // Warm both paths first; the dummy hash is generated lazily on first use
      // and that one-off cost would otherwise dominate the measurement.
      await verifyPassword(stored, 'pw');
      await verifyPasswordAgainstDummy('pw');

      const realStart = Date.now();
      await verifyPassword(stored, 'pw');
      const realMs = Date.now() - realStart;

      const dummyStart = Date.now();
      await verifyPasswordAgainstDummy('pw');
      const dummyMs = Date.now() - dummyStart;

      // Deliberately loose: this asserts the same order of magnitude, not a
      // constant-time guarantee, and must not flake on a busy CI box.
      expect(dummyMs).toBeGreaterThan(realMs * 0.25);
      expect(dummyMs).toBeLessThan(realMs * 4 + 50);
    });
  });

  describe('opaque tokens', () => {
    it('generates distinct high-entropy tokens', () => {
      const seen = new Set(Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => generateToken()));
      expect(seen.size).toBe(50);
      // 32 bytes base64url = 43 chars.
      expect([...seen][0]!.length).toBe(43);
    });

    it('matches only the digest of the same token', () => {
      const token = generateToken();
      expect(tokenMatches(hashToken(token), hashToken(token))).toBe(true);
      expect(tokenMatches(hashToken(token), hashToken(generateToken()))).toBe(false);
    });

    it('returns false rather than throwing on a length mismatch', () => {
      // timingSafeEqual throws on unequal lengths, which would itself be a leak
      // and a 500. The guard must absorb it.
      expect(() => tokenMatches(Buffer.from('short'), Buffer.alloc(32, 0xff))).not.toThrow();
      expect(tokenMatches(Buffer.from('short'), Buffer.alloc(32, 0xff))).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('api keys', () => {
    it('generates well-formed, distinct keys', () => {
      const a = generateApiKey();
      const b = generateApiKey();
      // Prefix is hex so it can never contain the `_` delimiter.
      expect(a.key).toMatch(/^swat_[0-9a-f]{8}_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/);
      expect(a.hash.length).toBe(32);
      expect(a.key).not.toBe(b.key);
      expect(a.prefix).not.toBe(b.prefix);
    });

    it('round-trips its lookup prefix even when the secret contains underscores', () => {
      // Regression: the first implementation parsed with `split('_')` and
      // required exactly 3 parts. base64url includes `_`, so any key whose
      // secret contained one was rejected as malformed — roughly half of them.
      for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
        const { key, prefix } = generateApiKey();
        expect(parseApiKeyPrefix(key)).toBe(prefix);
      }
      const withUnderscores = 'swat_0123abcd_secret_with_many_underscores';
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix(withUnderscores)).toBe('0123abcd');
    });

    it('rejects malformed keys', () => {
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('noprefix')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('vendor_0123abcd_xyz')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('swat_missing-secret')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('swat_0123abcd')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('swat_0123abcd_')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('swat_SHORT_secret')).toBe(null);
      // Non-hex prefix of the right length must still be rejected.
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('swat_zzzzzzzz_secret')).toBe(null);
      expect(parseApiKeyPrefix('')).toBe(null);
    });

    it('hashes the full key, not just the secret', () => {
      const { key, hash } = generateApiKey();
      expect(tokenMatches(hashToken(key), hash)).toBe(true);
      const secretOnly = key.split('_')[2]!;
      expect(tokenMatches(hashToken(secretOnly), hash)).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/credentials.ts <==
import { createHash, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
import { hash as argonHash, verify as argonVerify } from '@node-rs/argon2';

/**
 * Credential primitives shared by passwords, session tokens, and API keys.
 *
 * Two different hashing strategies live here on purpose, and conflating them is
 * the classic mistake in both directions:
 *
 *   * Passwords are low-entropy and human-chosen, so they need a *slow*,
 *     memory-hard hash (argon2id) to make offline cracking expensive.
 *   * Session tokens and API keys are 256 bits of CSPRNG output. There is no
 *     guessing attack to slow down, so a slow hash would buy nothing and would
 *     put ~110 ms on the critical path of *every authenticated request*.
 *     SHA-256 with a constant-time compare is the correct choice.
 */

/**
 * OWASP-recommended argon2id configuration. Measured at ~110 ms on a 2-core box;
 * see `docs/plans/stage-1-design.md` for the benchmark and why the higher-memory
 * variant was rejected.
 *
 * Safe to change without a migration: an argon2 encoded hash embeds its own
 * parameters, so `verifyPassword` keeps working against hashes written under any
 * previous configuration.
 */
const ARGON2_OPTIONS = {
  memoryCost: 47104,
  timeCost: 1,
  parallelism: 1
} as const;

/**
 * Verified against at login when the email is unknown, so that a request for a
 * nonexistent account costs the same time as one for a real account. Without
 * this, response latency is a user-enumeration oracle regardless of how careful
 * the response *bodies* are.
 *
 * Generated once at module load rather than hard-coded, so no real password can
 * ever collide with it.
 */
let dummyHashPromise: Promise<string> | null = null;
function dummyHash(): Promise<string> {
  dummyHashPromise ??= argonHash(randomBytes(32).toString('hex'), ARGON2_OPTIONS);
  return dummyHashPromise;
}

export async function hashPassword(password: string): Promise<string> {
  return argonHash(password, ARGON2_OPTIONS);
}

export async function verifyPassword(encoded: string, password: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    return await argonVerify(encoded, password);
  } catch {
    // A malformed or truncated stored hash must fail closed, not throw a 500
    // that tells the caller their password was at least well-formed.
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Burns the same time as a real verify for an account that does not exist.
 * Always returns false.
 */
export async function verifyPasswordAgainstDummy(password: string): Promise<boolean> {
  await argonVerify(await dummyHash(), password).catch(() => false);
  return false;
}

/** 256 bits of CSPRNG output, base64url so it is cookie- and header-safe. */
export function generateToken(): string {
  return randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
}

export function hashToken(token: string): Buffer {
  return createHash('sha256').update(token).digest();
}

/**
 * Constant-time comparison of two SHA-256 digests.
 *
 * `timingSafeEqual` throws on length mismatch, which would itself leak, so the
 * length is checked first and a mismatch simply returns false.
 */
export function tokenMatches(a: Buffer, b: Buffer): boolean {
  return a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

export interface ApiKeyParts {
  /** The full secret. Shown to the user once and never stored. */
  readonly key: string;
  /** Indexed lookup handle, safe to store and display. */
  readonly prefix: string;
  readonly hash: Buffer;
}

/** Length of the indexed lookup prefix, in characters. */
const API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH = 8;
const API_KEY_VENDOR = 'swat_';

/**
 * Format: `swat_<prefix>_<secret>`.
 *
 * The prefix is what makes verification one indexed equality instead of a scan
 * over every key row comparing hashes — that alternative degrades linearly with
 * key count and leaks timing.
 *
 * The prefix is **hex**, not base64url, specifically so it cannot contain `_` or
 * `-`. It appears in logs and support conversations, and a delimiter inside the
 * delimited field is how the first version of `parseApiKeyPrefix` broke.
 */
export function generateApiKey(): ApiKeyParts {
  const prefix = randomBytes(4).toString('hex').slice(0, API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH);
  const secret = randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
  const key = `${API_KEY_VENDOR}${prefix}_${secret}`;
  return { key, prefix, hash: hashToken(key) };
}

/**
 * Extracts the lookup prefix from a presented key, or null if malformed.
 *
 * Parsed by position rather than by `split('_')`: the secret is base64url, whose
 * alphabet includes `_`, so splitting yields a variable number of parts and a
 * naive `parts.length !== 3` check rejects perfectly valid keys. The prefix is
 * fixed-width, so slicing is both correct and unambiguous.
 */
export function parseApiKeyPrefix(key: string): string | null {
  if (!key.startsWith(API_KEY_VENDOR)) return null;
  const prefix = key.slice(API_KEY_VENDOR.length, API_KEY_VENDOR.length + API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH);
  if (prefix.length !== API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH) return null;
  if (!/^[0-9a-f]+$/.test(prefix)) return null;
  // The delimiter must sit exactly after the fixed-width prefix, and there must
  // be a non-empty secret after it.
  if (key[API_KEY_VENDOR.length + API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH] !== '_') return null;
  if (key.length <= API_KEY_VENDOR.length + API_KEY_PREFIX_LENGTH + 1) return null;
  return prefix;
}

import { query } from './client.js';

export async function logDiscoveryRun(source: string, seedValue: string, walletsDiscovered: number) {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO discovery_log (source, seed_value, wallets_discovered) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)`,
    [source, seedValue, walletsDiscovered]
  );
}

export async function findEarlyBuyers(tokenMint: string, minInvestedLamports = 500_000_000): Promise<string[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ wallet_address: string }>(`
    SELECT wallet_address
    FROM transactions
    WHERE target_token = $1
      AND direction = 'buy'
      AND timestamp < (
        SELECT MIN(timestamp) + INTERVAL '10 minutes'
        FROM transactions WHERE target_token = $1
      )
    GROUP BY wallet_address
    HAVING SUM(amount_in::bigint) > $2
    ORDER BY MIN(timestamp) ASC
    LIMIT 50
  `, [tokenMint, minInvestedLamports]);
  
  return rows.map(r => r.wallet_address);
}

export async function findFundedUnknownWallets(): Promise<string[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ wallet_b: string }>(`
    SELECT DISTINCT wr.wallet_b
    FROM wallet_relationships wr
    WHERE wr.relationship_type = 'funding'
      AND wr.wallet_a IN (
        SELECT address FROM wallets WHERE tier IN ('elite', 'pro')
      )
      AND wr.wallet_b NOT IN (SELECT address FROM wallets)
    LIMIT 100
  `);
  
  return rows.map(r => r.wallet_b);
}

export async function findFrequentCounterparties(): Promise<string[]> {
  const rows = await query<{ wallet_address: string }>(`
    SELECT t2.wallet_address
    FROM transactions t1
    JOIN transactions t2
      ON t1.target_token = t2.target_token
      AND ABS(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t1.timestamp - t2.timestamp))) < 300
      -- A wallet must not match itself (t1.id != t2.id) and the two sides must
      -- be different wallets; without these guards a wallet's own two buys
      -- match and counts are double-inflated.
      AND t1.id <> t2.id
      AND t1.wallet_address <> t2.wallet_address
    JOIN wallets w ON t1.wallet_address = w.address
    WHERE w.tier IN ('elite', 'pro')
      AND t1.direction = 'buy'
      AND t2.direction = 'buy'
      AND t2.wallet_address NOT IN (SELECT address FROM wallets)
    GROUP BY t2.wallet_address
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id) >= 5
    ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id) DESC
    LIMIT 50
  `);
  
  return rows.map(r => r.wallet_address);
}

==> packages/db/src/evm-nonce.test.ts <==
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const client = {
    query: vi.fn(),
    on: vi.fn(),
    off: vi.fn(),
    release: vi.fn()
  };
  return { client, connect: vi.fn(async () => client) };
});

vi.mock('./client.js', () => ({ pool: { connect: mocks.connect } }));

import { evmNonceLockKey, withEvmNonceLock } from './evm-nonce.js';

/** Mirrors `pg_try_advisory_lock` returning `locked`, then the unlock. */
function grantLock(): void {
  mocks.client.query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => {
    if (sql.includes('pg_try_advisory_lock')) return { rows: [{ locked: true }] };
    return { rows: [] };
  });
}

function refuseLock(): void {
  mocks.client.query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => {
    if (sql.includes('pg_try_advisory_lock')) return { rows: [{ locked: false }] };
    return { rows: [] };
  });
}

describe('evmNonceLockKey (S4-M12)', () => {
  it('separates the same address on different chains', () => {
    // Nonces are per (chain, account). Keying on the address alone would
    // serialise a user's Polymarket and Robinhood mirrors against each other.
    const account = '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111';
    expect(evmNonceLockKey('polygon', account)).not.toBe(
      evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', account)
    );
  });

  it('separates different accounts on the same chain', () => {
    expect(evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', '0x' + '1'.repeat(40))).not.toBe(
      evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', '0x' + '2'.repeat(40))
    );
  });

  it('treats checksummed and lowercased forms of one address as the same lock', () => {
    // viem returns `getAddress` (checksummed) form; `resolveChainValue`
    // lowercases every EVM value. If these keyed differently the two code paths
    // would not exclude each other, which is exactly the bug being fixed.
    const checksummed = '0xAbCdEf0123456789AbCdEf0123456789AbCdEf01';
    expect(evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', checksummed)).toBe(
      evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', checksummed.toLowerCase())
    );
  });

  it('ignores surrounding whitespace', () => {
    const account = '0x' + 'a'.repeat(40);
    expect(evmNonceLockKey('polygon', ` ${account} `)).toBe(evmNonceLockKey('polygon', account));
  });

  it('refuses a chain-prefixed address', () => {
    // A prefixed value would key differently from the bare address the executor
    // signs with, so the two would not exclude each other — silently.
    expect(() => evmNonceLockKey('robinhood-chain', 'robinhood-chain:0x' + '1'.repeat(40)))
      .toThrow(/bare address/);
  });

  it('refuses an empty account', () => {
    expect(() => evmNonceLockKey('polygon', '   ')).toThrow(/non-empty account/);
  });

  it('is namespaced away from other advisory locks', () => {
    expect(evmNonceLockKey('polygon', '0x' + '1'.repeat(40))).toContain('evm-nonce');
  });
});

describe('withEvmNonceLock (S4-M12)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    mocks.connect.mockImplementation(async () => mocks.client);
  });

  it('runs the critical section and releases the lock', async () => {
    grantLock();
    const run = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue('submitted');

    await expect(withEvmNonceLock({ chain: 'robinhood-chain', account: '0xabc', run }))
      .resolves.toEqual({ acquired: true, result: 'submitted' });

    expect(run).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    const sql = mocks.client.query.mock.calls.map(([text]) => text as string);
    expect(sql.some((s) => s.includes('pg_try_advisory_lock'))).toBe(true);
    expect(sql.some((s) => s.includes('pg_advisory_unlock'))).toBe(true);
    expect(mocks.client.release).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false);
  });

  it('does NOT run the critical section when another holder has the lock', async () => {
    // The whole point: a second concurrent job must not read the same pending
    // nonce. Running anyway would reintroduce the bug.
    refuseLock();
    const run = vi.fn();

    await expect(withEvmNonceLock({ chain: 'robinhood-chain', account: '0xabc', run }))
      .resolves.toEqual({ acquired: false });

    expect(run).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('does not attempt an unlock it never acquired', async () => {
    // Unlocking a lock we do not hold logs a Postgres warning and, worse, would
    // release a *different* holder's lock if the key ever collided.
    refuseLock();
    await withEvmNonceLock({ chain: 'polygon', account: '0xabc', run: vi.fn() });

    const sql = mocks.client.query.mock.calls.map(([text]) => text as string);
    expect(sql.some((s) => s.includes('pg_advisory_unlock'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('releases the lock and rethrows when the critical section fails', async () => {
    grantLock();
    const boom = new Error('submit failed');

    await expect(withEvmNonceLock({
      chain: 'robinhood-chain',
      account: '0xabc',
      run: vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(boom)
    })).rejects.toBe(boom);

    const sql = mocks.client.query.mock.calls.map(([text]) => text as string);
    expect(sql.some((s) => s.includes('pg_advisory_unlock'))).toBe(true);
    expect(mocks.client.release).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false);
  });

  it('destroys the connection when the unlock fails, so the lock cannot leak', async () => {
    // A session advisory lock dies with its backend session. Returning a client
    // that still holds the lock to the pool would wedge the account for the life
    // of that pooled connection — worse than failing this one trade.
    mocks.client.query.mockImplementation(async (sql: string) => {
      if (sql.includes('pg_try_advisory_lock')) return { rows: [{ locked: true }] };
      if (sql.includes('pg_advisory_unlock')) throw new Error('backend gone');
      return { rows: [] };
    });

    await expect(withEvmNonceLock({
      chain: 'robinhood-chain',
      account: '0xabc',
      run: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(1)
    })).resolves.toEqual({ acquired: true, result: 1 });

    expect(mocks.client.release).toHaveBeenCalledWith(true);
  });

  it('always returns the client to the pool', async () => {
    grantLock();
    await withEvmNonceLock({ chain: 'polygon', account: '0xabc', run: vi.fn() });
    expect(mocks.client.release).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it('registers and removes a client error handler around the critical section', async () => {
    // A database restart mid-trade emits 'error' on the checked-out client; with
    // no listener that throws and takes the process down instead of failing one
    // trade. Same hardening as `withTransaction`.
    grantLock();
    await withEvmNonceLock({ chain: 'polygon', account: '0xabc', run: vi.fn() });
    expect(mocks.client.on).toHaveBeenCalledWith('error', expect.any(Function));
    expect(mocks.client.off).toHaveBeenCalledWith('error', expect.any(Function));
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/evm-nonce.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { pool } from './client.js';

/**
 * Per-account EVM nonce serialisation (`S4-M12`).
 *
 * **This closes a correctness bug, not a performance one.** The EVM executor
 * reads the account's pending nonce and then increments it locally between the
 * approval and the swap (`apps/trade-executor/src/robinhood.ts`). Two concurrent
 * jobs for the same account read the *same* pending nonce, both submit a
 * transaction claiming it, and the node keeps one. The other is silently
 * replaced: no revert, no error, no failed job — a fill simply never happens,
 * and the only trace is a position that never opened. Under per-user fan-out
 * every user gets their own key, so the collision moves from "unlikely" to
 * "whenever one user's two signals overlap".
 *
 * `S3-25`'s concurrency-1-per-chain worker makes this rare inside a single
 * executor process, but it is not a fix: the pre-split `swat-trades` drain
 * worker is chain-agnostic and can run a second Robinhood job concurrently, and
 * a second executor replica reopens the window permanently. A lock outside the
 * process is the only thing that holds in both cases.
 *
 * **Why a session-level advisory lock rather than the transaction-scoped
 * `pg_advisory_xact_lock` used elsewhere in this file's sibling
 * (`copy-trade-lifecycle.ts:1404`):** the critical section spans RPC calls and a
 * receipt wait, so it cannot live inside one database transaction without
 * holding that transaction open across the network. A session lock releases on
 * `pg_advisory_unlock` *or* when the backend session ends — which means a crashed
 * executor releases its locks automatically, with no TTL sweep to write and no
 * possibility of a wedged account surviving a restart. A lease row in a table
 * would have needed both.
 */

/**
 * The lock's text key, hashed to a bigint by `hashtextextended` in SQL.
 *
 * Exported and pure so the keying rules are testable without a database, since
 * getting them wrong fails in the two directions that matter and neither is
 * visible at runtime: too coarse and unrelated accounts serialise against each
 * other, too fine and two jobs for one account both proceed.
 *
 * `chain` is part of the key because nonces are per (chain, account) — the same
 * address on `polygon` and on `robinhood-chain` has two independent nonce
 * sequences, and locking them together would serialise a user's Polymarket and
 * Robinhood mirrors for no reason. The address is lowercased because EVM
 * addresses are case-insensitive and arrive both checksummed (from viem, which
 * returns `getAddress` form) and lowercased (from `resolveChainValue`, which
 * lowercases every EVM value); the same account must not yield two keys.
 *
 * The `evm-nonce:` namespace keeps these keys away from every other advisory
 * lock in the codebase — notably `migrate.ts`'s `pg_advisory_lock(1)` and the
 * copy-position locks in `copy-trade-lifecycle.ts`.
 */
export function evmNonceLockKey(chain: Chain, account: string): string {
  const normalized = account.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!normalized) throw new Error('evmNonceLockKey requires a non-empty account');
  if (normalized.includes(':')) {
    // A chain-prefixed value here would key the lock differently from the bare
    // address the executor signs with, so the two would not exclude each other.
    throw new Error(`evmNonceLockKey requires a bare address, got prefixed ${account}`);
  }
  return JSON.stringify(['evm-nonce', chain, normalized]);
}

export type EvmNonceLockOutcome<T> =
  | { acquired: true; result: T }
  | { acquired: false; result?: undefined };

/**
 * Runs `run` while holding the exclusive nonce lock for `(chain, account)`.
 *
 * Returns `{acquired: false}` **without running** when another holder has the
 * lock. It does not block: a blocking `pg_advisory_lock` would sit past the
 * BullMQ job's lock duration and get the job declared stalled, which is a worse
 * failure than a clean retry. The caller should surface a retryable state so the
 * queue re-delivers the job after the current holder has submitted and the
 * node's pending nonce has advanced.
 *
 * Errors from `run` propagate unchanged, after the lock is released.
 */
export async function withEvmNonceLock<T>(input: {
  chain: Chain;
  account: string;
  run: () => Promise<T>;
}): Promise<EvmNonceLockOutcome<T>> {
  const key = evmNonceLockKey(input.chain, input.account);
  const client = await pool.connect();

  // Registered before the first statement, for the same reason
  // `withTransaction` does it: a checked-out client is not covered by the pool's
  // error handler, and an EventEmitter that emits 'error' with no listener
  // throws — so a database restart mid-trade would take the process down rather
  // than failing the one trade in flight.
  const swallowClientError = (): void => {};
  client.on('error', swallowClientError);

  let connectionBroken = false;
  let held = false;
  try {
    const locked = await client.query<{ locked: boolean }>(
      `SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0)) AS locked`,
      [key]
    );
    held = locked.rows[0]?.locked === true;
    if (!held) return { acquired: false };
    return { acquired: true, result: await input.run() };
  } catch (error) {
    // A failure here must not return the connection to the pool still holding
    // the lock; the finally below handles that. Rethrow so the caller fails the
    // trade rather than proceeding unserialised.
    throw error;
  } finally {
    if (held) {
      try {
        await client.query(`SELECT pg_advisory_unlock(hashtextextended($1, 0))`, [key]);
      } catch {
        // The unlock failed, so this session may still hold the lock. Destroying
        // the client ends the session, and a session-scoped advisory lock dies
        // with it. Returning it to the pool instead would leak the lock for the
        // life of that pooled connection and wedge the account indefinitely —
        // the one outcome worse than failing this trade.
        connectionBroken = true;
      }
    }
    client.off('error', swallowClientError);
    client.release(connectionBroken);
  }
}

==> packages/db/src/execution-config.ts <==
import type { Chain, ExecutionConfig, ExecutionMode } from '@swat/shared';
import { parseExecutionMode, parseLiveEnabledChains } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { getActiveCertifiedChains } from './chain-certifications.js';

const EXECUTION_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_MS = 30_000;
const executionChains = new Set<Chain>(['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'base', 'ethereum', 'bsc']);
const executionConfigKeys = new Set(['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'base', 'ethereum', 'bsc', '*']);
const executionModes = new Set<ExecutionMode>(['off', 'paper', 'live', 'live+shadow']);
const failClosedConfig: ExecutionConfig = Object.freeze({
  solana: 'paper',
  polygon: 'paper',
  'robinhood-chain': 'paper',
  base: 'paper',
  ethereum: 'paper',
  bsc: 'paper'
});

interface ExecutionConfigSnapshot {
  config: ExecutionConfig | null;
  reason?: string;
}

interface CachedExecutionConfig {
  snapshot: ExecutionConfigSnapshot;
  timestamp: number;
}

let cachedConfig: CachedExecutionConfig | null = null;
let configLoad: { generation: number; promise: Promise<ExecutionConfigSnapshot> } | null = null;
let cacheGeneration = 0;

function parseDatabaseConfig(value: unknown): ExecutionConfigSnapshot {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {
    return {
      config: failClosedConfig,
      reason: 'Database execution configuration is invalid; fail-closed to paper'
    };
  }

  const entries = Object.entries(value);
  const isValid = entries.every(([key, mode]) => (
    executionConfigKeys.has(key)
      && typeof mode === 'string'
      && executionModes.has(mode as ExecutionMode)
      && (key !== '*' || mode === 'off')
  ));

  if (!isValid) {
    return {
      config: failClosedConfig,
      reason: 'Database execution configuration is invalid; fail-closed to paper'
    };
  }

  return { config: Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(entries)) as ExecutionConfig };
}

async function loadExecutionConfig(): Promise<ExecutionConfigSnapshot> {
  const rows = await query<{ value: unknown }>(
    `SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = 'execution_config'`
  );

  if (rows.length === 0) return { config: null };
  return parseDatabaseConfig(rows[0]?.value);
}

async function getExecutionConfigSnapshot(): Promise<ExecutionConfigSnapshot> {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (cachedConfig && now - cachedConfig.timestamp < EXECUTION_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_MS) {
    return cachedConfig.snapshot;
  }

  if (configLoad?.generation === cacheGeneration) return configLoad.promise;

  const generation = cacheGeneration;
  const promise = loadExecutionConfig().then((snapshot) => {
    if (generation === cacheGeneration) {
      cachedConfig = { snapshot, timestamp: Date.now() };
    }
    return snapshot;
  });
  configLoad = { generation, promise };

  try {
    return await promise;
  } finally {
    if (configLoad?.promise === promise) configLoad = null;
  }
}

/** Retrieves the validated execution configuration with a maximum 30-second TTL. */
export async function getExecutionConfig(): Promise<ExecutionConfig | null> {
  return (await getExecutionConfigSnapshot()).config;
}

export interface ChainModeResolution {
  requestedMode: ExecutionMode;
  effectiveMode: ExecutionMode;
  certified: boolean;
  reason?: string;
}

function requestedModeForChain(chain: Chain, dbConfig: ExecutionConfig | null): ExecutionMode {
  const dbMode = dbConfig?.[chain];
  if (dbMode !== undefined) return dbMode;

  const envKey = `TRADING_MODE_${chain.replace(/-/g, '_').toUpperCase()}`;
  const chainMode = process.env[envKey];
  if (chainMode !== undefined) return parseExecutionMode(chainMode);

  return parseExecutionMode(process.env.TRADING_MODE);
}

function resolveMode(
  chain: Chain,
  requestedMode: ExecutionMode,
  activeCertifications: readonly Chain[],
  globalOff: boolean,
  configReason?: string
): ChainModeResolution {
  const liveEnabledChains = parseLiveEnabledChains(process.env.LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS);
  const operatorEnabled = liveEnabledChains.includes(chain);
  const evidenceCertified = activeCertifications.includes(chain);
  const certified = operatorEnabled && evidenceCertified;

  if (globalOff) {
    return {
      requestedMode,
      effectiveMode: 'off',
      certified,
      reason: 'Global kill switch active (*)'
    };
  }

  if (configReason) {
    return {
      requestedMode: 'paper',
      effectiveMode: 'paper',
      certified,
      reason: configReason
    };
  }

  if (requestedMode === 'live' || requestedMode === 'live+shadow') {
    if (!operatorEnabled) {
      return {
        requestedMode,
        effectiveMode: 'paper',
        certified,
        reason: `Chain ${chain} is not enabled in LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS`
      };
    }
    if (!evidenceCertified) {
      return {
        requestedMode,
        effectiveMode: 'paper',
        certified,
        reason: `Chain ${chain} has no active reviewed certification record`
      };
    }
  }

  return { requestedMode, effectiveMode: requestedMode, certified };
}

/**
 * Resolves a consistent mode snapshot for multiple chains. One call shares the
 * same DB configuration and certification snapshot without storing a
 * process-global "current chain".
 */
export async function resolveChainModes<const Chains extends readonly Chain[]>(
  chains: Chains
): Promise<Record<Chains[number], ChainModeResolution>> {
  const [snapshot, activeCertifications] = await Promise.all([
    getExecutionConfigSnapshot(),
    getActiveCertifiedChains()
  ]);
  const globalOff = snapshot.config?.['*'] === 'off';
  const resolutions: Partial<Record<Chain, ChainModeResolution>> = {};

  for (const chain of chains) {
    const requestedMode = requestedModeForChain(chain, snapshot.config);
    resolutions[chain] = resolveMode(
      chain,
      requestedMode,
      activeCertifications,
      globalOff,
      snapshot.reason
    );
  }

  return resolutions as Record<Chains[number], ChainModeResolution>;
}

/** Resolves one chain using DB, chain env, legacy env, then paper precedence. */
export async function resolveChainMode(chain: Chain): Promise<ChainModeResolution> {
  return (await resolveChainModes([chain]))[chain];
}

/** Atomically changes one requested chain mode and invalidates this process's cache. */
export async function setChainExecutionMode(chain: Chain, mode: ExecutionMode): Promise<void> {
  if (!executionChains.has(chain) || !executionModes.has(mode)) {
    throw new Error('Invalid execution mode update');
  }

  await query(
    `INSERT INTO config (key, value)
     VALUES ('execution_config', jsonb_build_object($1::text, $2::text))
     ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET
       value = CASE
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(config.value) = 'object' THEN config.value
         ELSE '{}'::jsonb
       END || jsonb_build_object($1::text, $2::text),
       updated_at = NOW()`,
    [chain, mode]
  );
  clearExecutionConfigCache();
}

/** Replaces all requested modes with the atomic, fail-closed global switch. */
export async function activateAllChainEmergencyOff(): Promise<void> {
  await query(
    `INSERT INTO config (key, value)
     VALUES ('execution_config', jsonb_build_object($1::text, $2::text))
     ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET
       value = EXCLUDED.value,
       updated_at = NOW()`,
    ['*', 'off']
  );
  clearExecutionConfigCache();
}

/** Resets the in-memory cache for tests and successful hot mutations. */
export function clearExecutionConfigCache(): void {
  cacheGeneration += 1;
  cachedConfig = null;
  configLoad = null;
}

/**
 * Delegated-authority grants (`S4-7`, migration `047`).
 *
 * Two things are asserted here that a database cannot assert for us: that the
 * public read projection has no path to `sealed_secret`, and that the SQL text of
 * `047` still expresses the keyless invariant as a *set*. The constraint's
 * behaviour is covered by `tests/integration/user-execution.integration.test.ts`;
 * what this file guards is the shape of the statement, which is what decides
 * whether the next keyless venue fails loudly or quietly acquires a key.
 */

const SOLANA_VAULT = 'So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112';
const EVM_ACCOUNT = '0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678';
const scope = forUser('11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555');

/**
 * DDL statements in a migration that are not re-runnable.
 *
 * Comments are stripped first: the prose in these files talks about `CREATE`, and
 * `created_at` starts with the same six letters, so a line-anchored match on the
 * raw text finds statements that do not exist.
 */
function nonIdempotentStatements(sql: string): string[] {
  return sql
    .split(';')
    .map((statement) => statement.replace(/--[^\n]*/g, '').trim())
    .filter((statement) => /^(?:CREATE|ALTER|DROP)\s/i.test(statement))
    .filter((statement) => !/IF NOT EXISTS/i.test(statement))
    .map((statement) => statement.slice(0, 100));
}

function grantRow(overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
  return {
    id: 'grant-1',
    user_id: scope.userId,
    chain: 'solana',
    grant_kind: 'solana_vault',
    account_address: SOLANA_VAULT,
    has_sealed_secret: false,
    key_version: null,
    scope_policy: null,
    expires_at: null,
    revoked_at: null,
    status: 'active',
    created_at: new Date('2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
    ...overrides
  };
}

      expect(isKeylessGrantKind(kind)).toBe(false);

    expect(grantKindRequiresExpiry('session_key_4337')).toBe(true);
    expect(grantKindRequiresExpiry('solana_vault')).toBe(false);
    expect(grantKindRequiresExpiry('polymarket_signer')).toBe(false);

describe('assertGrantSecretMatchesKind', () => {
  it('accepts a keyless grant with neither secret nor version', () => {
    expect(() => assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({ grantKind: 'solana_vault' })).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('rejects a keyless grant carrying a secret', () => {
    expect(() =>
      assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({
        grantKind: 'solana_vault',
        sealedSecret: 'v1.env.abc',
        keyVersion: 1
      })
    ).toThrow(InvalidExecutionGrantError);
  });

  it('rejects a keyless grant carrying only a key version', () => {
    // The half-populated case is the one a rotation bug produces: it looks
    // harmless because no ciphertext is present, and it makes a keyless row claim
    // to be openable.
    expect(() =>
      assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({ grantKind: 'solana_vault', keyVersion: 2 })
    ).toThrow(/keyless/);
  });

  it.each(['eip7702', 'session_key_4337', 'polymarket_signer'] as GrantKind[])(
    'rejects %s with no secret',
    (grantKind) => {
      expect(() => assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({ grantKind })).toThrow(
        /requires a sealed secret/
      );
    }
  );

  it('rejects a keyed grant with a secret but no version', () => {
    expect(() =>
      assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({ grantKind: 'polymarket_signer', sealedSecret: 'v1.env.abc' })
    ).toThrow(/requires a sealed secret and a key version/);
  });

  it('rejects a secret that is not a versioned envelope', () => {
    expect(() =>
      assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({
        grantKind: 'polymarket_signer',
        sealedSecret: 'YmFzZTY0LW9ubHk=',
        keyVersion: 1
      })
    ).toThrow(/versioned envelope/);
  });

  it('accepts a versioned envelope', () => {
    expect(() =>
      assertGrantSecretMatchesKind({
        grantKind: 'polymarket_signer',
        sealedSecret: 'v1.env-local.Zm9vYmFy',
        keyVersion: 1
      })
    ).not.toThrow();
  });
});

describe('047 DDL contract', () => {
  let sql = '';

  beforeEach(async () => {
    sql = await readFile(
      resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../sql/047_user_execution_grants.sql'),
      'utf8'
    );
  });

  it('expresses the keyless invariant as a set, not as an equality on one kind', () => {
    // `grant_kind = 'solana_vault' … OR grant_kind <> 'solana_vault' …` would put a
    // *future* keyless kind in the keyed branch, silently requiring it to carry a
    // secret — the exact inversion of the invariant. The set form makes that
    // addition fail at insert time instead, and names the set once.
    expect(sql).toMatch(/grant_kind = ANY \(ARRAY\['solana_vault'\]\)/);
    expect(sql).not.toMatch(/grant_kind\s*<>\s*'solana_vault'/);
  });

  it('keeps the TypeScript keyless set and the SQL array in agreement', () => {
    const array = /grant_kind = ANY \(ARRAY\[([^\]]*)\]\)/.exec(sql)?.[1] ?? '';
    const kinds = array.split(',').map((entry) => entry.trim().replace(/^'|'$/g, ''));
    expect(kinds).toEqual([...KEYLESS_GRANT_KINDS]);
  });

  it('allows exactly the four documented grant kinds', () => {
    const kinds = /chk_ueg_kind CHECK \(grant_kind IN\s*([^)]*)\)/.exec(sql)?.[1] ?? '';
    expect(kinds.match(/'[a-z0-9_]+'/g)).toEqual([
      "'solana_vault'",
      "'eip7702'",
      "'session_key_4337'",
      "'polymarket_signer'"
    ]);
  });

  it('requires a versioned envelope and a key version on a keyed row', () => {
    expect(sql).toContain('sealed_secret IS NOT NULL');
    expect(sql).toContain('key_version IS NOT NULL');
    expect(sql).toContain("sealed_secret LIKE 'v%'");
  });

  it('requires an expiry on a session-shaped kind', () => {
    expect(sql).toMatch(
      /grant_kind NOT IN \('eip7702','session_key_4337'\)\s+OR expires_at IS NOT NULL/
    );
  });

  it('allows exactly the four documented statuses', () => {
    expect(sql).toContain("status IN ('active','retired','revoked','compromised')");
  });

  it('holds one execution account per chain globally', () => {
    expect(sql).toContain('CONSTRAINT uq_ueg_account UNIQUE (chain, account_address)');
  });

  it('indexes expires_at so the S4-P9 sweep does not scan the table', () => {
    expect(sql).toMatch(
      /CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ueg_expiring\s+ON user_execution_grants\(expires_at\)/
    );
  });

  it('permits exactly one active grant per user, chain and kind', () => {
    expect(sql).toMatch(
      /CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_ueg_active_per_user_chain_kind\s+ON user_execution_grants\(user_id, chain, grant_kind\)\s+WHERE status = 'active'/
    );
  });

  it('replays safely, because migrate.ts has no applied-migrations table', () => {
    // Every statement must be re-runnable: `migrate.ts` replays every file on
    // every invocation under an advisory lock, so one bare CREATE breaks
    // `pnpm db:migrate` for every developer on the second run.
    expect(nonIdempotentStatements(sql)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/execution-grants.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { resolveChainAddress } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { isCrossTenant, type UserScope } from './tenancy.js';

/**
 * Scoped delegated authority to trade on a user's behalf (`S4-7`, migration
 * `047`, ADR-0003).
 *
 * The shape this module protects: **a grant record read by the API never carries
 * the sealed secret.** `ExecutionGrant` has no field for it, so an API route
 * cannot leak one by serialising a row it fetched for another purpose — the
 * closest it can get is calling `loadSealedGrantSecret`, which is named to be
 * greppable and is only useful inside a process that holds a wrapper key.
 *
 * The keyless/keyed split is duplicated here and in
 * `chk_ueg_secret_matches_kind`, on purpose. The database constraint is the
 * guarantee; the check in `recordExecutionGrant` exists so that a caller bug
 * surfaces as a named error naming the kind, rather than as a 23514 whose text
 * mentions a constraint the caller has never heard of.
 */

export type GrantKind =
  | 'solana_vault'
  | 'eip7702'
  | 'session_key_4337'
  | 'polymarket_signer';

export type GrantStatus = 'active' | 'retired' | 'revoked' | 'compromised';

/**
 * Grant kinds that hold no secret, as a set — mirroring the SQL
 * `grant_kind = ANY (ARRAY['solana_vault'])`.
 *
 * A Solana vault is a PDA: there is no key, so there is nothing to seal. Adding a
 * second keyless venue means editing this array and the array in the migration's
 * CHECK, and nothing else.
 */
export const KEYLESS_GRANT_KINDS: readonly GrantKind[] = ['solana_vault'] as const;

export function isKeylessGrantKind(kind: GrantKind): boolean {
  return KEYLESS_GRANT_KINDS.includes(kind);
}

/** Kinds that are a time-boxed delegation rather than a standing key. */
const EXPIRING_GRANT_KINDS: readonly GrantKind[] = ['eip7702', 'session_key_4337'] as const;

export function grantKindRequiresExpiry(kind: GrantKind): boolean {
  return EXPIRING_GRANT_KINDS.includes(kind);
}

/**
 * A grant as the API and the fan-out path see it. **No `sealedSecret` field.**
 *
 * `keyVersion` is included because it is not secret and is what the wrapper
 * rotation sweep reports progress against.
 */
export interface ExecutionGrant {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly grantKind: GrantKind;
  readonly accountAddress: string;
  /** True when the row carries a sealed secret. The secret itself is not here. */
  readonly hasSealedSecret: boolean;
  readonly keyVersion: number | null;
  readonly scopePolicy: unknown | null;
  readonly expiresAt: Date | null;
  readonly revokedAt: Date | null;
  readonly status: GrantStatus;
  readonly createdAt: Date;
}

interface GrantRow {
  id: string;
  user_id: string;
  chain: Chain;
  grant_kind: GrantKind;
  account_address: string;
  has_sealed_secret: boolean;
  key_version: number | null;
  scope_policy: unknown | null;
  expires_at: Date | null;
  revoked_at: Date | null;
  status: GrantStatus;
  created_at: Date;
}

/**
 * The projection every public read uses.
 *
 * `sealed_secret IS NOT NULL AS has_sealed_secret` rather than `sealed_secret`:
 * the column is never selected by these queries at all, so it cannot reach a log
 * line, an error message, or a JSON response by accident.
 */
const GRANT_COLUMNS = `id, user_id, chain, grant_kind, account_address,
       sealed_secret IS NOT NULL AS has_sealed_secret,
       key_version, scope_policy, expires_at, revoked_at, status, created_at`;

function toGrant(row: GrantRow): ExecutionGrant {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    userId: row.user_id,
    chain: row.chain,
    grantKind: row.grant_kind,
    accountAddress: row.account_address,
    hasSealedSecret: row.has_sealed_secret,
    keyVersion: row.key_version,
    scopePolicy: row.scope_policy,
    expiresAt: row.expires_at,
    revokedAt: row.revoked_at,
    status: row.status,
    createdAt: row.created_at
  };
}

/**
 * The grant violates the keyless/keyed invariant, or a session grant has no
 * expiry.
 *
 * Distinct from a generic error so the API can map it to a 400 rather than a 500:
 * every case is a malformed request, not a server fault.
 */
export class InvalidExecutionGrantError extends Error {
  constructor(message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'InvalidExecutionGrantError';
  }
}

/** An active grant already exists for this (user, chain, kind). */
export class ExecutionGrantConflictError extends Error {
  constructor() {
    super('An active execution grant already exists for this chain and kind');
    this.name = 'ExecutionGrantConflictError';
  }
}

export interface RecordExecutionGrantInput {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly grantKind: GrantKind;
  /**
   * The settlement account. Stored unprefixed; normalised and validated by
   * `normalizeGrantAccountAddress`, so a mixed-case EVM address or a prefixed
   * `polygon:0x…` from a `copy_positions` join is accepted and written in the one
   * form the column holds.
   */
  readonly accountAddress: string;
  /** The `v1.<wrapperId>.…` envelope. Omit or pass null for a keyless kind. */
  readonly sealedSecret?: string | null;
  readonly keyVersion?: number | null;
  readonly scopePolicy?: unknown;
  readonly expiresAt?: Date | null;
}

/**
 * Validates the invariant the database also enforces, so the caller gets a
 * message naming the kind rather than a constraint violation.
 *
 * Exported for the API's request validation, which needs the same answer before
 * it has a database connection.
 */
export function assertGrantSecretMatchesKind(input: {
  grantKind: GrantKind;
  sealedSecret?: string | null;
  keyVersion?: number | null;
}): void {
  const keyless = isKeylessGrantKind(input.grantKind);
  const hasSecret = input.sealedSecret !== null && input.sealedSecret !== undefined;
  const hasVersion = input.keyVersion !== null && input.keyVersion !== undefined;

  if (keyless) {
    if (hasSecret || hasVersion) {
      throw new InvalidExecutionGrantError(
        `${input.grantKind} is keyless and must carry no sealed secret or key version`
      );
    }
    return;
  }

  if (!hasSecret || !hasVersion) {
    throw new InvalidExecutionGrantError(
      `${input.grantKind} requires a sealed secret and a key version`
    );
  }
  // Mirrors the `sealed_secret LIKE 'v%'` tripwire: reject anything that is not a
  // versioned envelope before it reaches the database, so the failure names the
  // format rather than the constraint.
  if (!/^v\d+\./.test(input.sealedSecret as string)) {
    throw new InvalidExecutionGrantError(
      'sealed secret must be a versioned envelope, e.g. v1.<wrapperId>.…'
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Normalises `account_address` to the form the column is documented to hold:
 * **unprefixed**, EVM lowercased, Solana case-preserved.
 *
 * `047` stores the account unprefixed because `chain` already carries the
 * discriminator, so the repo-wide `${chain}:${raw}` invariant does not apply to
 * this column — but the *normalisation* half of it still does, and without this
 * `uq_ueg_account` is defeated by case. `0xAbC…` and `0xabc…` are the same EVM
 * account and would occupy two rows, which is exactly the "two users' funds at one
 * address" failure that constraint exists to prevent.
 *
 * `resolveChainAddress` also validates the shape, so a truncated or malformed
 * address fails here rather than at the first signing attempt. It accepts an
 * already-prefixed value and strips the prefix, and throws when the prefix
 * disagrees with `chain` — so a caller that passes a prefixed address from a
 * `copy_positions` join gets the right answer instead of a `polygon:0x…` literal
 * in a column that must not carry one.
 */
export function normalizeGrantAccountAddress(chain: Chain, accountAddress: string): string {
  try {
    return resolveChainAddress(accountAddress, chain).raw;
  } catch (error) {
    throw new InvalidExecutionGrantError(
      `account_address is not a valid ${chain} address: ${(error as Error).message}`
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Inserts a grant.
 *
 * `user_id` comes from `scope`, never from the input — the input type has no
 * `userId` field, which is the point.
 */
export async function recordExecutionGrant(
  scope: UserScope,
  input: RecordExecutionGrantInput
): Promise<ExecutionGrant> {
  assertGrantSecretMatchesKind(input);
  if (grantKindRequiresExpiry(input.grantKind) && !input.expiresAt) {
    throw new InvalidExecutionGrantError(
      `${input.grantKind} requires expires_at — a scoped grant with no expiry is not scoped`
    );
  }
  const accountAddress = normalizeGrantAccountAddress(input.chain, input.accountAddress);

  try {
    const rows = await query<GrantRow>(
      `INSERT INTO user_execution_grants
         (user_id, chain, grant_kind, account_address, sealed_secret, key_version,
          scope_policy, expires_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
       RETURNING ${GRANT_COLUMNS}`,
      [
        scope.userId,
        input.chain,
        input.grantKind,
        accountAddress,
        input.sealedSecret ?? null,
        input.keyVersion ?? null,
        input.scopePolicy === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(input.scopePolicy),
        input.expiresAt ?? null
      ]
    );
    return toGrant(rows[0]!);
  } catch (error) {
    // 23505 is a unique violation. Both the partial active index and the global
    // account uniqueness land here; the caller's remedy is the same either way —
    // revoke the existing grant first.
    if ((error as { code?: string }).code === '23505') throw new ExecutionGrantConflictError();
    throw error;
  }
}

export async function listExecutionGrants(scope: UserScope): Promise<ExecutionGrant[]> {
  const rows = await query<GrantRow>(
    `SELECT ${GRANT_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_execution_grants
      WHERE user_id = $1
      ORDER BY created_at DESC`,
    [scope.userId]
  );
  return rows.map(toGrant);
}

/**
 * The one active grant for a (user, chain, kind), or null.
 *
 * Single-row by construction: `uq_ueg_active_per_user_chain_kind` is the
 * guarantee, so this does not need a `LIMIT` to be deterministic.
 */
export async function findActiveExecutionGrant(
  scope: UserScope,
  chain: Chain,
  grantKind: GrantKind
): Promise<ExecutionGrant | null> {
  const rows = await query<GrantRow>(
    `SELECT ${GRANT_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_execution_grants
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND chain = $2 AND grant_kind = $3 AND status = 'active'`,
    [scope.userId, chain, grantKind]
  );
  return rows[0] ? toGrant(rows[0]) : null;
}

/**
 * Reads the sealed envelope for one grant.
 *
 * **Only useful inside a process that holds a wrapper key**, which is
 * `trade-executor` and nothing else. Named separately from every other read so
 * that `grep -rn loadSealedGrantSecret` returns the complete list of places the
 * ciphertext is fetched, and any new occurrence is a security review item — the
 * same convention as `crossTenantScope`.
 *
 * Still scoped by `user_id`. The envelope's AAD binds the ciphertext to
 * `(userId, chainKind, keyVersion)`, so opening it under the wrong user fails on
 * the auth tag — but a query that could fetch another tenant's ciphertext at all
 * should not exist, whether or not the next step would fail.
 */
export async function loadSealedGrantSecret(
  scope: UserScope,
  grantId: string
): Promise<{ sealedSecret: string; keyVersion: number } | null> {
  const rows = await query<{ sealed_secret: string | null; key_version: number | null }>(
    `SELECT sealed_secret, key_version
       FROM user_execution_grants
      WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2`,
    [grantId, scope.userId]
  );
  const row = rows[0];
  if (!row || row.sealed_secret === null || row.key_version === null) return null;
  return { sealedSecret: row.sealed_secret, keyVersion: row.key_version };
}

/**
 * Marks a grant revoked.
 *
 * The row is kept, never deleted: it is the only record that this authority once
 * existed, and for a keyed kind it is the only thing that can still open a
 * secret protecting dust left at the account.
 */
export async function revokeExecutionGrant(
  scope: UserScope,
  grantId: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
    `UPDATE user_execution_grants
        SET status = 'revoked', revoked_at = NOW()
      WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status = 'active'
      RETURNING id`,
    [grantId, scope.userId]
  );
  return rows.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Marks a grant compromised. Terminal, and deliberately not reachable by the
 * ordinary revoke path: 'revoked' is a user decision and 'compromised' is an
 * incident, and conflating them loses the distinction in the audit trail.
 */
export async function markExecutionGrantCompromised(
  scope: UserScope,
  grantId: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
    `UPDATE user_execution_grants
        SET status = 'compromised', revoked_at = COALESCE(revoked_at, NOW())
      WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status <> 'compromised'
      RETURNING id`,
    [grantId, scope.userId]
  );
  return rows.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Active grants expiring at or before `before`. Drives the `S4-P9` re-consent
 * sweep, so it crosses tenants by design and requires a `crossTenantScope`.
 *
 * Served by the partial `idx_ueg_expiring`.
 */
export async function listExpiringExecutionGrants(
  scope: UserScope,
  before: Date,
  limit = 500
): Promise<ExecutionGrant[]> {
  if (!isCrossTenant(scope)) {
    throw new Error(
      'listExpiringExecutionGrants is a platform sweep; pass crossTenantScope(reason)'
    );
  }
  const rows = await query<GrantRow>(
    `SELECT ${GRANT_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_execution_grants
      WHERE status = 'active' AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at <= $1
      ORDER BY expires_at
      LIMIT $2`,
    [before, limit]
  );
  return rows.map(toGrant);
}

/**
 * Retires every active grant that has already lapsed.
 *
 * 'retired' rather than 'revoked': nobody revoked it, it simply ran out, and the
 * distinction is what tells an operator whether a user withdrew consent or just
 * stopped renewing.
 */
export async function retireLapsedExecutionGrants(scope: UserScope): Promise<number> {
  if (!isCrossTenant(scope)) {
    throw new Error(
      'retireLapsedExecutionGrants is a platform sweep; pass crossTenantScope(reason)'
    );
  }
  const rows = await query<{ id: string }>(
    `UPDATE user_execution_grants
        SET status = 'retired'
      WHERE status = 'active' AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at <= NOW()
      RETURNING id`
  );
  return rows.length;
}

==> packages/db/src/fanout-candidates.ts <==
import type { Chain, UserTier } from '@swat/shared';
import { USER_TIERS } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import type { FanoutCandidate } from './fanout-eligibility.js';
import { isCrossTenant, type UserScope } from './tenancy.js';
import {
  BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS,
  resolveKnownBalanceUsd,
  type BalanceSource,
  type UserBalance
} from './user-balances.js';
import { DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS } from './user-execution-settings.js';

/**
 * The fetch half of fan-out enumeration (`S4-13`, closing the open half of it).
 *
 * `fanout-eligibility.ts` decides *who copies a signal*; this produces the
 * `FanoutCandidate[]` it decides over. The split is the whole point and it runs
 * one way only: **this module fetches, `planFanout` decides.** A condition
 * expressed here as a WHERE clause cannot be unit-tested without Postgres, and
 * there is no Postgres available on this branch — so every rule that could
 * plausibly be either a filter or a verdict lives in the pure module, and what
 * remains here is scoping.
 *
 * Three filters do appear in the SQL, and each is a *scope*, not a decision:
 *
 *   1. `wallet_address = $1` — the signal's master wallet. That is the join
 *      ADR-0005 specified: single-master mirroring keys on the source wallet of
 *      a `source_trade` signal, never on cluster membership.
 *   2. `state <> 'ended'` — an ended subscription mirrors nothing and its rows
 *      are retained **forever** for attribution (`051`), so without the
 *      predicate every mirror would enumerate the accumulated history of
 *      everyone who ever left this master. `idx_uws_wallet_live` is the partial
 *      index built for exactly this predicate. It is also double-covered:
 *      `mirrorEligibilityForState('ended')` is `'none'`, so a leaked row would
 *      still be excluded with `subscription-not-mirroring` rather than copied.
 *      `winding_down` is deliberately **enumerated** — those users mirror sells,
 *      and dropping them strands their open positions with no exit.
 *   3. `users.status = 'active'` — see the note on `accountStatus` below. This
 *      one is **not** double-covered, and that is a gap worth knowing about.
 *
 * **Membership slots are deliberately not consulted.** A `winding_down` row
 * holds no `membership_slot` (migration `056`'s CHECK makes that
 * unrepresentable) and still has to be enumerated. Keying enumeration on the
 * slot instead of on the state is how a leaver's positions get stranded, so this
 * module never reads `membership_slot` — the same rule `master-membership.ts`
 * states from the other side.
 */

/**
 * Account status is filtered in SQL, and here is why that is unsatisfying.
 *
 * A suspended or soft-deleted account must not copy a trade. The API enforces
 * that at the session layer (`apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`), but a fan-out has
 * no session, so the enumeration has to. `FanoutExclusionCode` has no member for
 * it, so `planFanout` *cannot* report it — which means a suspended user
 * disappears from the fan-out instead of appearing with a reason. That is the
 * silent-filter shape this codebase avoids everywhere else.
 *
 * Filtering is still the lesser evil: the alternative is enumerating a suspended
 * account and letting it trade. Overloading `killed` to carry it was rejected —
 * `killed` is the per-user kill switch (`S6-8`), and reporting `user-killed` for
 * a suspended account sends an operator to check a switch that is off.
 *
 * The real fix is an `account-not-active` exclusion code in
 * `fanout-eligibility.ts`, which this module does not own.
 */

export interface ListFanoutCandidatesInput {
  /** The signal's master wallet, chain-prefixed (`solana:ABC...`). */
  readonly masterWalletAddress: string;
  /**
   * The signal's chain, used to scope the balance read.
   *
   * Balances are read **per chain**, not summed across chains, because
   * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` returns `null` if *any* row it is given is stale or
   * unpriced. Summed across chains, one stale Solana price would report every
   * user's Polymarket buying power as unknown and halt copying on a chain whose
   * own feed is healthy. Per chain, a feed outage is contained to the chain that
   * has it.
   */
  readonly chain: Chain;
  /** Injected so balance staleness is testable without waiting. */
  readonly now?: Date;
  /** Defaults to `BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS`; passed straight to `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`. */
  readonly balanceMaxAgeMs?: number;
}

interface CandidateRow {
  user_id: string;
  active_since: Date | null;
  /**
   * Typed `unknown` on purpose, matching `FanoutCandidate.subscriptionState`.
   *
   * The column can carry a value written by a future migration, a manual UPDATE,
   * or a service on another release. Narrowing it here would be a claim this
   * module cannot make; `mirrorEligibilityForState` is the only place that reads
   * it, and it fails closed.
   */
  subscription_state: unknown;
  tier: string;
  tier_expires_at: Date | null;
  /** `null` for every column below when the user has no settings row. */
  auto_execute: boolean | null;
  killed: boolean | null;
  min_signal_score: number | null;
  max_concurrent_positions: number | null;
  open_position_count: string;
}

interface BalanceRow {
  user_id: string;
  chain: Chain;
  asset: string;
  amount: number | string;
  decimals: number;
  usd: number | string | null;
  usd_priced_at: Date | null;
  fetched_at: Date;
  source: BalanceSource;
}

/**
 * `NUMERIC` arrives as a `number` when it fits a float64 without drift and as
 * the original text when it does not, per `configurePostgresNumericParsers`.
 *
 * Duplicated from `user-balances.ts` rather than imported because the function
 * there is module-private. The rule is identical and must stay so: re-parsing
 * the text half with `Number()` would reintroduce exactly the drift that parser
 * exists to prevent, so an unrepresentable value reads as `null` — unknown — and
 * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` then refuses the whole user rather than sizing
 * against a rounded figure.
 */
function toSafeNumber(value: number | string | null): number | null {
  if (value === null) return null;
  if (typeof value === 'number') return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null;
  return null;
}

function toBalance(row: BalanceRow): UserBalance {
  return {
    userId: row.user_id,
    chain: row.chain,
    asset: row.asset,
    amount: toSafeNumber(row.amount),
    amountRaw: String(row.amount),
    decimals: row.decimals,
    usd: toSafeNumber(row.usd),
    usdPricedAt: row.usd_priced_at,
    fetchedAt: row.fetched_at,
    source: row.source
  };
}

/**
 * An unrecognised tier reads as the **least** capable tier, not as a crash and
 * not as `ultra`.
 *
 * `capabilitiesFor` indexes `TIER_CAPABILITIES` directly, so an out-of-CHECK
 * value would produce `undefined` and throw inside `tierAllowsChain` — taking
 * the whole signal's fan-out down for one bad row. `'free'` is the same floor
 * `effectiveTier` already degrades an expired tier to, so this introduces no new
 * policy: it narrows to the smallest chain set rather than inventing one.
 */
function toTier(value: string): UserTier {
  return (USER_TIERS as readonly string[]).includes(value) ? (value as UserTier) : 'free';
}

/**
 * A count that cannot be read must not read as zero.
 *
 * `openPositionCount` is compared with `>=` against the user's cap, so a `NaN`
 * would make the comparison false and *admit* — failing toward opening a
 * position past the cap. Throwing fails the whole fan-out closed instead, which
 * is the correct direction for an unreadable count on a money path.
 */
function toOpenPositionCount(value: string, userId: string): number {
  const parsed = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed < 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `copy_positions open count for user ${userId} is not a non-negative integer: ${value}`
    );
  }
  return parsed;
}

/**
 * Every live subscriber of one master wallet, with the inputs `planFanout` needs.
 *
 * Cross-tenant by nature — it spans users on behalf of a background service — so
 * it takes a `crossTenantScope(reason)` and refuses a per-user scope, following
 * `listStaleUserBalances`. The refusal matters: called with a real user's scope
 * it would silently enumerate one subscriber and look like a working fan-out.
 *
 * Two round trips rather than one, deliberately. The balance total is produced by
 * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` in TypeScript because its rule — `null` on *any*
 * stale or unpriced row, never a partial sum — is a decision, and a `SUM()` in
 * SQL would either coalesce the unknowns away or need a hand-rolled staleness
 * predicate that no unit test could reach. One extra query is a cheap price for
 * keeping that rule in the one place it is already tested.
 */
export async function listFanoutCandidates(
  scope: UserScope,
  input: ListFanoutCandidatesInput
): Promise<FanoutCandidate[]> {
  if (!isCrossTenant(scope)) {
    throw new Error('listFanoutCandidates spans tenants; pass crossTenantScope(reason)');
  }

  const rows = await query<CandidateRow>(
    `SELECT
       subscription.user_id,
       subscription.active_since,
       subscription.state AS subscription_state,
       account.tier,
       account.tier_expires_at,
       settings.auto_execute,
       settings.killed,
       settings.min_signal_score,
       settings.max_concurrent_positions,
       (
         SELECT COUNT(*)::text
           FROM copy_positions position
          WHERE position.user_id = subscription.user_id
            AND position.confirmed_quantity > 0
       ) AS open_position_count
     FROM user_wallet_subscriptions subscription
     JOIN users account
       ON account.id = subscription.user_id
      AND account.status = 'active'
     LEFT JOIN user_execution_settings settings
       ON settings.user_id = subscription.user_id
     WHERE subscription.wallet_address = $1
       AND subscription.state <> 'ended'
     ORDER BY subscription.user_id`,
    [input.masterWalletAddress]
  );

  if (rows.length === 0) return [];

  const userIds = rows.map((row) => row.user_id);
  const balanceRows = await query<BalanceRow>(
    `SELECT user_id, chain, asset, amount, decimals, usd, usd_priced_at, fetched_at, source
       FROM user_balances
      WHERE chain = $1 AND user_id = ANY($2::uuid[])
      ORDER BY user_id, asset`,
    [input.chain, userIds]
  );

  const balancesByUser = new Map<string, UserBalance[]>();
  for (const row of balanceRows) {
    const balance = toBalance(row);
    const existing = balancesByUser.get(balance.userId);
    if (existing) existing.push(balance);
    else balancesByUser.set(balance.userId, [balance]);
  }

  const now = input.now ?? new Date();
  const maxAgeMs = input.balanceMaxAgeMs ?? BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS;

  return rows.map((row) => ({
    userId: row.user_id,
    activeSince: row.active_since,
    subscriptionState: row.subscription_state,
    tier: toTier(row.tier),
    tierExpiresAt: row.tier_expires_at,
    // A missing settings row is defaults, not "opted out" — see
    // `DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS`. The join is therefore an outer one: an
    // inner join would drop the user entirely and `planFanout` would report no
    // exclusion at all, which is indistinguishable from "not subscribed". With
    // the defaults the same user appears and is excluded as `auto-execute-off`,
    // which is the true reason (nothing creates the row at signup, so
    // auto-execute is off until the user turns it on — D13).
    autoExecute: row.auto_execute ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.autoExecute,
    killed: row.killed ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.killed,
    minSignalScore: row.min_signal_score ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.minSignalScore,
    maxConcurrentPositions:
      row.max_concurrent_positions ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.maxConcurrentPositions,
    openPositionCount: toOpenPositionCount(row.open_position_count, row.user_id),
    // Passed straight through, `null` included. A user with no balance row on
    // this chain gets `null` from `resolveKnownBalanceUsd([])` — unknown, not
    // zero — and is excluded as `balance-unknown`. Coalescing to 0 here would
    // report `balance-below-minimum` instead, which reads as "this user is
    // broke" when the truth is "we never priced them".
    knownBalanceUsd: resolveKnownBalanceUsd(
      balancesByUser.get(row.user_id) ?? [],
      now,
      maxAgeMs
    )
  }));
}

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

/**
 * `./subscriptions.js` -- where `mirrorEligibilityForState` lives, and using the
 * real one is the point, since it is the single definition of what each state
 * permits -- statically imports `./client.js`, which throws
 * `DATABASE_URL is required` while being evaluated. Hoisted so it runs before

  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??= 'postgres://swat:swat@127.0.0.1:5432/swat_unit_tests';

import { capabilitiesFor, tierAllowsChain } from '@swat/shared';

  assessFanoutCandidate,

  score: 90,
  eventAt: new Date('2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z')

const candidate: FanoutCandidate = {
  userId: 'u1',
  activeSince: new Date('2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
  subscriptionState: 'active',
  tier: 'ultra',
  tierExpiresAt: null,

  killed: false,
  minSignalScore: 70,
