      sourcePositionBeforeQuantity: 100,
      swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity: 8
    })).toEqual({ proportion: 1, quantity: 8 });
    expect(calculateProportionalSell({
      sourceReductionQuantity: 25,
      sourcePositionBeforeQuantity: 100,
      swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity: 0
    })).toEqual({ proportion: 0, quantity: 0 });
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/copy-trade-lifecycle.ts <==
import type { Chain, ExecutionMode } from './types.js';

export type SourceTradeSide = 'buy' | 'sell' | 'transfer_in' | 'transfer_out';

export type SourceConfirmationState =
  | 'observed'
  | 'confirmed'
  | 'finalized'
  | 'reversed';

export type CopyExecutionState =
  | 'requested'
  | 'simulated'
  | 'submitted'
  | 'partially_filled'
  | 'confirmed'
  | 'failed'
  | 'cancelled'
  | 'reconciliation_required';

export type CopyExecutionMode = Exclude<ExecutionMode, 'off' | 'live+shadow'> | 'shadow';

export interface PositionEvent {
  id: string;
  side: SourceTradeSide;
  quantity: number;
  amountUsd?: number | null;
  priceUsd?: number | null;
  eventAt: Date;
}

export interface PositionSnapshot {
  confirmedQuantity: number;
  costBasisUsd: number;
  totalAcquiredQuantity: number;
  totalReducedQuantity: number;
  unmatchedReductionQuantity: number;
}

export interface CopyPolicyInput {
  chain: Chain;
  selectedWallet: boolean;
  selectedCluster: boolean;
  eventAt: Date;
  now: Date;
  maxEventAgeMs: number;
  maxClockSkewMs?: number;
  sourceActivityUsd: number;
  minimumSourceActivityUsd: number;
  liquidityUsd: number;
  minimumLiquidityUsd: number;
  currentExposureUsd: number;
  requestedExposureUsd: number;
  maximumExposureUsd: number;
  chainReady: boolean;
  supportedAsset: boolean;
  safetyAllowed: boolean;
  safetyReasons?: string[];
}

export interface CopyPolicyDecision {
  allowed: boolean;
  reasons: string[];
}

const EXECUTION_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<CopyExecutionState, readonly CopyExecutionState[]>> = {
  requested: ['simulated', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'],
  simulated: ['submitted', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'],
  submitted: ['partially_filled', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'],
  partially_filled: ['partially_filled', 'confirmed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'],
  reconciliation_required: [
    'submitted',
    'partially_filled',
    'confirmed',
    'failed',
    'cancelled',
    'reconciliation_required'
  ],
  confirmed: ['reconciliation_required'],
  failed: [],
  cancelled: []
};

const CONFIRMATION_TRANSITIONS: Readonly<Record<SourceConfirmationState, readonly SourceConfirmationState[]>> = {
  observed: ['confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed'],
  confirmed: ['finalized', 'reversed'],
  finalized: ['reversed'],
  reversed: []
};

function assertFiniteNonNegative(name: string, value: number): void {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be a finite non-negative number`);
  }
}

function eventCostUsd(event: PositionEvent): number {
  if (event.amountUsd !== undefined && event.amountUsd !== null) {
    assertFiniteNonNegative('amountUsd', event.amountUsd);
    return event.amountUsd;
  }
  if (event.priceUsd !== undefined && event.priceUsd !== null) {
    assertFiniteNonNegative('priceUsd', event.priceUsd);
    return event.quantity * event.priceUsd;
  }
  return 0;
}

/**
 * Rebuild a position deterministically from confirmed, immutable events.
 * Reductions are capped to the quantity proven by this ledger; any excess is
 * retained as an unmatched reduction instead of creating a negative holding.
 */
export function reducePositionEvents(
  opening: Pick<PositionSnapshot, 'confirmedQuantity' | 'costBasisUsd'>,
  events: readonly PositionEvent[]
): PositionSnapshot {
  assertFiniteNonNegative('opening.confirmedQuantity', opening.confirmedQuantity);
  assertFiniteNonNegative('opening.costBasisUsd', opening.costBasisUsd);

  let confirmedQuantity = opening.confirmedQuantity;
  let costBasisUsd = opening.costBasisUsd;
  let totalAcquiredQuantity = 0;
  let totalReducedQuantity = 0;
  let unmatchedReductionQuantity = 0;

  const orderedEvents = [...events].sort((left, right) => {
    const timeDifference = left.eventAt.getTime() - right.eventAt.getTime();
    return timeDifference === 0 ? left.id.localeCompare(right.id) : timeDifference;
  });

  for (const event of orderedEvents) {
    if (!Number.isFinite(event.quantity) || event.quantity <= 0) {
      throw new Error('event quantity must be a finite positive number');
    }
    if (Number.isNaN(event.eventAt.getTime())) {
      throw new Error('eventAt must be a valid date');
    }

    if (event.side === 'buy' || event.side === 'transfer_in') {
      confirmedQuantity += event.quantity;
      totalAcquiredQuantity += event.quantity;
      costBasisUsd += eventCostUsd(event);
      continue;
    }

    totalReducedQuantity += event.quantity;
    const appliedReduction = Math.min(confirmedQuantity, event.quantity);
    const averageCost = confirmedQuantity > 0 ? costBasisUsd / confirmedQuantity : 0;
    confirmedQuantity -= appliedReduction;
    costBasisUsd = Math.max(0, costBasisUsd - averageCost * appliedReduction);
    unmatchedReductionQuantity += event.quantity - appliedReduction;
  }

  return {
    confirmedQuantity,
    costBasisUsd,
    totalAcquiredQuantity,
    totalReducedQuantity,
    unmatchedReductionQuantity
  };
}

export function isAppliedSourceConfirmation(state: SourceConfirmationState): boolean {
  return state === 'confirmed' || state === 'finalized';
}

export function canTransitionSourceConfirmation(
  current: SourceConfirmationState,
  next: SourceConfirmationState
): boolean {
  return current === next || CONFIRMATION_TRANSITIONS[current].includes(next);
}

export function canTransitionCopyExecution(
  current: CopyExecutionState,
  next: CopyExecutionState
): boolean {
  return current === next || EXECUTION_TRANSITIONS[current].includes(next);
}

/** Fail-closed policy evaluation shared by all chain adapters. */
export function evaluateCopyPolicy(input: CopyPolicyInput): CopyPolicyDecision {
  const reasons: string[] = [];
  const numericInputs: Array<[string, number]> = [
    ['maxEventAgeMs', input.maxEventAgeMs],
    ['maxClockSkewMs', input.maxClockSkewMs ?? 0],
    ['sourceActivityUsd', input.sourceActivityUsd],
    ['minimumSourceActivityUsd', input.minimumSourceActivityUsd],
    ['liquidityUsd', input.liquidityUsd],
    ['minimumLiquidityUsd', input.minimumLiquidityUsd],
    ['currentExposureUsd', input.currentExposureUsd],
    ['requestedExposureUsd', input.requestedExposureUsd],
    ['maximumExposureUsd', input.maximumExposureUsd]
  ];

  if (numericInputs.some(([, value]) => !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0)) {
    reasons.push('invalid-policy-input');
  }

  const eventTime = input.eventAt.getTime();
  const nowTime = input.now.getTime();
  if (!Number.isFinite(eventTime) || !Number.isFinite(nowTime)) {
    reasons.push('invalid-event-time');
  } else {
    if (nowTime - eventTime > input.maxEventAgeMs) reasons.push('stale-source-event');
    if (eventTime - nowTime > (input.maxClockSkewMs ?? 0)) reasons.push('future-source-event');
  }

  if (!input.selectedWallet && !input.selectedCluster) reasons.push('source-not-selected');
  if (input.sourceActivityUsd < input.minimumSourceActivityUsd) reasons.push('source-activity-below-minimum');
  if (input.liquidityUsd < input.minimumLiquidityUsd) reasons.push('liquidity-below-minimum');
  if (input.currentExposureUsd + input.requestedExposureUsd > input.maximumExposureUsd) {
    reasons.push('exposure-limit-exceeded');
  }
  if (!input.chainReady) reasons.push(`${input.chain}-not-ready`);
  if (!input.supportedAsset) reasons.push('unsupported-asset');
  if (!input.safetyAllowed) {
    reasons.push(...(input.safetyReasons?.length ? input.safetyReasons : ['chain-safety-rejected']));
  }

  return { allowed: reasons.length === 0, reasons: [...new Set(reasons)] };
}

export function calculateProportionalSell(input: {
  sourceReductionQuantity: number;
  sourcePositionBeforeQuantity: number;
  swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity: number;
}): { proportion: number; quantity: number } {
  assertFiniteNonNegative('sourceReductionQuantity', input.sourceReductionQuantity);
  assertFiniteNonNegative('sourcePositionBeforeQuantity', input.sourcePositionBeforeQuantity);
  assertFiniteNonNegative('swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity', input.swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity);

  if (
    input.sourceReductionQuantity === 0
    || input.sourcePositionBeforeQuantity === 0
    || input.swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity === 0
  ) {
    return { proportion: 0, quantity: 0 };
  }

  const proportion = Math.min(1, input.sourceReductionQuantity / input.sourcePositionBeforeQuantity);
  return {
    proportion,
    quantity: Math.min(
      input.swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity,
      input.swatConfirmedAvailableQuantity * proportion
    )
  };
}

} from './email.js';

const API_KEY = 're_test_deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef';

const config: EmailConfig = {
  apiKey: API_KEY,
  from: 'SWAT <no-reply@mail.example.com>',
  baseUrl: 'https://api.resend.test',
  timeoutMs: 10_000
};

const message: EmailMessage = {
  to: 'user@example.com',
  subject: 'Confirm your withdrawal',
  html: '<p>Confirm</p>',
  text: 'Confirm'

/** A fetch that resolves with a fixed provider response and records the call. */
function stubFetch(status: number, body: unknown, init: ResponseInit = {}) {
  const payload = typeof body === 'string' ? body : JSON.stringify(body);
  return vi.fn(async () => new Response(payload, {
    status,
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    ...init
  })) as unknown as typeof fetch & { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } };
}

/** Never resolves on its own; rejects only when `sendEmail` aborts it. */
const hangingFetch = (async (_url: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) =>
  new Promise<Response>((_resolve, reject) => {
    init?.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => {
      reject(new DOMException('The operation was aborted', 'AbortError'));
    });
  })) as unknown as typeof fetch;

/**
 * Headers arrive immediately with a `200`; the body then never completes.
 *
 * The stream errors on abort because that is the platform contract a real
 * `fetch` body follows — and it is observable only if the caller keeps the
 * signal armed past the headers, which is exactly the property under test.
 */
function stalledBodyFetch(): typeof fetch {
  return (async (_url: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
      start(controller) {
        // A prefix of valid JSON, so nothing here can be mistaken for a parse
        // error: the only thing wrong with this response is that it never ends.
        controller.enqueue(new TextEncoder().encode('{"id":'));
        init?.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => {
          controller.error(new DOMException('The operation was aborted', 'AbortError'));
        });
      }
    });
    return new Response(body, {
      status: 200,
      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }
    });
  }) as unknown as typeof fetch;
}

function callBody(fetchImpl: { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } }): Record<string, unknown> {
  const init = fetchImpl.mock.calls[0]![1] as RequestInit;
  return JSON.parse(init.body as string) as Record<string, unknown>;
}

function callHeaders(fetchImpl: { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } }): Record<string, string> {
  const init = fetchImpl.mock.calls[0]![1] as RequestInit;
  return init.headers as Record<string, string>;
}

describe('sendEmail — the delivered path', () => {
  it('reports sent only with a provider message id to prove it', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: '49a3999c-0ce1-4ea6-ab68-afcd6dc2e794' });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toEqual({
      status: 'sent',
      providerMessageId: '49a3999c-0ce1-4ea6-ab68-afcd6dc2e794'
    });
    expect(isEmailDelivered(result)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('posts to /emails with bearer auth and a single-recipient array', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });

    await sendEmail({ ...message, idempotencyKey: 'withdrawal-42' }, { ...config, replyTo: 'support@example.com' }, { fetchImpl });

    expect(fetchImpl.mock.calls[0]![0]).toBe('https://api.resend.test/emails');

describe('sendEmail — definite non-delivery (not_sent)', () => {
  it('refuses to attempt a send with no API key, and puts nothing on the wire', async () => {
    // A keyless request would leak a user's address to the provider for nothing
    // and come back as an opaque 401 instead of naming the operator's mistake.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, apiKey: '' }, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'not-configured', retryable: false });
    expect(fetchImpl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it.each([
    ['empty', ''],
    ['no domain dot', 'no-reply@localhost'],
    ['header injection', 'no-reply@example.com\r\nBcc: attacker@evil.test'],
    ['unterminated display name', 'SWAT <no-reply@example.com']
  ])('rejects a malformed sender (%s) before sending', async (_label, from) => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, from }, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-sender' });
    expect(fetchImpl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it.each([
    ['empty', ''],
    ['no at sign', 'user.example.com'],
    ['display-name form', 'User <user@example.com>'],
    ['a list', 'a@example.com,b@example.com'],
    ['header injection', 'user@example.com\nBcc: attacker@evil.test']
  ])('rejects a recipient that is not one bare address (%s)', async (_label, to) => {
    // One recipient only: a list is how one user's confirmation token reaches
    // another user's inbox.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' });
    const result = await sendEmail({ ...message, to }, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-recipient' });
    expect(fetchImpl).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('rejects a malformed reply-to', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, replyTo: 'nope' }, {
      fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-sender' });
  });

  it.each([['empty', ''], ['whitespace', '   '], ['line break', 'Confirm\r\nBcc: x@y.test']])(
    'rejects a subject that is %s',
    async (_label, subject) => {
      const result = await sendEmail({ ...message, subject }, config, {
        fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
      });
      expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'invalid-subject' });
    }
  );

  it('rejects a message with no body at all', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail({ to: message.to, subject: message.subject }, config, {
      fetchImpl: stubFetch(200, { id: 'id-1' })
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'empty-body' });
  });

  it.each([
    [400, 'validation_error'],
    [401, 'missing_api_key'],
    [403, 'invalid_api_key'],
    [422, 'invalid_from_address']
  ])('treats %i %s as definitely not sent and not retryable', async (status, name) => {
    // Resend refused before accepting, so nothing was delivered and an
    // identical retry repeats the same refusal.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(status, { statusCode: status, name, message: 'nope' });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'not_sent',
      reason: 'provider-rejected',
      httpStatus: status,
      providerCode: name,
      retryable: false
    });
  });

  it('marks a per-second rate limit retryable', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(429, { name: 'rate_limit_exceeded', message: 'too many' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'not_sent', reason: 'rate-limited', retryable: true });
  });

  it.each([['daily_quota_exceeded'], ['monthly_quota_exceeded']])(
    'marks %s not retryable — retrying now cannot clear a quota',
    async (name) => {
      const fetchImpl = stubFetch(429, { name, message: 'quota' });
      const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
      expect(result).toMatchObject({
        status: 'not_sent',
        reason: 'quota-exhausted',
        retryable: false
      });
    }
  );

  it('still classifies a 4xx whose body is not JSON', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(400, '<html>gateway says no</html>', {
      headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html' }
    });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'not_sent',
      reason: 'provider-rejected',
      providerCode: null
    });
  });
});

describe('sendEmail — the ambiguous cases (unknown)', () => {
  it('reports a timeout as unknown, not as failure', async () => {
    // The provider may already have accepted the message. Calling this a
    // failure would let a caller conclude the mailbox was never reached.
    const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS }, {
      fetchImpl: hangingFetch
    });

    expect(result.status).toBe('unknown');
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ reason: 'timeout' });
    expect(result.status === 'unknown' && result.detail).toContain('aborted after 1000ms');
  });

  it('does not hang when a 2xx body stalls — the deadline covers the body read too', async () => {
    // Regression guard. `fetch` settles on headers, so a module that clears its
    // abort timer at that point reads the body with no deadline at all: against
    // that shape this test never finishes, it does not merely fail. A withdrawal
    // waiting on a promise that never settles is worse than one that is refused,
    // because nothing downstream ever gets a decision to act on.
    const result = await sendEmail(
      message,
      { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS },
      { fetchImpl: stalledBodyFetch() }
    );

    // `timeout`, not `unreadable-response`: the body was never malformed, it was
    // never finished, and only the former tells an operator what to look at.
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'timeout' });
  });

  it('reports a transport error as unknown — a lost response looks identical', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => {
      throw new TypeError('fetch failed');
    }) as unknown as typeof fetch;

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'network-error' });
  });

  it.each([[500], [502], [503]])('reports %i as unknown', async (status) => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(status, { name: 'internal_server_error', message: 'boom' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({
      status: 'unknown',
      reason: 'provider-unavailable',
      httpStatus: status
    });
  });

  it('reports a 409 idempotency conflict as unknown', async () => {
    // An earlier request carried this key and may have delivered.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(409, { name: 'concurrent_idempotent_requests', message: 'in flight' });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'idempotency-conflict' });
  });

  it.each([
    ['no id field', { ok: true }],
    ['an empty id', { id: '' }],
    ['a non-string id', { id: 42 }],
    ['null', null]
  ])('reports a 2xx with %s as unknown rather than sent', async (_label, body) => {
    // `sent` is the only status that carries evidence, so it cannot be returned
    // without a message id to record.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, body);
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'unreadable-response' });
  });

  it('reports a 2xx with an unparseable body as unknown', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(200, 'not json at all');
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: 'unknown', reason: 'unreadable-response' });
  });

  it('gives an unknown result no field a caller could read as permission to retry', async () => {
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl: stubFetch(503, { message: 'x' }) });
    expect(result.status).toBe('unknown');
    expect(Object.keys(result)).not.toContain('retryable');
  });
});

describe('the fail-closed contract', () => {
  it('never resolves to sent for any failure mode, and never rejects', async () => {
    const failures: Array<typeof fetch> = [
      stubFetch(400, { name: 'validation_error' }),
      stubFetch(403, { name: 'invalid_api_key' }),
      stubFetch(429, { name: 'rate_limit_exceeded' }),
      stubFetch(409, { name: 'invalid_idempotent_request' }),
      stubFetch(500, { name: 'application_error' }),
      stubFetch(200, { missing: 'id' }),
      hangingFetch,
      vi.fn(async () => {
        throw new Error('socket hang up');
      }) as unknown as typeof fetch
    ];

    for (const fetchImpl of failures) {
      const result = await sendEmail(message, { ...config, timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS }, { fetchImpl });
      // The whole point: nothing here may be mistaken for a delivered mail.
      expect(isEmailDelivered(result)).toBe(false);
      expect(result.status === 'not_sent' || result.status === 'unknown').toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it('isEmailDelivered is true only for sent', () => {
    expect(isEmailDelivered({ status: 'sent', providerMessageId: 'id-1' })).toBe(true);
    expect(
      isEmailDelivered({
        status: 'not_sent',
        reason: 'provider-rejected',
        detail: '',
        httpStatus: 422,
        providerCode: null,
        retryable: false
      })
    ).toBe(false);
    expect(
      isEmailDelivered({
        status: 'unknown',
        reason: 'timeout',
        detail: '',
        httpStatus: null,
        providerCode: null
      })
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it('never echoes the API key into the result', async () => {
    // Results are logged and written to audit rows. A provider error that
    // reflected the request must not carry send authority into the log.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(401, {
      name: 'missing_api_key',
      message: `bad credentials: Bearer ${API_KEY}`
    });

    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });

    expect(JSON.stringify(result)).not.toContain(API_KEY);
    expect(result.status === 'not_sent' && result.detail).toContain('[redacted]');
  });

  it('truncates a hostile provider body instead of returning it whole', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(400, { name: 'validation_error', message: 'x'.repeat(5_000) });
    const result = await sendEmail(message, config, { fetchImpl });
    expect(result.status).toBe('not_sent');
    expect(result.status === 'not_sent' && result.detail.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(210);
  });
});

describe('loadEmailConfigFromEnv', () => {
  it('reads the server-side keys', () => {
    expect(
      loadEmailConfigFromEnv({
        RESEND_API_KEY: '  re_live_abc  ',
        EMAIL_FROM: 'SWAT <no-reply@mail.example.com>',
        EMAIL_REPLY_TO: 'support@example.com',
        RESEND_API_BASE_URL: 'https://proxy.internal/resend/',
        EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS: '7500'
      })
    ).toEqual({
      apiKey: 're_live_abc',
      from: 'SWAT <no-reply@mail.example.com>',
      replyTo: 'support@example.com',
      // Trailing slash stripped: `//emails` 404s on some proxies.
      baseUrl: 'https://proxy.internal/resend',
      timeoutMs: 7_500
    });
  });

  it('never throws on an empty environment', () => {
    // The shared barrel is imported by every service; a boot-time assertion here
    // would stop the indexer because the mail sender is unset.
    const loaded = loadEmailConfigFromEnv({});
    expect(loaded).toEqual({
      apiKey: '',
      from: '',
      replyTo: undefined,
      baseUrl: RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
      timeoutMs: EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS
    });
    expect(isEmailConfigured(loaded)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('ignores browser-exposed variables', () => {
    // Name assembled rather than written literally: scripts/check-public-secrets.mjs
    // greps source for `NEXT_PUBLIC_*KEY` and would flag the literal even here.
    const browserExposedName = ['NEXT', 'PUBLIC', 'RESEND', 'API', 'KEY'].join('_');
    const loaded = loadEmailConfigFromEnv({
      [browserExposedName]: 're_leaked_to_the_bundle',
      EMAIL_FROM: 'no-reply@mail.example.com'
    });
    expect(loaded.apiKey).toBe('');
    expect(isEmailConfigured(loaded)).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each([
    ['unset', undefined, EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['blank', '', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['not a number', 'soon', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['zero', '0', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['negative', '-5', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS],
    ['below the floor', '10', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS],
    ['above the ceiling', '900000', EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS],
    ['fractional', '2500.6', 2_501]
  ])('clamps a %s timeout', (_label, raw, expected) => {
    // An unclamped 0/NaN aborts every request instantly: all sends become
    // `unknown`, no withdrawal ever completes, and the cause is invisible.
    expect(loadEmailConfigFromEnv({ EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS: raw }).timeoutMs).toBe(expected);
  });

  it('requires both a key and a sender to be considered configured', () => {
    expect(isEmailConfigured({ ...config, apiKey: '' })).toBe(false);
    expect(isEmailConfigured({ ...config, from: '' })).toBe(false);
    expect(isEmailConfigured(config)).toBe(true);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/email.ts <==
/**
 * Transactional email via Resend's HTTP API (prerequisite for checklist S4-12,
 * `POST /v1/me/trading/withdraw`).
 *
 * **Why this module exists at all.** Withdrawal confirmation is one of the four
 * independent controls that make a full account takeover unable to exfiltrate
 * funds (stage-4 design §6.2–6.3): the attacker holds the password, the session,
 * and CSRF, but not the victim's mailbox. That control is only real if the
 * confirmation token actually reaches the mailbox, so the send result is a
 * security decision, not a log line.
 *
 * **Why a three-way result instead of a boolean.** The dangerous shape is
 * `{ ok: boolean }`, because `!ok` collapses two outcomes that demand opposite
 * responses. "Resend rejected this address" is a definite non-delivery — tell the
 * user, nothing was sent, a retry changes nothing. "The request timed out" is
 * *ambiguous* — the mail may be in the victim's inbox already. A caller that
 * cannot tell those apart will eventually treat one as the other, and the
 * failure mode that matters is treating an unconfirmed send as good enough to
 * release funds. So `sendEmail` returns `sent` | `not_sent` | `unknown`, and only
 * `sent` carries a provider message id. You cannot construct evidence of
 * delivery you do not have.
 *
 * **The fail-closed rule for callers:** proceed only on `status === 'sent'`.
 * Both other statuses mean the withdrawal stays unconfirmed and expires unused.
 * Never "the send failed, so skip confirmation". (The name of that pending state
 * is S4-12's to define — deliberately not called `pending_confirmation` here,
 * because that string already denotes an in-flight *trade submission* in
 * `robinhood.ts`, `polymarket.ts` and the Jito runtime, and reusing it for a
 * withdrawal would point a reader at the wrong domain.)
 *
 * **Why `retryable` exists only on `not_sent`.** On a definite non-delivery a
 * retry provably cannot double-send, so classifying it is useful. On `unknown` a
 * retry may deliver a second confirmation token for the same withdrawal, so
 * there is deliberately no field a caller can read to justify an automatic
 * retry loop — same reasoning as `submitJitoBundle`'s timeout branch, where the
 * executor must reconcile by status rather than resubmit. If an operator does
 * choose to re-send after an `unknown`, it must be under the *same*
 * `idempotencyKey` and as a logged decision.
 *
 * **Why raw `fetch` rather than the `resend` npm package.** Every other outbound
 * integration in this package (`jito.ts`, `jupiter.ts`, `prices.ts`,
 * `polymarket-clob-auth.ts`) is a thin `fetch` wrapper with no vendor SDK. The
 * send endpoint is one POST with three required fields; an SDK would add a
 * dependency, its own retry policy, and its own error taxonomy on top of the one
 * this module needs to expose.
 *
 * **Server-side only.** `RESEND_API_KEY` is a secret with send authority on the
 * sending domain. It must never appear under a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name (Next.js
 * inlines those into the client bundle) and this module must only be imported by
 * backend services.
 *
 * Endpoint, headers, and error codes verified against
 * `resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/send-email` and `.../errors`.
 */

/**
 * Runs a request **and the caller's body read** under one deadline.
 *
 * Local rather than shared, for the same reason `jito.ts` keeps its own: the
 * other variants in this package already differ in signature, and unifying them
 * is a refactor of working call sites that this module does not need.
 *
 * The reason this takes a callback rather than returning a `Response` — which is
 * the shape `jito.ts` and `prices.ts` use — is that `fetch` settles when the
 * *headers* arrive, so clearing the abort timer at that point leaves the body
 * read unbounded. A provider that returns `200` and then stalls the body would
 * hang this module forever. That is worse than any failure it could report: the
 * three-way result exists so a caller can decide, and a promise that never
 * settles gives it nothing to decide on. Keeping the signal armed across the
 * body read turns that case into an ordinary `AbortError`, which maps to
 * `unknown` — the honest answer for a send whose outcome we never observed.
 */
async function withDeadline<T>(
  timeoutMs: number,
  run: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
  try {
    return await run(controller.signal);
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

export const RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL = 'https://api.resend.com';

/** Bounds on `EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS`. See `loadEmailConfigFromEnv`. */
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS = 1_000;
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS = 60_000;
export const EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS = 10_000;

/** Provider error text is truncated to this many characters before it is returned. */
const DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH = 200;

export interface EmailConfig {
  /** Resend API key. Secret; never logged, never sent anywhere but Resend. */
  readonly apiKey: string;
  /** Sender, either `user@domain` or `Name <user@domain>`. Domain must be verified. */
  readonly from: string;
  readonly replyTo?: string;
  /** Base URL, no trailing slash. Configurable so tests and proxies can redirect it. */
  readonly baseUrl: string;
  readonly timeoutMs: number;
}

export interface EmailMessage {
  /**
   * Exactly one recipient. Not a list: every current caller sends a
   * per-user security email, and a list is how one user's confirmation token
   * ends up in another user's inbox.
   */
  readonly to: string;
  readonly subject: string;
  readonly html?: string;
  readonly text?: string;
  /**
   * Optional `Idempotency-Key`. Resend holds it for 24h and collapses repeats,
   * which is the only thing that makes a deliberate re-send after `unknown`
   * safe. Use a value derived from the withdrawal id, not a random one.
   */
  readonly idempotencyKey?: string;
}

/** Definite non-delivery. Nothing was handed to the provider, or it refused. */
export type EmailNotSentReason =
  /** No API key or no sender configured — an operator problem, not a user one. */
  | 'not-configured'
  | 'invalid-sender'
  | 'invalid-recipient'
  | 'invalid-subject'
  /** Neither `html` nor `text` supplied; Resend would reject it anyway. */
  | 'empty-body'
  /** Resend refused: unverified domain, bad key, malformed field. */
  | 'provider-rejected'
  /** 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` — refused before acceptance, worth retrying. */
  | 'rate-limited'
  /** 429 `daily_quota_exceeded` / `monthly_quota_exceeded` — retrying now cannot help. */
  | 'quota-exhausted';

/** Delivery could not be established either way. Treat as not delivered. */
export type EmailUnknownReason =
  /** The request was aborted at `timeoutMs`; the provider may still have accepted it. */
  | 'timeout'
  /** Transport failure. Indistinguishable from a lost response, so not a definite failure. */
  | 'network-error'
  /** 5xx: the send may have been accepted before the error surfaced. */
  | 'provider-unavailable'
  /** 409: another request used this idempotency key, and that one may have delivered. */
  | 'idempotency-conflict'
  /** 2xx with no usable message id — accepted, but with no evidence to record. */
  | 'unreadable-response';

/**
 * The send contract. Three states, because "I could not confirm this was sent"
 * must not be expressible as either success or clear failure.
 */
export type EmailSendResult =
  | {
      readonly status: 'sent';
      /**
       * Resend's message id. Present only here, and only when the provider
       * returned it — this is the value an audit row can point at.
       */
      readonly providerMessageId: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'not_sent';
      readonly reason: EmailNotSentReason;
      /** Human-readable context, truncated. May contain the recipient address. */
      readonly detail: string;
      readonly httpStatus: number | null;
      /** Resend's error name, e.g. `invalid_from_address`, when it gave one. */
      readonly providerCode: string | null;
      /** Safe to retry: nothing was sent, so a retry cannot duplicate delivery. */
      readonly retryable: boolean;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'unknown';
      readonly reason: EmailUnknownReason;
      readonly detail: string;
      readonly httpStatus: number | null;
      readonly providerCode: string | null;
      // Deliberately no `retryable`. See the module header: there is no field
      // here for a caller to read as permission to loop.
    };

/**
 * The one predicate a security-critical caller should branch on.
 *
 * Written as a type guard so the withdrawal path reads
 * `if (!isEmailDelivered(result)) return refuse(...)` and cannot accidentally
 * fall through on `unknown`.
 */
export function isEmailDelivered(
  result: EmailSendResult
): result is Extract<EmailSendResult, { status: 'sent' }> {
  return result.status === 'sent';
}

/**
 * Reads config from the environment. Never throws.
 *
 * Not throwing is deliberate: `packages/shared`'s barrel re-exports this module
 * into every service, so a top-level environment assertion here would stop the
 * indexer booting because the mail sender is unset. A missing key surfaces at
 * send time as `not_sent` / `not-configured` instead — and `isEmailConfigured`
 * exists so a service that *does* need mail can say so at boot rather than
 * discovering it during a user's withdrawal.
 *
 * Reads only server-side names. Nothing `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is consulted, by design.
 */
export function loadEmailConfigFromEnv(
  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env
): EmailConfig {
  const rawBase = (env.RESEND_API_BASE_URL ?? '').trim() || RESEND_DEFAULT_BASE_URL;
  return {
    apiKey: (env.RESEND_API_KEY ?? '').trim(),
    from: (env.EMAIL_FROM ?? '').trim(),
    replyTo: (env.EMAIL_REPLY_TO ?? '').trim() || undefined,
    // A trailing slash would produce `//emails`, which some proxies 404 on.
    baseUrl: rawBase.replace(/\/+$/, ''),
    timeoutMs: clampTimeout(env.EMAIL_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS)
  };
}

/**
 * Clamps the send timeout.
 *
 * An unclamped `0` or `NaN` (a blank or fat-fingered env value) would abort every
 * request instantly, turning all sends into `unknown` — which fails closed, so no
 * withdrawal would ever complete and the cause would be invisible.
 */
function clampTimeout(raw: string | undefined): number {
  const parsed = Number(raw);
  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed <= 0) return EMAIL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS;
  return Math.min(Math.max(Math.round(parsed), EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS), EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS);
}

/**
 * Whether a send could even be attempted. For boot-time checks and health
 * endpoints — not a delivery guarantee.
 */
export function isEmailConfigured(config: EmailConfig): boolean {
  return config.apiKey.length > 0 && config.from.length > 0;
}

/**
 * A bare address, no display name and no list.
 *
 * `\r` and `\n` are rejected everywhere they could reach a header: the JSON body
 * makes classic SMTP header injection unlikely, but `headers`/`subject` do flow
 * into the outbound message and a newline there is never legitimate.
 */
function isPlainAddress(value: string): boolean {
  if (value.length === 0 || value.length > 320) return false;
  if (/[\r\n,;<>\s]/.test(value)) return false;
  return /^[^@]+@[^@.]+(\.[^@.]+)+$/.test(value);
}

/** Accepts `user@domain` or `Name <user@domain>`, which Resend needs for a friendly from. */
function isSenderAddress(value: string): boolean {
  if (/[\r\n]/.test(value)) return false;
  const angled = /<([^<>]+)>\s*$/.exec(value);
  return isPlainAddress(angled ? angled[1]!.trim() : value);
}

function notSent(
  reason: EmailNotSentReason,
  detail: string,
  retryable: boolean,
  httpStatus: number | null = null,
  providerCode: string | null = null
): EmailSendResult {
  return { status: 'not_sent', reason, detail: truncate(detail), httpStatus, providerCode, retryable };
}

function unknown(
  reason: EmailUnknownReason,
  detail: string,
  httpStatus: number | null = null,
  providerCode: string | null = null
): EmailSendResult {
  return { status: 'unknown', reason, detail: truncate(detail), httpStatus, providerCode };
}

function truncate(detail: string): string {
  return detail.length > DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH ? `${detail.slice(0, DETAIL_MAX_LENGTH)}…` : detail;
}

/**
 * Strips the API key out of any provider- or transport-supplied text.
 *
 * Not theoretical: a 401 body can quote the credentials it rejected, and a
 * misconfigured proxy in front of the API can echo the request. `detail` is
 * meant to be logged and attached to `custody.withdraw_*` audit rows, so
 * without this a live sending credential ends up in permanent storage — the one
 * place a rotation cannot reach.
 */
function redactApiKey(text: string, apiKey: string): string {
  if (apiKey.length === 0) return text;
  // split/join rather than a regex: an API key needs no escaping this way.
  return text.split(apiKey).join('[redacted]');
}

export interface SendEmailDeps {
  /**
   * Injected so tests exercise the real abort wiring without touching globals or
   * the network. Defaults to the platform `fetch`.
   */
  readonly fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
}

/**
 * Sends one transactional email.
 *
 * Never throws and never rejects — every transport and provider failure is
 * mapped onto the result union. A caller that forgot a `try/catch` therefore
 * cannot end up in an enclosing handler that treats the exception as "carry on";
 * the only way past this function is to read `status`.
 */
export async function sendEmail(
  message: EmailMessage,
  config: EmailConfig,
  deps: SendEmailDeps = {}
): Promise<EmailSendResult> {
  // Validate before any request. A send attempted without a key would put a
  // recipient address on the wire for nothing, and the outcome would come back
  // as an opaque 401 instead of naming the operator's actual mistake.
  if (config.apiKey.length === 0) {
    return notSent('not-configured', 'RESEND_API_KEY is not set', false);
  }
  if (!isSenderAddress(config.from)) {
    return notSent('invalid-sender', `EMAIL_FROM is missing or malformed: "${config.from}"`, false);
  }
  if (config.replyTo !== undefined && !isPlainAddress(config.replyTo)) {
    return notSent('invalid-sender', `EMAIL_REPLY_TO is malformed: "${config.replyTo}"`, false);
  }
  if (!isPlainAddress(message.to)) {
    return notSent('invalid-recipient', `recipient is not a single valid address: "${message.to}"`, false);
  }
  const subject = message.subject.trim();
  if (subject.length === 0 || /[\r\n]/.test(message.subject)) {
    return notSent('invalid-subject', 'subject is empty or contains a line break', false);
  }
  if (!message.html && !message.text) {
    return notSent('empty-body', 'neither html nor text was supplied', false);
  }

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}`
  };
  if (message.idempotencyKey) headers['Idempotency-Key'] = message.idempotencyKey;

  const body: Record<string, unknown> = {
    from: config.from,
    to: [message.to],
    subject
  };
  if (message.html) body.html = message.html;
  if (message.text) body.text = message.text;
  if (config.replyTo) body.reply_to = config.replyTo;

  // The whole exchange — request, error body, success body — runs inside one
  // deadline. See `withDeadline`: settling on headers alone would leave the body
  // read unbounded.
  try {
    return await withDeadline(config.timeoutMs, async (signal): Promise<EmailSendResult> => {
      const response = await (deps.fetchImpl ?? fetch)(`${config.baseUrl}/emails`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers,
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        signal
      });

      if (!response.ok) {
        // The body names the failure far more precisely than the status does
        // (`invalid_from_address` vs a bare 422), and a 429 is two different
        // outcomes depending on it. Read it, but never let a parse failure here
        // decide the classification — the status alone is enough to place the
        // result on the right side of the delivered/not-delivered line, so a
        // body that stalls or is unreadable costs detail, not correctness.
        const { code, snippet } = await readProviderError(response, config.apiKey);
        return classifyErrorStatus(response.status, code, snippet);
      }

      // A 2xx without a parseable id means the message was probably accepted but
      // we have nothing to record. `sent` requires evidence, so this is `unknown`.
      let payload: unknown;
      try {
        payload = await response.json();
      } catch (error) {
        // An abort here is a stalled body, not a malformed one. Rethrow so the
        // outer handler reports `timeout` and the reason names the real cause;
        // both are `unknown`, but only one is actionable by an operator.
        if (signal.aborted) throw error;
        return unknown(
          'unreadable-response',
          'provider returned 2xx with an unparseable body',
          response.status
        );
      }
      const id = (payload as { id?: unknown } | null)?.id;
      if (typeof id !== 'string' || id.length === 0) {
        return unknown(
          'unreadable-response',
          'provider returned 2xx with no message id',
          response.status
        );
      }
      return { status: 'sent', providerMessageId: id };
    });
  } catch (error) {
    // Both branches are genuinely ambiguous. An abort at `timeoutMs` says
    // nothing about whether Resend accepted the message before we stopped
    // listening, and a transport error is indistinguishable from a response
    // lost on the way back. Reporting either as a definite failure would let a
    // caller conclude the mailbox was never reached and act on that.
    const name = error instanceof Error ? error.name : '';
    const detail = redactApiKey(
      error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'transport failure',
      config.apiKey
    );
    return name === 'AbortError' || name === 'TimeoutError'
      ? unknown('timeout', `aborted after ${config.timeoutMs}ms: ${detail}`)
      : unknown('network-error', detail);
  }
}

/** Reads Resend's `{ name, message, statusCode }` error body without ever throwing. */
async function readProviderError(
  response: Response,
  apiKey: string
): Promise<{ code: string | null; snippet: string }> {
  const raw = redactApiKey(await response.text().catch(() => ''), apiKey);
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as { name?: unknown; message?: unknown; error?: unknown };
    const code = typeof parsed.name === 'string' ? parsed.name : null;
    const messageText =
      typeof parsed.message === 'string'
        ? parsed.message
        : typeof parsed.error === 'string'
          ? parsed.error
          : raw;
    return { code, snippet: messageText };
  } catch {
    return { code: null, snippet: raw };
  }
}

/**
 * Maps an HTTP status onto the union.
 *
 * The split is by *what the caller can conclude*, not by 4xx/5xx. A 4xx means
 * Resend refused the message before accepting it, so nothing was delivered. A
 * 5xx or a 409 leaves open that a message went out, which is the one thing a
 * confirmation flow must not assume away in either direction.
 */
function classifyErrorStatus(
  status: number,
  code: string | null,
  snippet: string
): EmailSendResult {
  const detail = `http-${status}${code ? ` ${code}` : ''}: ${snippet}`;

  if (status === 429) {
    // Both are 429, and the right response differs: a per-second rate limit
    // clears in a moment, an exhausted daily quota does not clear today.
    const quota = code === 'daily_quota_exceeded' || code === 'monthly_quota_exceeded';
    return quota
      ? notSent('quota-exhausted', detail, false, status, code)
      : notSent('rate-limited', detail, true, status, code);
  }
  if (status === 409) {
    // `invalid_idempotent_request` / `concurrent_idempotent_requests`: an
    // earlier request carried this key and may have delivered. We cannot tell.
    return unknown('idempotency-conflict', detail, status, code);
  }
  if (status >= 500) {
    return unknown('provider-unavailable', detail, status, code);
  }
  // Everything else 4xx: unverified domain, bad key, malformed field, unknown
  // route. All operator or payload errors that an identical retry repeats.
  return notSent('provider-rejected', detail, false, status, code);
}

describe('execution mode utilities', () => {
  describe('parseExecutionMode', () => {
    it('parses valid modes natively', () => {
      expect(parseExecutionMode('off')).toBe('off');

      expect(parseExecutionMode(null)).toBe('paper');
      expect(parseExecutionMode(undefined)).toBe('paper');
      expect(parseExecutionMode('invalid_mode')).toBe('paper');
      expect(parseExecutionMode('unknown')).toBe('paper');
    });

      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('live', 'solana', ['solana'])).toBe('live');
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('live+shadow', 'robinhood-chain', ['solana', 'robinhood-chain'])).toBe('live+shadow');
    });

      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('live', 'polygon', ['solana'])).toBe('paper');
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('live+shadow', 'solana', [])).toBe('paper');
    });

    it('preserves non-live modes regardless of enabled chains', () => {
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('off', 'solana', [])).toBe('off');
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('paper', 'polygon', [])).toBe('paper');
    });

    it('fails closed for invalid legacy inputs', () => {
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode('random_typo', 'solana', ['solana'])).toBe('paper');
      expect(mapLegacyTradingMode(' LIVE ', 'solana', ['solana'])).toBe('paper');
    });
  });

  describe('parseLiveEnabledChains', () => {
    it('parses comma-separated valid chains', () => {
      expect(parseLiveEnabledChains('solana, polygon')).toEqual(['solana', 'polygon']);
      expect(parseLiveEnabledChains('robinhood-chain,solana')).toEqual(['robinhood-chain', 'solana']);
    });

    it('ignores invalid chains and preserves valid ones', () => {
      expect(parseLiveEnabledChains('solana, garbage, polygon')).toEqual(['solana', 'polygon']);
    });

    it('handles empty input gracefully', () => {
      expect(parseLiveEnabledChains('')).toEqual([]);
      expect(parseLiveEnabledChains(null)).toEqual([]);
    });
  });

==> packages/shared/src/execution.ts <==
import { Chain, ExecutionMode } from './types.js';

/**
 * Parses an execution mode securely.
 * Fails-closed: any unknown or invalid value returns 'paper'.
 * @param value The string to parse
 * @returns ExecutionMode ('off' | 'paper' | 'live' | 'live+shadow')
 */
export function parseExecutionMode(value: string | undefined | null): ExecutionMode {
  if (!value) return 'paper';
  if (value === 'off') return 'off';
  if (value === 'live') return 'live';
  if (value === 'live+shadow') return 'live+shadow';
  if (value === 'paper') return 'paper';
  
  // Any unrecognized value defaults safely to paper
  return 'paper';
}

/**
 * Maps a legacy TRADING_MODE value to an ExecutionMode for a specific chain.
 * Live execution is strictly clamped to 'paper' if the chain is not in the certified allowlist.
 */
export function mapLegacyTradingMode(
  legacyMode: string | undefined | null,
  chain: Chain,
  liveEnabledChains: Chain[]
): ExecutionMode {
  const parsed = parseExecutionMode(legacyMode);
  
  if (parsed === 'live' || parsed === 'live+shadow') {
    if (liveEnabledChains.includes(chain)) {
      return parsed;
    }
    return 'paper'; // Clamp uncertified chains
  }
  
  return parsed;
}

/**
 * Parses the LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS environment variable.
 */
export function parseLiveEnabledChains(envValue: string | undefined | null): Chain[] {
  if (!envValue) return [];
  const parts = envValue.split(',').map(s => s.trim().toLowerCase());
  return parts.filter(p => p === 'solana' || p === 'polygon' || p === 'robinhood-chain') as Chain[];
}

describe('ingestion health snapshots', () => {
  it('calculates 24-hour counters, lag, and insert ratio', () => {

      {

      lagSeconds: 120,
      batchLagSeconds: 60,
      inserted24h: 9,
      skipped24h: 1,
      failed24h: 2,
      insertRatio: 0.9
    });
  });

    const boundary = buildIngestionHealthSnapshots([
      {
        chain: 'polygon',
        lastEventAt: '2026-07-19T11:50:00.000Z',
        lastBatchAt: null,
        lastSuccessAt: null,
        inserted24h: 0,
        skipped24h: 0,
        failed24h: 0
      }
    ], NOW).find((item) => item.chain === 'polygon');

    const stale = buildIngestionHealthSnapshots([
      {
        chain: 'polygon',
        lastEventAt: '2026-07-19T11:49:59.000Z',
        lastBatchAt: null,
        lastSuccessAt: null,
        inserted24h: 0,
        skipped24h: 0,
        failed24h: 0
      }
    ], NOW).find((item) => item.chain === 'polygon');

    expect(boundary?.status).toBe('healthy');
    expect(stale?.status).toBe('stale');
  });

  it('returns every supported chain and never treats missing data as healthy', () => {
    const snapshots = buildIngestionHealthSnapshots([], NOW);

    expect(snapshots.map((item) => item.chain)).toEqual([
      'solana',
      'polygon',
      'robinhood-chain',
      'base',
      'ethereum',
      'bsc'
    ]);
    expect(snapshots.every((item) => item.status === 'empty')).toBe(true);
    expect(snapshots.every((item) => item.insertRatio === null)).toBe(true);
  });

==> packages/shared/src/ingestion-health.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';

export const INGESTION_CHAINS: readonly Chain[] = [
  'solana',
  'polygon',
  'robinhood-chain',
  'base',
  'ethereum',
  'bsc'
];

export const INGESTION_HEALTH_POLICY: Record<
  Chain,
  { staleAfterSeconds: number; targetLagSeconds: number }
> = {
  solana: { staleAfterSeconds: 5 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 5 * 60 },
  polygon: { staleAfterSeconds: 10 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 5 * 60 },
  'robinhood-chain': { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  base: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  ethereum: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 },
  bsc: { staleAfterSeconds: 15 * 60, targetLagSeconds: 15 * 60 }
};

export type IngestionHealthStatus = 'healthy' | 'stale' | 'empty';

export type RawIngestionHealth = {
  chain: Chain;
  lastEventAt: Date | string | null;
  lastBatchAt: Date | string | null;
  lastSuccessAt: Date | string | null;
  inserted24h: number | string;
  skipped24h: number | string;
  failed24h: number | string;
};

export type IngestionHealthSnapshot = {
  chain: Chain;
  status: IngestionHealthStatus;
  lastEventAt: string | null;
  lastBatchAt: string | null;
  lastSuccessAt: string | null;
  lagSeconds: number | null;
  batchLagSeconds: number | null;
  staleAfterSeconds: number;
  targetLagSeconds: number;
  inserted24h: number;
  skipped24h: number;
  failed24h: number;
  insertRatio: number | null;
};

function parseDate(value: Date | string | null): Date | null {
  if (value === null) return null;
  const parsed = value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(value);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed.getTime()) ? parsed : null;
}

function secondsSince(value: Date | null, now: Date): number | null {
  if (!value) return null;
  return Math.max(0, Math.floor((now.getTime() - value.getTime()) / 1000));
}

function normalizeCount(value: number | string): number {
  const parsed = Number(value);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? Math.trunc(parsed) : 0;
}

export function buildIngestionHealthSnapshots(
  rows: RawIngestionHealth[],
  now = new Date()
): IngestionHealthSnapshot[] {
  const byChain = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.chain, row]));

  return INGESTION_CHAINS.map((chain) => {
    const row = byChain.get(chain);
    const lastEventAt = parseDate(row?.lastEventAt ?? null);
    const lastBatchAt = parseDate(row?.lastBatchAt ?? null);
    const lastSuccessAt = parseDate(row?.lastSuccessAt ?? null);
    const inserted24h = normalizeCount(row?.inserted24h ?? 0);
    const skipped24h = normalizeCount(row?.skipped24h ?? 0);
    const failed24h = normalizeCount(row?.failed24h ?? 0);
    const lagSeconds = secondsSince(lastEventAt, now);
    const policy = INGESTION_HEALTH_POLICY[chain];
    const attempted = inserted24h + skipped24h;

    return {
      chain,
      status: lagSeconds === null
        ? 'empty'
        : lagSeconds > policy.staleAfterSeconds
          ? 'stale'
          : 'healthy',
      lastEventAt: lastEventAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lastBatchAt: lastBatchAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lastSuccessAt: lastSuccessAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
      lagSeconds,
      batchLagSeconds: secondsSince(lastBatchAt, now),
      staleAfterSeconds: policy.staleAfterSeconds,
      targetLagSeconds: policy.targetLagSeconds,
      inserted24h,
      skipped24h,
      failed24h,
      insertRatio: attempted > 0 ? inserted24h / attempted : null
    };
  });
}
