    expect(serialized).not.toContain(credentials.passphrase);
    expect(redacted.secret).toBe('[redacted]');
    expect(redacted.passphrase).toBe('[redacted]');
  });

  it('keeps only a short api-key prefix for correlation', () => {
    const redacted = redactCredentials(credentials);
    expect(redacted.apiKey).toBe('7b1e2d60…');
    expect(redacted.apiKey).not.toBe(credentials.apiKey);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/polymarket-clob-auth.ts <==
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto';

/**
 * Polymarket CLOB **V2** L2 authentication (checklist S3-20).
 *
 * Verified against the live docs (`docs.polymarket.com/getting-started/api`)
 * rather than written from memory — the V1→V2 cutover on 2026-04-28 invalidated
 * every legacy SDK and V1-signed order, so a remembered signing scheme would
 * fail against production.
 *
 * Two layers exist:
 *   * **L1** — the wallet signs an EIP-712 `ClobAuth` payload. Used once, to
 *     create or derive API credentials.
 *   * **L2** — every private request is signed with those credentials using
 *     HMAC-SHA256. This module implements L2.
 *
 * Order *placement* needs both: L2 authenticates the request, and a separate
 * wallet signature authorises the order itself.
 *
 * **Not to be confused with the Perps API.** Perps lives under `/v1/trade/*` and
 * does carry client order IDs (`coid`). The predictions CLOB used here does not
 * — its order payload has no client-order-ID field, which is why idempotency is
 * carried by our own persisted signal/execution identity instead (audit G3-P6,
 * closed as venue-limited; re-verified against the docs 2026-08-05).
 */

export const CLOB_BASE_URL = 'https://clob.polymarket.com';

/** Chain ID pinned by the CLOB auth domain. Polygon mainnet. */
export const CLOB_CHAIN_ID = 137;

export interface ClobCredentials {
  readonly apiKey: string;
  /** Base64-encoded HMAC key. Decoded before use — never used as raw text. */
  readonly secret: string;
  readonly passphrase: string;
}

/**
 * Builds the EIP-712 `ClobAuth` payload for L1 signing.
 *
 * The signer address, timestamp, and nonce used here must be passed unchanged to
 * `/auth/api-key` or `/auth/derive-api-key`; the server re-derives the same
 * struct and recovers the signer, so any drift fails verification.
 */
export function buildClobAuthTypedData(input: {
  signerAddress: string;
  timestampSeconds: number;
  /** Credential nonce. `0` unless managing multiple credential sets. */
  nonce?: number;
}) {
  return {
    domain: {
      name: 'ClobAuthDomain',
      version: '1',
      chainId: CLOB_CHAIN_ID
    },
    types: {
      EIP712Domain: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'version', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' }
      ],
      ClobAuth: [
        { name: 'address', type: 'address' },
        { name: 'timestamp', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'nonce', type: 'uint256' },
        { name: 'message', type: 'string' }
      ]
    },
    primaryType: 'ClobAuth' as const,
    message: {
      address: input.signerAddress,
      // String, not number — the type is `string` in the struct, and a numeric
      // encoding would hash differently and fail signature recovery.
      timestamp: String(input.timestampSeconds),
      nonce: input.nonce ?? 0,
      message: 'This message attests that I control the given wallet'
    }
  };
}

/**
 * URL-safe base64 **with padding retained**.
 *
 * Node's built-in `'base64url'` encoding strips the `=` padding, which the CLOB
 * rejects. The docs specify `urlsafeBase64WithPadding`, so the transform is done
 * explicitly here rather than relying on the built-in.
 */
function urlSafeBase64WithPadding(buffer: Buffer): string {
  return buffer.toString('base64').replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_');
}

export interface L2SignatureInput {
  readonly secret: string;
  readonly timestampSeconds: number;
  readonly method: string;
  /** Route path only, e.g. `/data/orders`. No host, no query string. */
  readonly path: string;
  /**
   * The **exact serialized body sent over the wire**, or omitted for bodyless
   * requests. Re-serializing here would risk key-order or whitespace drift from
   * what is actually transmitted, and the signature would not verify.
   */
  readonly body?: string;
}

/**
 * Signs an L2 request.
 *
 * `message = timestamp + METHOD + path + body`, HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the
 * **base64-decoded** secret. Using the secret as raw text is the classic error
 * here and produces a signature that never verifies.
 */
export function signClobL2Request(input: L2SignatureInput): string {
  const message = `${input.timestampSeconds}${input.method.toUpperCase()}${input.path}${input.body ?? ''}`;
  const key = Buffer.from(input.secret, 'base64');
  return urlSafeBase64WithPadding(createHmac('sha256', key).update(message).digest());
}

export interface ClobAuthHeaders {
  readonly POLY_ADDRESS: string;
  readonly POLY_SIGNATURE: string;
  readonly POLY_TIMESTAMP: string;
  readonly POLY_API_KEY: string;
  readonly POLY_PASSPHRASE: string;
}

/**
 * Builds the five headers every L2-authenticated CLOB request carries.
 *
 * The timestamp is generated per request and must be the same value that went
 * into the signature — deriving it twice would let a slow call sign one second
 * and send another.
 */
export function buildClobL2Headers(input: {
  credentials: ClobCredentials;
  signerAddress: string;
  method: string;
  path: string;
  body?: string;
  timestampSeconds?: number;
}): ClobAuthHeaders {
  const timestampSeconds = input.timestampSeconds ?? Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const signature = signClobL2Request({
    secret: input.credentials.secret,
    timestampSeconds,
    method: input.method,
    path: input.path,
    body: input.body
  });
  return {
    POLY_ADDRESS: input.signerAddress,
    POLY_SIGNATURE: signature,
    POLY_TIMESTAMP: String(timestampSeconds),
    POLY_API_KEY: input.credentials.apiKey,
    POLY_PASSPHRASE: input.credentials.passphrase
  };
}

/**
 * Redacts credentials for logging.
 *
 * The audit requires no secrets in logs (G3-P3). Passing a whole credential
 * object to a logger is the easy mistake; this makes the safe form available so
 * there is no reason to.
 */
export function redactCredentials(credentials: ClobCredentials): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    apiKey: `${credentials.apiKey.slice(0, 8)}…`,
    secret: '[redacted]',
    passphrase: '[redacted]'
  };
}

==> packages/shared/src/polymarket-clob-credentials.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  assertUsableClobCredentials,
  clobCredentialCacheKey,
  clobL1SignerFrom,
  createClobCredentialStore,
  deriveClobCredentials,
  fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature,
  normalizeClobSignerAddress,
  parseClobCredentials,
  resolveClobCredentials,
  ClobCredentialError,
  type ClobAuthTypedData,
  type ClobL1Signer
} from './polymarket-clob-credentials.js';
import { signClobL2Request, type ClobCredentials } from './polymarket-clob-auth.js';

/**
 * Tests for the `S3-20` seam: credentials as a function of a signer.
 *
 * Two properties matter more than the rest and are named so a mutation check can
 * point at them:
 *
 *   * `never hands one signer the credentials of another` — the cross-signer
 *     cache isolation.
 *   * `never puts the secret or passphrase in a thrown error` — the redaction
 *     boundary in `parseClobCredentials`.
 */

const ADDRESS_A = '0xAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAaAa';
const ADDRESS_B = '0xBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBbBb';
const SIGNATURE = `0x${'11'.repeat(65)}`;
const ORIGIN = 'https://clob.test';

// Real base64, so `Buffer.from(secret, 'base64')` yields actual key bytes.
const SECRET_A = Buffer.from('signer-a-secret-key-material-32b').toString('base64');
const SECRET_B = Buffer.from('signer-b-secret-key-material-32b').toString('base64');

function credentialsFor(label: string, secret: string): ClobCredentials {
  return {
    apiKey: `api-key-${label}`,
    secret,
    passphrase: `passphrase-${label}`
  };
}

const CREDENTIALS_A = credentialsFor('a', SECRET_A);
const CREDENTIALS_B = credentialsFor('b', SECRET_B);

interface RecordingSigner extends ClobL1Signer {
  readonly payloads: ClobAuthTypedData[];
}

function recordingSigner(address: string, signature: string = SIGNATURE): RecordingSigner {
  const payloads: ClobAuthTypedData[] = [];
  return {
    address,
    payloads,
    async signTypedData(typedData) {
      payloads.push(typedData);
      return signature;
    }
  };
}

function jsonResponse(status: number, body: unknown): Response {
  return {
    ok: status >= 200 && status < 300,
    status,
    json: async () => body
  } as unknown as Response;
}

function stubFetch(...responses: Response[]) {
  const calls: Array<{ url: string; init: RequestInit }> = [];
  const impl = vi.fn(async (url: unknown, init: unknown) => {
    calls.push({ url: String(url), init: init as RequestInit });
    const next = responses.shift();
    if (!next) throw new Error('stubFetch ran out of responses');
    return next;
  });
  return { impl: impl as unknown as typeof fetch, calls, mock: impl };
}

function headersOf(init: RequestInit): Record<string, string> {
  return init.headers as Record<string, string>;
}

describe('L1 derivation is a function of the signer', () => {
  it('signs ClobAuth and sends the four documented L1 headers', async () => {
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));

    const credentials = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl,
      nowSeconds: () => 1_780_000_000
    });

    expect(credentials).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.url).toBe(`${ORIGIN}/auth/api-key`);
    expect(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init.method).toBe('POST');
    // Exactly the set the installed SDK sends for both auth routes.
    expect(Object.keys(headersOf(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init)).sort()).toEqual([
      'POLY_ADDRESS',
      'POLY_NONCE',
      'POLY_SIGNATURE',
      'POLY_TIMESTAMP'
    ]);
    expect(headersOf(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init)).toEqual({
      POLY_ADDRESS: ADDRESS_A,
      POLY_NONCE: '0',
      POLY_SIGNATURE: SIGNATURE,
      POLY_TIMESTAMP: '1780000000'
    });
  });

  it('signs the payload the venue re-derives, with the same timestamp it sends', async () => {
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));

    await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl,
      nonce: 3,
      nowSeconds: () => 1_780_000_001
    });

    const payload = signer.payloads[0]!;
    expect(payload.domain).toEqual({ name: 'ClobAuthDomain', version: '1', chainId: 137 });
    expect(payload.primaryType).toBe('ClobAuth');
    expect(payload.message.address).toBe(ADDRESS_A);
    expect(payload.message.timestamp).toBe('1780000001');
    expect(payload.message.nonce).toBe(3);
    // Signature and headers must agree, or the server recovers a different struct.
    expect(headersOf(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init).POLY_TIMESTAMP).toBe('1780000001');
    expect(headersOf(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init).POLY_NONCE).toBe('3');
  });

  it('preserves the caller checksummed address on the wire', async () => {
    // The venue recovers the signer from the signature; lowercasing here would
    // be us rewriting a value the caller controls for no reason.
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    await deriveClobCredentials({ signer, baseUrl: ORIGIN, fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl });
    expect(headersOf(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init).POLY_ADDRESS).toBe(ADDRESS_A);
    expect(signer.payloads[0]!.message.address).toBe(ADDRESS_A);
  });

  it('derives with GET /auth/derive-api-key when asked to derive', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      mode: 'derive',
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    });
    expect(fetchImpl.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.url).toBe(`${ORIGIN}/auth/derive-api-key`);
    expect(fetchImpl.calls[0]!.init.method).toBe('GET');
  });

  it('falls back from create to derive on HTTP 400 only', async () => {
    // Mirrors @polymarket/client@0.2.0 createOrDeriveApiKey, which rethrows any
    // status other than 400 rather than making a second call.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(400, { error: 'already exists' }),
      jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));

    const credentials = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    });

    expect(credentials).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(fetchImpl.calls.map((call) => call.url)).toEqual([
      `${ORIGIN}/auth/api-key`,
      `${ORIGIN}/auth/derive-api-key`
    ]);
  });

  it('does not fall back on 401, 429 or 500', async () => {
    for (const status of [401, 429, 500]) {
      const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(status, { error: 'nope' }));
      await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
        signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
        baseUrl: ORIGIN,
        fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
      })).rejects.toMatchObject({
        code: 'clob-credential-rejected',
        status
      });
      expect(fetchImpl.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    }
  });

  it('treats a 400 as a failure when the caller asked to create', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(400, { error: 'already exists' }));
    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      mode: 'create',
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-rejected', status: 400 });
    expect(fetchImpl.calls).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('signs before it touches the transport', async () => {
    // Ordering is the safety net: a signer that cannot sign never produces a
    // venue request, so an unstubbed caller fails locally, not on the network.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    const signer: ClobL1Signer = {
      address: ADDRESS_A,
      signTypedData: async () => {
        throw new TypeError('_signTypedData is not a function');
      }
    };

    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-signing-failed' });
    expect(fetchImpl.mock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('rejects a signer that returns something other than a hex signature', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A, 'user rejected request'),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-signature-malformed' });
    expect(fetchImpl.mock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('accepts an ERC-1271 length signature, which a Deposit Wallet produces', async () => {
    // Every Polymarket wallet deployed on or after 2026-05-04 is a Deposit
    // Wallet with ERC-7739-wrapped signatures, longer than 65 bytes. A strict
    // 65-byte check would reject the majority wallet type.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A, `0x${'ab'.repeat(200)}`),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    })).resolves.toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
  });

  it('surfaces a transport failure without making a second attempt', async () => {
    const impl = vi.fn(async () => {
      throw new Error('ECONNREFUSED');
    });
    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: impl as unknown as typeof fetch
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-transport-failed' });
    expect(impl).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('rejects a malformed signer address without echoing it', async () => {
    // The realistic bad value here is a private key in the wrong field.
    const key = `0x${'de'.repeat(32)}`;
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    const failure = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(key),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    }).catch((error: unknown) => error as ClobCredentialError);

    expect(failure.code).toBe('clob-credential-address-invalid');
    expect(failure.message).not.toContain(key);
    expect(failure.message).toContain('66-character string');
  });

  it('rejects a non-integer nonce and a non-positive clock', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      nonce: 1.5,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-nonce-invalid' });

    await expect(deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl,
      nowSeconds: () => 0
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-timestamp-invalid' });
  });

  it('derives credentials that actually sign an L2 request', async () => {
    // End to end within the module boundary: the derived secret is the HMAC key
    // `signClobL2Request` expects, base64-decoded.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    const credentials = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    });
    const signature = signClobL2Request({
      secret: credentials.secret,
      timestampSeconds: 1_780_000_000,
      method: 'GET',
      path: '/data/orders'
    });
    expect(signature).toHaveLength(44);
  });
});

describe('credential payload validation', () => {
  it('reads apiKey from the wire, which the SDK renames to key', async () => {
    // @polymarket/bindings ApiKeyCredsSchema maps apiKey -> key, so SDK-shaped
    // code and wire-shaped code disagree on this one name.
    const parsed = parseClobCredentials(
      { apiKey: 'k', secret: SECRET_A, passphrase: 'p' },
      'GET /auth/derive-api-key'
    );
    expect(parsed.apiKey).toBe('k');
    expect(parsed).not.toHaveProperty('key');
  });

  it('rejects a secret that decodes to no key bytes', () => {
    // Buffer.from('=', 'base64') is empty, so every L2 signature would be
    // computed with an empty HMAC key: well-formed, and rejected forever.
    expect(() => parseClobCredentials(
      { apiKey: 'k', secret: '=', passphrase: 'p' },
      'GET /auth/derive-api-key'
    )).toThrow('not base64 that decodes to any key bytes');
  });

  it('reports every missing field at once, by name', () => {
    const failure = (() => {
      try {
        parseClobCredentials({ apiKey: 'k' }, 'GET /auth/derive-api-key');
        return null;
      } catch (error) {
        return error as ClobCredentialError;
      }
    })();
    expect(failure?.code).toBe('clob-credential-response-malformed');
    expect(failure?.message).toContain('secret is');
    expect(failure?.message).toContain('passphrase is');
  });

  it('validates preconfigured credentials the same way as derived ones', () => {
    expect(() => assertUsableClobCredentials({
      apiKey: 'k',
      secret: '',
      passphrase: 'p'
    })).toThrow('preconfigured credentials');
    expect(assertUsableClobCredentials(CREDENTIALS_A)).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
  });
});

describe('secret redaction (G3-P3: no secrets in logs or errors)', () => {
  it('never puts the secret or passphrase in a thrown error', () => {
    // The venue answered 200 with two perfectly good bearer credentials and a
    // broken apiKey. The easy implementation interpolates the whole body into
    // the message; the body is two bearer credentials.
    const livePassphrase = 'pass-a-live-bearer-value';
    const body = { apiKey: 42, secret: SECRET_A, passphrase: livePassphrase };
    const failure = (() => {
      try {
        parseClobCredentials(body, 'POST /auth/api-key');
        return null;
      } catch (error) {
        return error as ClobCredentialError;
      }
    })();

    expect(failure).toBeInstanceOf(ClobCredentialError);
    const surfaces = [
      failure!.message,
      String(failure),
      failure!.stack ?? '',
      JSON.stringify(failure, Object.getOwnPropertyNames(failure))
    ];
    for (const surface of surfaces) {
      expect(surface).not.toContain(SECRET_A);
      expect(surface).not.toContain('signer-a-secret');
      expect(surface).not.toContain(livePassphrase);
    }
    // It still says what went wrong.
    expect(failure!.message).toContain('apiKey is a value of type number');
  });

  it('never puts a venue response body in a rejection error', async () => {
    // The same route returns credentials on success, so nothing is assumed about
    // what a non-2xx body echoes back.
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(403, { detail: `leaked ${SECRET_A}` }));
    const failure = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      mode: 'derive',
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    }).catch((error: unknown) => error as ClobCredentialError);

    expect(failure.message).toBe(
      'clob-credential-rejected: GET /auth/derive-api-key returned HTTP 403'
    );
    expect(failure.message).not.toContain(SECRET_A);
  });

  it('never chains a signer error message, only its constructor name', async () => {
    // A third-party signer's text is outside our control; a badly written
    // adapter could put key material in it.
    const secretish = 'private key 0xdeadbeefcafe';
    const fetchImpl = stubFetch(jsonResponse(200, CREDENTIALS_A));
    const failure = await deriveClobCredentials({
      signer: {
        address: ADDRESS_A,
        signTypedData: async () => {
          throw new RangeError(secretish);
        }
      },
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      fetchImpl: fetchImpl.impl
    }).catch((error: unknown) => error as ClobCredentialError);

    expect(failure.message).toContain('RangeError');
    expect(failure.message).not.toContain(secretish);
    expect((failure as { cause?: unknown }).cause).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('exposes cache keys that carry no secret', async () => {
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      derive: async () => CREDENTIALS_A
    });
    await store.credentialsFor(recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A));
    const serialized = store.keys().join(' ');
    expect(serialized).not.toContain(SECRET_A);
    expect(serialized).not.toContain(CREDENTIALS_A.passphrase);
    expect(serialized).toContain(ADDRESS_A.toLowerCase());
  });
});

describe('cache key', () => {
  it('carries the origin, the lowercased address, and the nonce', () => {
    expect(clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: ADDRESS_A, baseUrl: ORIGIN })).toBe(
      `clob-creds:v1|${ORIGIN}|${ADDRESS_A.toLowerCase()}|0`
    );
  });

  it('gives one key to the checksummed and lowercase forms of one account', () => {
    // EVM addresses are case-insensitive and arrive both ways; one account must
    // not occupy two entries and pay two derivations.
    expect(clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: ADDRESS_A, baseUrl: ORIGIN })).toBe(
      clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: ADDRESS_A.toLowerCase(), baseUrl: ORIGIN })
    );
  });

  it('separates different addresses, nonces and origins', () => {
    const base = { signerAddress: ADDRESS_A, baseUrl: ORIGIN };
    const keys = new Set([
      clobCredentialCacheKey(base),
      clobCredentialCacheKey({ ...base, signerAddress: ADDRESS_B }),
      clobCredentialCacheKey({ ...base, nonce: 1 }),
      clobCredentialCacheKey({ ...base, baseUrl: 'https://clob.staging.test' })
    ]);
    expect(keys.size).toBe(4);
  });

  it('normalizes a trailing path or query away rather than splitting the venue', () => {
    expect(clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: ADDRESS_A, baseUrl: `${ORIGIN}/?x=1` })).toBe(
      clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: ADDRESS_A, baseUrl: ORIGIN })
    );
  });

  it('refuses to key on a malformed address instead of inventing a key', () => {
    expect(() => clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: '', baseUrl: ORIGIN })).toThrow(
      ClobCredentialError
    );
    expect(() => clobCredentialCacheKey({ signerAddress: '0xshort', baseUrl: ORIGIN })).toThrow(
      'clob-credential-address-invalid'
    );
    expect(() => normalizeClobSignerAddress(ADDRESS_A)).not.toThrow();
  });
});

describe('per-signer credential store', () => {
  function storeOverTwoSigners() {
    const derive = vi.fn(async (signer: ClobL1Signer) => {
      if (signer.address.toLowerCase() === ADDRESS_A.toLowerCase()) return CREDENTIALS_A;
      if (signer.address.toLowerCase() === ADDRESS_B.toLowerCase()) return CREDENTIALS_B;
      throw new Error(`unexpected signer ${signer.address}`);
    });
    return { derive, store: createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive }) };
  }

  it('never hands one signer the credentials of another', async () => {
    // The worst available bug in this module: the request succeeds and
    // authenticates as the wrong account, with no local symptom.
    const { store, derive } = storeOverTwoSigners();
    const signerA = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    const signerB = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_B);

    const first = await store.credentialsFor(signerA);
    const second = await store.credentialsFor(signerB);
    // Interleaved, and again after both are warm, because a broken key shows up
    // on the second read rather than the first.
    const firstAgain = await store.credentialsFor(signerA);
    const secondAgain = await store.credentialsFor(signerB);

    expect(first).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(firstAgain).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(second).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_B);
    expect(secondAgain).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_B);
    expect(first.secret).not.toBe(second.secret);
    expect(first.passphrase).not.toBe(second.passphrase);
    expect(store.size()).toBe(2);
    expect(new Set(store.keys()).size).toBe(2);
    // One derivation each: caching happened, and it happened per signer.
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('separates one address nonce 0 from the same address nonce 1', async () => {
    const derive = vi.fn(async (_signer: ClobL1Signer, options: { nonce: number }) =>
      credentialsFor(`nonce-${options.nonce}`, SECRET_A));
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive });
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);

    const zero = await store.credentialsFor(signer);
    const one = await store.credentialsFor(signer, { nonce: 1 });

    expect(zero.apiKey).toBe('api-key-nonce-0');
    expect(one.apiKey).toBe('api-key-nonce-1');
    expect(store.size()).toBe(2);
  });

  it('derives once per signer and reuses the result', async () => {
    const { store, derive } = storeOverTwoSigners();
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    await store.credentialsFor(signer);
    await store.credentialsFor(signer);
    await store.credentialsFor(recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A.toLowerCase()));
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('shares one derivation between concurrent callers for one signer', async () => {
    // Two overlapping signals for one principal must not burn two L1 signatures.
    let resolveDerivation: (credentials: ClobCredentials) => void = () => {};
    const derive = vi.fn(() => new Promise<ClobCredentials>((resolve) => {
      resolveDerivation = resolve;
    }));
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive });
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);

    const both = Promise.all([store.credentialsFor(signer), store.credentialsFor(signer)]);
    resolveDerivation(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(await both).toEqual([CREDENTIALS_A, CREDENTIALS_A]);
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('does not cache a failed derivation', async () => {
    // A cached rejection would replay one venue outage forever.
    const derive = vi.fn()
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('venue unavailable'))
      .mockResolvedValueOnce(CREDENTIALS_A);
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive });
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);

    await expect(store.credentialsFor(signer)).rejects.toThrow('venue unavailable');
    expect(store.size()).toBe(0);
    await expect(store.credentialsFor(signer)).resolves.toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('refuses to serve an entry whose stored identity does not match the signer', async () => {
    // Second half of the guard, proven by forcing the collision the key
    // function is supposed to make impossible.
    const derive = vi.fn(async (signer: ClobL1Signer) =>
      credentialsFor(signer.address, SECRET_A));
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({
      baseUrl: ORIGIN,
      derive,
      cacheKeyFor: () => 'one-key-for-everyone'
    });

    await store.credentialsFor(recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A));
    await expect(store.credentialsFor(recordingSigner(ADDRESS_B))).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'clob-credential-cache-collision'
    });
  });

  it('invalidates one signer without disturbing the other', async () => {
    const { store, derive } = storeOverTwoSigners();
    const signerA = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);
    const signerB = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_B);
    await store.credentialsFor(signerA);
    await store.credentialsFor(signerB);

    expect(store.invalidate(signerA)).toBe(true);
    expect(store.invalidate(signerA)).toBe(false);
    expect(store.size()).toBe(1);

    await store.credentialsFor(signerA);
    await store.credentialsFor(signerB);
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);

    store.clear();
    expect(store.size()).toBe(0);
  });

  it('rejects a malformed signer address before it reaches the deriver', async () => {
    const derive = vi.fn(async () => CREDENTIALS_A);
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive });
    await expect(store.credentialsFor(recordingSigner('not-an-address'))).rejects.toMatchObject({
      code: 'clob-credential-address-invalid'
    });
    expect(derive).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

describe('resolveClobCredentials: the operator is a caller, not a branch', () => {
  it('uses preconfigured credentials without signing anything', async () => {
    const derive = vi.fn(async () => CREDENTIALS_B);
    const signer = recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A);

    const resolved = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      preconfigured: CREDENTIALS_A,
      derive
    });

    expect(resolved).toEqual({ credentials: CREDENTIALS_A, source: 'preconfigured' });
    expect(derive).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(signer.payloads).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('derives when none were supplied', async () => {
    const derive = vi.fn(async () => CREDENTIALS_A);
    const resolved = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      preconfigured: null,
      derive
    });
    expect(resolved).toEqual({ credentials: CREDENTIALS_A, source: 'derived' });
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ address: ADDRESS_A }), {
      nonce: 0
    });
  });

  it('takes the identical path for the operator signer and a per-user signer', async () => {
    // The branch is on whether credentials were supplied, never on who is
    // asking. Two different signers with no preconfigured credentials produce
    // structurally identical calls.
    const derive = vi.fn(async (signer: ClobL1Signer) =>
      credentialsFor(signer.address, SECRET_A));

    const operator = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      derive
    });
    const user = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_B),
      derive
    });

    expect(operator.source).toBe('derived');
    expect(user.source).toBe('derived');
    expect(derive.mock.calls[0]![1]).toEqual(derive.mock.calls[1]![1]);
    expect(operator.credentials.apiKey).not.toBe(user.credentials.apiKey);
  });

  it('rejects preconfigured credentials that cannot sign an L2 request', async () => {
    await expect(resolveClobCredentials({
      signer: recordingSigner(ADDRESS_A),
      preconfigured: { apiKey: 'k', secret: '=', passphrase: 'p' },
      derive: async () => CREDENTIALS_A
    })).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'clob-credential-response-malformed' });
  });

  it('wires a store as the deriver, so the operator gets caching for free', async () => {
    const derive = vi.fn(async () => CREDENTIALS_A);
    const store = createClobCredentialStore({ baseUrl: ORIGIN, derive });
    const signer = clobL1SignerFrom(ADDRESS_A, async () => SIGNATURE);

    const first = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      derive: (candidate, options) => store.credentialsFor(candidate, options)
    });
    const second = await resolveClobCredentials({
      signer,
      derive: (candidate, options) => store.credentialsFor(candidate, options)
    });

    expect(first.credentials).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(second.credentials).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
    expect(derive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  describe('fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature', () => {
    it('creates or derives credentials using an existing L1 signature', async () => {
      const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async (url: string | URL | Request) => {
        const u = String(url);
        if (u.includes('/auth/api-key')) {
          return new Response(JSON.stringify(CREDENTIALS_A), { status: 200 });
        }
        return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
      });

      const creds = await fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature({
        address: ADDRESS_A,
        signature: SIGNATURE,
        timestampSeconds: 1730000000,
        baseUrl: ORIGIN,
        fetchImpl: fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch
      });

      expect(creds).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_A);
      expect(fetchImpl).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    });

    it('falls back to derive-api-key if create returns 400', async () => {
      const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async (url: string | URL | Request) => {
        const u = String(url);
        if (u.includes('/auth/api-key')) {
          return new Response('User exists', { status: 400 });
        }
        if (u.includes('/auth/derive-api-key')) {
          return new Response(JSON.stringify(CREDENTIALS_B), { status: 200 });
        }
        return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
      });

      const creds = await fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature({
        address: ADDRESS_B,
        signature: SIGNATURE,
        timestampSeconds: 1730000000,
        baseUrl: ORIGIN,
        fetchImpl: fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch
      });

      expect(creds).toEqual(CREDENTIALS_B);
      expect(fetchImpl).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    });
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/polymarket-clob-credentials.ts <==
import {
  buildClobAuthTypedData,
  CLOB_BASE_URL,
  type ClobCredentials
} from './polymarket-clob-auth.js';

/**
 * Deriving Polymarket CLOB L2 credentials **as a function of a signer**
 * (checklist `S3-20`, ADR-0003 section 4).
 *
 * ## What this adds to `polymarket-clob-auth.ts`
 *
 * That module already builds the L1 `ClobAuth` typed data and computes the L2
 * HMAC. What it never did was join them: nothing turned "I hold this signer" into
 * "here are its three credential values". The operator got its credentials from
 * environment variables, or from inside `@polymarket/client`'s own
 * `createSecureClient`, which reads a private key at the edge of the process.
 * Neither shape can serve a second principal.
 *
 * This module is that join, and it takes the signer as an argument. There is no
 * module-level credential, no `process.env` read, and no notion of *whose* signer
 * it is — the operator and a Stage 4 per-user grant are two callers of one
 * function, exactly as `solana-signer.ts` is a parameter to
 * `createJupiterJitoRuntime` and `UserExecutionAuthority`'s operator adapter is
 * one entry in a list rather than a branch in the executor.
 *
 * ## What credentials do and do not buy you
 *
 * L2 credentials authenticate an HTTP *request*. They cannot place an order:
 * every order carries an EIP-712 `Order` struct with a fresh `salt`, signed by
 * the account signer (ADR-0003 section 4.2). So a caller that holds only
 * credentials can read private endpoints and cancel, and cannot trade. This is
 * why ADR-0003 section 4.3 concludes that Polymarket cannot be made
 * non-custodial and why fork (b) exists: per-user credentials are necessary and
 * nowhere near sufficient.
 *
 * Deriving them still has to be per-signer, because the credentials the venue
 * issues are bound to the signer address that produced the L1 signature. One
 * operator-wide credential set cannot authenticate a request made on behalf of a
 * different wallet.
 *
 * ## Verified, not remembered
 *
 * Endpoints, headers and the create/derive fallback rule were read off the live
 * docs (`getting-started/api`) and off the installed SDK, not recalled:
 *
 *   * `POST /auth/api-key` creates; `GET /auth/derive-api-key` derives.
 *   * Both take exactly `POLY_ADDRESS`, `POLY_NONCE`, `POLY_SIGNATURE`,
 *     `POLY_TIMESTAMP` (`@polymarket/client@0.2.0`
 *     `dist/chunk-FA3ZDOJN.js`, the header builder for both routes).
 *   * The response field is `apiKey`. The SDK renames it to `key` in
 *     `ApiKeyCredsSchema` (`@polymarket/bindings@0.2.0/dist/clob/index.js`), so
 *     code written against the SDK type and code written against the wire
 *     disagree on that one name. This module speaks the wire.
 *   * `create-or-derive` tries create first and falls back to derive **only on
 *     HTTP 400**, which is what the SDK's `createOrDeriveApiKey` does:
 *     `try { return await create(...) } catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof HttpError)
 *     || e.status !== 400) throw e } return derive(...)`. Any other status is a
 *     real failure and must not be papered over by a second call.
 *
 * ## Nothing here logs, and nothing here echoes a value it was given
 *
 * Every value this module handles is a bearer credential or a private key's
 * public shadow. So: no logger, no `console`, and every error message is built
 * from field *names*, HTTP statuses and lengths only. `describeOpaque` exists
 * because the most likely malformed "address" a caller passes is a private key,
 * and an error that echoed its argument would write that key to a log.
 *
 * The same discipline as `packages/db/src/execution-grants.ts`, which never
 * selects the `sealed_secret` column on a read path so the ciphertext cannot
 * reach a response by accident.
 */

/** The EIP-712 payload `buildClobAuthTypedData` produces. */
export type ClobAuthTypedData = ReturnType<typeof buildClobAuthTypedData>;

/**
 * The whole of what credential derivation needs from a principal.
 *
 * Two members, neither of them a key: an address, and the ability to sign one
 * specific payload. An ethers `Wallet`, a viem account, a KMS client, a Privy
 * remote signer (ADR-0003 section 4.3's reopened fork (c)) and a test stub all
 * fit, and none of them has to be imported here — this module pulls in no chain
 * library at all, for the same reason `execution-authority.ts` declares
 * `Eip712TypedData` locally rather than importing it from `viem`.
 */
export interface ClobL1Signer {
  /** Polygon address the signature must recover to. `0x` + 40 hex. */
  readonly address: string;
  signTypedData(typedData: ClobAuthTypedData): Promise<string>;
}

/**
 * Wraps an address and a signing function as a `ClobL1Signer`.
 *
 * Exists so callers do not hand-roll the object literal and get the member name
 * wrong; every adapter (ethers v5's `_signTypedData`, viem's `signTypedData`, a
 * remote signer's HTTP call) is a one-line closure through here.
 */
export function clobL1SignerFrom(
  address: string,
  signTypedData: (typedData: ClobAuthTypedData) => Promise<string>
): ClobL1Signer {
  return { address, signTypedData };
}

/** How credentials are obtained for a signer the caller has not cached. */
export type ClobCredentialDeriver = (
  signer: ClobL1Signer,
  options: { readonly nonce: number }
) => Promise<ClobCredentials>;

export type ClobCredentialFailureCode =
  /** The signer's `address` is not an EVM address. */
  | 'clob-credential-address-invalid'
  /** The credential nonce is not a non-negative safe integer. */
  | 'clob-credential-nonce-invalid'
  /** The clock produced something that is not a positive integer second. */
  | 'clob-credential-timestamp-invalid'
  /** `baseUrl` is not a URL we can take an origin from. */
  | 'clob-credential-base-url-invalid'
  /** The injected signer threw. The mechanism is present; it refused or broke. */
  | 'clob-credential-signing-failed'
  /** The signer returned something that is not a hex signature. */
  | 'clob-credential-signature-malformed'
  /** The request never completed: DNS, TCP, TLS, timeout. */
  | 'clob-credential-transport-failed'
  /** The venue answered with a non-2xx status. */
  | 'clob-credential-rejected'
  /** 2xx, but the body is not usable credentials. */
  | 'clob-credential-response-malformed'
  /**
   * Two different signer identities landed on one cache key. Should be
   * unreachable; it is checked because the failure it guards against — handing
   * one user's credentials to another — is invisible from the outside.
   */
  | 'clob-credential-cache-collision';

/**
 * A derivation failure, with a stable code.
 *
 * `cause` is attached for `clob-credential-transport-failed` only. A transport
 * error comes from `fetch` and describes a socket; a *signing* error comes from
 * whatever signer the caller injected, and a third-party signer's message text
 * is outside our control — chaining it would let a badly written adapter put key
 * material into our error. So the signing path records the cause's constructor
 * name and nothing else.
 */
export class ClobCredentialError extends Error {
  readonly code: ClobCredentialFailureCode;
  /** HTTP status when the venue answered, else `null`. */
  readonly status: number | null;

  constructor(
    code: ClobCredentialFailureCode,
    detail: string,
    options: { readonly status?: number | null; readonly cause?: unknown } = {}
  ) {
    super(`${code}: ${detail}`);
    this.name = 'ClobCredentialError';
    this.code = code;
    this.status = options.status ?? null;
    if (options.cause !== undefined) {
      (this as { cause?: unknown }).cause = options.cause;
    }
  }
}

const EVM_ADDRESS_PATTERN = /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$/;
const HEX_SIGNATURE_PATTERN = /^0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$/;

/**
 * Describes a value by shape, never by content.
 *
 * Used for every rejected input. The realistic bad "signer address" is a private
 * key pasted into the wrong field, and the realistic bad "signature" is an
 * error string from a signer; echoing either into a message that reaches a log
 * is the leak this function exists to prevent.
 */
function describeOpaque(value: unknown): string {
  if (typeof value === 'string') return `a ${value.length}-character string`;
  if (value === null) return 'null';
  return `a value of type ${typeof value}`;
}

/**
 * Validates an EVM address and returns it lowercased.
 *
 * The lowercase form is the **cache identity**, not what goes on the wire.
 * `POLY_ADDRESS` and the typed data both carry the caller's own string, so a
 * checksummed address stays checksummed for the venue's benefit, while
 * `0xAbC…` and `0xabc…` still resolve to one cache entry — the same split
 * `evmNonceLockKey` makes in `packages/db/src/evm-nonce.ts`, and for the same
 * reason: one account must not yield two keys.
 */
export function normalizeClobSignerAddress(address: string): string {
  const trimmed = typeof address === 'string' ? address.trim() : '';
  if (!EVM_ADDRESS_PATTERN.test(trimmed)) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-address-invalid',
      `signer address must be 0x followed by 40 hex characters, got ${describeOpaque(address)}`
    );
  }
  return trimmed.toLowerCase();
}

/**
 * Credential nonce. `0` unless a principal deliberately holds several sets.
 *
 * Part of the identity of a credential set, so it is part of the cache key: two
 * nonces for one address are two different credential sets, and serving one
 * where the other was asked for would authenticate as the wrong set.
 */
export function normalizeClobNonce(nonce?: number): number {
  const resolved = nonce ?? 0;
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(resolved) || resolved < 0) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-nonce-invalid',
      `credential nonce must be a non-negative safe integer, got ${describeOpaque(nonce)}`
    );
  }
  return resolved;
}

/**
 * Reduces a base URL to its origin.
 *
 * The origin, not the whole URL, because it is a cache-key component and a
 * trailing slash or a stray query string must not split one venue into two
 * entries. It is also the only free-form component of the key, and a serialized
 * origin cannot contain the key separator (see `clobCredentialCacheKey`).
 */
export function normalizeClobOrigin(baseUrl: string): string {
  let url: URL;
  try {
    url = new URL(baseUrl);
  } catch {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-base-url-invalid',
      `CLOB base URL is not a URL, got ${describeOpaque(baseUrl)}`
    );
  }
  if (url.protocol !== 'https:' && url.protocol !== 'http:') {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-base-url-invalid',
      `CLOB base URL must be http or https, got protocol ${url.protocol}`
    );
  }
  return url.origin;
}

/**
 * The cache identity of one credential set.
 *
 * **This is the function that must not collide.** A key that ignored any
 * component would let one principal read another's credentials out of the cache,
 * which is the worst available outcome here: the request succeeds, the venue
 * accepts it, and it authenticates as the wrong account. Every component is
 * therefore part of the key, and each is normalized first so the same identity
 * cannot produce two keys:
 *
 *   * **origin** — staging and production issue unrelated credentials for the
 *     same address, and a test double's origin must never share a key with
 *     production.
 *   * **address**, lowercased — the venue binds credentials to the signer that
 *     produced the L1 signature.
 *   * **nonce** — one address can hold several sets.
 *
 * The key cannot be ambiguous, because the separator `|` cannot appear in any
 * component: a serialized URL origin is scheme, host and optional port with `|`
 * excluded from all three, an EVM address is `0x` plus hex, and a nonce is
 * digits. So key strings and identity triples are one-to-one.
 *
 * Pure and exported for the same reason `evmNonceLockKey` is: getting it wrong
 * fails in two directions and neither is visible at runtime — too coarse and
 * principals share credentials, too fine and every request re-derives.
 */
export function clobCredentialCacheKey(input: {
  readonly signerAddress: string;
  readonly nonce?: number;
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
}): string {
  const origin = normalizeClobOrigin(input.baseUrl ?? CLOB_BASE_URL);
  const address = normalizeClobSignerAddress(input.signerAddress);
  const nonce = normalizeClobNonce(input.nonce);
  return `clob-creds:v1|${origin}|${address}|${nonce}`;
}

/**
 * Which endpoint to use.
 *
 * `create-or-derive` mirrors `@polymarket/client`'s `createOrDeriveApiKey`
 * exactly, including that the fallback is scoped to HTTP 400. The other two
 * exist because a caller that knows which case it is in should say so: Stage 4
 * onboarding creates once, and every later execution derives.
 */
export type ClobCredentialMode = 'create-or-derive' | 'create' | 'derive';

const CREATE_ROUTE = '/auth/api-key';
const DERIVE_ROUTE = '/auth/derive-api-key';
const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

export interface DeriveClobCredentialsInput {
  /** The principal. The only thing that makes this call about one account. */
  readonly signer: ClobL1Signer;
  readonly nonce?: number;
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
  readonly mode?: ClobCredentialMode;
  /**
   * The HTTP transport. **Required, with no default.**
   *
   * Every other injected dependency in this repo defaults (`email.ts` uses
   * `deps.fetchImpl ?? fetch`). This one does not, because the route it calls
   * issues bearer credentials against a real signature: a test that forgot to
   * stub would reach `clob.polymarket.com` with the operator's key. Making the
   * transport a required argument turns that into a compile error.
   */
  readonly fetchImpl: typeof fetch;
  /** Unix **seconds**. Injected so signature fixtures are reproducible. */
  readonly nowSeconds?: () => number;
  readonly timeoutMs?: number;
}

/**
 * Derives one principal's CLOB L2 credentials from its signer.
 *
 * The signer is signed *before* the transport is touched, deliberately: a signer
 * that cannot sign must not produce a venue request, and the ordering means an
 * unstubbed test fails at the signer rather than on the network.
 */
export async function deriveClobCredentials(
  input: DeriveClobCredentialsInput
): Promise<ClobCredentials> {
  const origin = normalizeClobOrigin(input.baseUrl ?? CLOB_BASE_URL);
  // Validated for shape, then kept only as the identity used in messages. What
  // travels on the wire is `input.signer.address` unchanged, because the venue
  // recovers the signer from the signature and the caller owns the checksum.
  const signerAddress = normalizeClobSignerAddress(input.signer.address);
  const nonce = normalizeClobNonce(input.nonce);
  const timestampSeconds = resolveTimestampSeconds(input.nowSeconds);

  const typedData = buildClobAuthTypedData({
    signerAddress: input.signer.address,
    timestampSeconds,
    nonce
  });

  let signature: string;
  try {
    signature = await input.signer.signTypedData(typedData);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-signing-failed',
      `the signer for ${signerAddress} threw ${errorLabel(error)}`
    );
  }
  assertL1Signature(signature);

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    POLY_ADDRESS: input.signer.address,
    POLY_NONCE: String(nonce),
    POLY_SIGNATURE: signature,
    POLY_TIMESTAMP: String(timestampSeconds)
  };

  const mode = input.mode ?? 'create-or-derive';
  const timeoutMs = input.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  const transport = { fetchImpl: input.fetchImpl, origin, headers, timeoutMs };

  if (mode === 'derive') {
    return requireCredentials(
      await requestCredentials({ ...transport, method: 'GET', route: DERIVE_ROUTE })
    );
  }

  const created = await requestCredentials({
    ...transport,
    method: 'POST',
    route: CREATE_ROUTE,
    // Only `create-or-derive` treats 400 as "already exists"; a caller that
    // asked for `create` gets the 400 as the failure it is.
    tolerateAlreadyExists: mode === 'create-or-derive'
  });
  if (created) return created;

  return requireCredentials(
    await requestCredentials({ ...transport, method: 'GET', route: DERIVE_ROUTE })
  );
}

function resolveTimestampSeconds(nowSeconds?: () => number): number {
  const value = nowSeconds ? nowSeconds() : Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value <= 0) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-timestamp-invalid',
      `L1 timestamp must be a positive integer number of seconds, got ${describeOpaque(value)}`
    );
  }
  return value;
}

/** The cause's constructor name only. Never its message. See `ClobCredentialError`. */
function errorLabel(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof Error) return error.name || 'Error';
  return `a non-Error ${typeof error}`;
}

/**
 * Accepts any `0x` hex signature of even byte length.
 *
 * Deliberately **not** a 65-byte check. A Deposit Wallet signs L1 through an
 * ERC-1271 / ERC-7739 wrapper (ADR-0003 section 4: every account deployed on or
 * after 4 May 2026 is a Deposit Wallet), and those signatures are longer than 65
 * bytes. Pinning the length here would reject the majority wallet type.
 */
function assertL1Signature(signature: unknown): asserts signature is string {
  const valid =
    typeof signature === 'string' &&
    HEX_SIGNATURE_PATTERN.test(signature) &&
    signature.length >= 4 &&
    signature.length % 2 === 0;
  if (!valid) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-signature-malformed',
      `the signer returned ${describeOpaque(signature)} instead of a 0x-prefixed hex signature`
    );
  }
}

interface CredentialRequest {
  readonly fetchImpl: typeof fetch;
  readonly origin: string;
  readonly route: string;
  readonly method: 'GET' | 'POST';
  readonly headers: Record<string, string>;
  readonly timeoutMs: number;
  readonly tolerateAlreadyExists?: boolean;
}

/**
 * One call to one auth route. `null` only when a tolerated 400 came back.
 *
 * **The response body never reaches an error message.** On this route a 2xx body
 * *is* the credentials, and there is no guarantee about what a non-2xx body
 * echoes back of the request — so the rejection carries the method, the route and
 * the status, which is what an operator needs, and nothing that could carry a
 * secret.
 */
async function requestCredentials(request: CredentialRequest): Promise<ClobCredentials | null> {
  const label = `${request.method} ${request.route}`;
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), request.timeoutMs);

  let response: Response;
  try {
    response = await request.fetchImpl(`${request.origin}${request.route}`, {
      method: request.method,
      headers: request.headers,
      signal: controller.signal
    });
  } catch (error) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-transport-failed',
      `${label} did not complete`,
      { cause: error }
    );
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }

  if (request.tolerateAlreadyExists && response.status === 400) return null;
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-rejected',
      `${label} returned HTTP ${response.status}`,
      { status: response.status }
    );
  }

  let body: unknown;
  try {
    body = await response.json();
  } catch {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-response-malformed',
      `${label} returned a body that is not JSON`
    );
  }
  return parseClobCredentials(body, label);
}

function requireCredentials(credentials: ClobCredentials | null): ClobCredentials {
  // Unreachable: only a tolerated 400 yields null, and that path never reaches
  // here. Present so the type narrows without a non-null assertion.
  if (!credentials) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-response-malformed',
      'the auth route yielded no credentials'
    );
  }
  return credentials;
}

/**
 * Validates a credential payload, naming fields and never values.
 *
 * **This is the redaction boundary.** The obvious implementation of a
 * "malformed response" error is to interpolate the body, and on this one route
 * the body is two bearer credentials. So each problem is reported as a field
 * name plus a shape, and `describeOpaque` is the only thing allowed near a
 * value.
 *
 * The base64 check is not cosmetic: `signClobL2Request` keys the HMAC on
 * `Buffer.from(secret, 'base64')`, so a `secret` that decodes to zero bytes
 * produces a signature computed with an empty key. That signature is
 * well-formed, 44 characters long, and rejected by the venue on every request —
 * a failure mode with no local symptom at all.
 */
export function parseClobCredentials(body: unknown, route: string): ClobCredentials {
  const record: Record<string, unknown> =
    typeof body === 'object' && body !== null ? (body as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
  const problems: string[] = [];

  const apiKey = readCredentialField(record.apiKey, 'apiKey', problems);
  const secret = readCredentialField(record.secret, 'secret', problems);
  const passphrase = readCredentialField(record.passphrase, 'passphrase', problems);

  if (secret !== null && Buffer.from(secret, 'base64').length === 0) {
    problems.push('secret is not base64 that decodes to any key bytes');
  }

  if (problems.length > 0 || apiKey === null || secret === null || passphrase === null) {
    throw new ClobCredentialError(
      'clob-credential-response-malformed',
      `${route} returned credentials this client cannot use: ${problems.join('; ')}`
    );
  }
  return { apiKey, secret, passphrase };
}

function readCredentialField(
  value: unknown,
  field: string,
  problems: string[]
): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') {
    problems.push(`${field} is ${describeOpaque(value)}, not a string`);
    return null;
  }
  const trimmed = value.trim();
  if (trimmed === '') {
    problems.push(`${field} is an empty string`);
    return null;
  }
  return trimmed;
}

/**
 * Runs a credential set through the same validation a derived one gets.
 *
 * Exported because preconfigured credentials arrive from an operator's
 * environment and are the *more* likely of the two to be mistyped — a truncated
 * `POLYMARKET_API_SECRET` decodes to a short key and fails every L2 request with
 * a venue-side 401 and no local clue.
 */
export function assertUsableClobCredentials(credentials: ClobCredentials): ClobCredentials {
  return parseClobCredentials(credentials, 'preconfigured credentials');
}

export type ClobCredentialSource = 'preconfigured' | 'derived';

export interface ResolveClobCredentialsInput {
  readonly signer: ClobL1Signer;
  /**
   * Credentials the caller already holds, if any.
   *
   * The operator has these when `POLYMARKET_API_KEY` and friends are set. A
   * Stage 4 per-user grant never does. That is a property of the *input*, not of
   * who is asking — which is why there is no principal on this type and no
   * branch on one anywhere in this module.
   */
  readonly preconfigured?: ClobCredentials | null;
  readonly derive: ClobCredentialDeriver;
  readonly nonce?: number;
}

/**
 * The call every principal makes: use the credentials you were given, or derive
 * them from your signer.
 *
 * This is the seam `apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket.ts` becomes a caller of.
 * Before `S3-20` the operator's version of this decision was spread across an
 * environment read, a module-level `ethers.Wallet` built from
 * `process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY` at import, and `createSecureClient`'s own
 * internal derivation — three things a second principal cannot reuse.
 */
export async function resolveClobCredentials(input: ResolveClobCredentialsInput): Promise<{
  readonly credentials: ClobCredentials;
  readonly source: ClobCredentialSource;
}> {
  const nonce = normalizeClobNonce(input.nonce);
  if (input.preconfigured) {
    return {
      credentials: assertUsableClobCredentials(input.preconfigured),
      source: 'preconfigured'
    };
  }
  return { credentials: await input.derive(input.signer, { nonce }), source: 'derived' };
}

/**
 * A per-signer credential cache.
 *
 * Credentials have **no documented expiry or rotation** on this venue (ADR-0003
 * section 4.2), so re-deriving per request would burn an L1 signature and a
 * round trip for a value that never changes. Caching is therefore worth doing —
 * and is also the single most dangerous thing in this module, because a cache
 * keyed too coarsely hands one principal another's credentials and the resulting
 * request succeeds.
 */
export interface ClobCredentialStore {
  credentialsFor(
    signer: ClobL1Signer,
    options?: { readonly nonce?: number }
  ): Promise<ClobCredentials>;
  /** The cache keys held. Addresses and origins only — safe to log. */
  keys(): readonly string[];
  size(): number;
  /** Drops one entry, e.g. after the venue rejects its credentials. */
  invalidate(signer: ClobL1Signer, options?: { readonly nonce?: number }): boolean;
  clear(): void;
}

export interface ClobCredentialStoreOptions {
  /**
   * How to derive for a signer that is not cached. No default: the store holds
   * no transport, so a caller must decide what talks to the venue.
   */
  readonly derive: ClobCredentialDeriver;
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
  /**
   * Overridable **only so the collision guard below can be tested**. Production
   * callers must leave this alone; a key function that drops a component is
   * exactly the defect the guard exists to catch.
   */
  readonly cacheKeyFor?: (input: {
    readonly signerAddress: string;
    readonly nonce: number;
    readonly baseUrl: string;
  }) => string;
}

interface CacheEntry {
  readonly signerAddress: string;
  readonly nonce: number;
  readonly origin: string;
  readonly credentials: Promise<ClobCredentials>;
}

export function createClobCredentialStore(
  options: ClobCredentialStoreOptions
): ClobCredentialStore {
  const baseUrl = options.baseUrl ?? CLOB_BASE_URL;
  const origin = normalizeClobOrigin(baseUrl);
  const keyFor = options.cacheKeyFor ?? clobCredentialCacheKey;
  const entries = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();

  function identify(signer: ClobL1Signer, given?: { readonly nonce?: number }) {
    const signerAddress = normalizeClobSignerAddress(signer.address);
    const nonce = normalizeClobNonce(given?.nonce);
    return { signerAddress, nonce, key: keyFor({ signerAddress, nonce, baseUrl }) };
  }

  return {
    async credentialsFor(signer, given) {
      const { signerAddress, nonce, key } = identify(signer, given);
      const existing = entries.get(key);
      if (existing) {
        // The outbound half of the guard, in the spirit of `authorizeThrough` in
        // `execution-authority.ts`: the key says these credentials belong here,
        // and this re-checks the identity they were stored under. Belt and
        // braces, because "the cache served the wrong principal" produces a
        // successful venue request and is undetectable downstream.
        if (
          existing.signerAddress !== signerAddress ||
          existing.nonce !== nonce ||
          existing.origin !== origin
        ) {
          throw new ClobCredentialError(
            'clob-credential-cache-collision',
            `cache key ${key} holds credentials for ${existing.signerAddress} nonce ` +
              `${existing.nonce}; refusing to serve them to ${signerAddress} nonce ${nonce}`
          );
        }
        return existing.credentials;
      }

      // Stored before the first await, so two concurrent calls for one signer
      // share one derivation rather than racing two L1 signatures.
      const pending = options.derive(signer, { nonce });
      entries.set(key, { signerAddress, nonce, origin, credentials: pending });
      pending.catch(() => {
        // A rejected derivation must not be cached: the next call would replay
        // the same failure forever without ever retrying the venue. Guarded on
        // identity so a retry already in flight is not evicted.
        if (entries.get(key)?.credentials === pending) entries.delete(key);
      });
      return pending;
    },

    keys() {
      return [...entries.keys()];
    },

    size() {
      return entries.size;
    },

    invalidate(signer, given) {
      return entries.delete(identify(signer, given).key);
    },

    clear() {
      entries.clear();
    }
  };
}

export interface FetchClobCredentialsInput {
  readonly address: string;
  readonly signature: string;
  readonly timestampSeconds: number;
  readonly nonce?: number;
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
  readonly fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
}

/**
 * Calls Polymarket CLOB auth endpoints using an existing L1 EIP-712 signature
 * (e.g. produced by a browser wallet via eth_signTypedData_v4).
 *
 * Tries POST /auth/api-key first, and on HTTP 400 falls back to GET /auth/derive-api-key.
 */
export async function fetchClobCredentialsFromSignature(
  input: FetchClobCredentialsInput
): Promise<ClobCredentials> {
  const fetchImpl = input.fetchImpl ?? globalThis.fetch;
  const origin = normalizeClobOrigin(input.baseUrl ?? CLOB_BASE_URL);
  normalizeClobSignerAddress(input.address);
  const nonce = normalizeClobNonce(input.nonce);
  assertL1Signature(input.signature);

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    POLY_ADDRESS: input.address,
    POLY_NONCE: String(nonce),
    POLY_SIGNATURE: input.signature,
    POLY_TIMESTAMP: String(input.timestampSeconds)
  };

  const transport = {
    fetchImpl,
    origin,
    headers,
    timeoutMs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS
  };

  const created = await requestCredentials({
    ...transport,
    method: 'POST',
    route: CREATE_ROUTE,
    tolerateAlreadyExists: true
  });
  if (created) return created;

  return requireCredentials(
    await requestCredentials({
      ...transport,
      method: 'GET',
      route: DERIVE_ROUTE
    })
  );
}

// Re-exported from the authority module rather than redeclared. Two independent
// literals for the same chain id in one package is exactly what drifts: a future
// testnet or chain-id change would be applied to one and not the other, and the
// symptom (prices resolve, permissions deny) would look unrelated to the cause.
import { ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID } from './authority/permission-policy.js';
import { resolveChainValue } from './address.js';
import type { Chain } from './types.js';

const PRICE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.PRICE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 8000);
const ROBINHOOD_API_BASE_URL = 'https://api.robinhood.com/rhj';
const ROBINHOOD_ASSET_CACHE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
const ROBINHOOD_PRICE_MAX_AGE_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000;

export type DexScreenerChainId = 'solana' | 'polygon' | 'robinhood' | 'base' | 'ethereum' | 'bsc';

export type DexScreenerPair = {
  chainId: string;
  priceUsd?: string | number | null;
  liquidity?: {
    usd?: string | number | null;
  } | null;
  baseToken?: {
    address?: string;
    name?: string;
    symbol?: string;
  } | null;
};

const DEX_SCREENER_CHAIN_IDS: Readonly<Record<Chain, DexScreenerChainId>> = {
  solana: 'solana',
  polygon: 'polygon',
  'robinhood-chain': 'robinhood',
  base: 'base',
  ethereum: 'ethereum',
  bsc: 'bsc'
};

type RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo = {
  symbol: string;
  multiplier: number;
};

let robinhoodAssetCache:
  | {
      expiresAt: number;
      byAddress: Map<string, RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo>;
    }
  | null = null;
let robinhoodAssetRequest: Promise<Map<string, RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo> | null> | null = null;

async function fetchWithTimeout(url: string, timeoutMs = PRICE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<Response> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
  try {
    return await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal });
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null;
}

function parsePositiveNumber(value: unknown): number | null {
  const parsed = typeof value === 'number'
    ? value
    : typeof value === 'string'
      ? Number(value)
      : Number.NaN;
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : null;
}

function hasRobinhoodDeployment(value: unknown, tokenAddress: string): boolean {
  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return false;
  return value.some((deployment) => (
    isRecord(deployment)
    && deployment.chainId === ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID
    && typeof deployment.contractAddress === 'string'
    && deployment.contractAddress.toLowerCase() === tokenAddress
  ));
}

function parseRobinhoodAssetIndex(data: unknown): Map<string, RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo> {
  const byAddress = new Map<string, RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo>();
  if (!isRecord(data) || !Array.isArray(data.assets)) return byAddress;

  for (const asset of data.assets) {
    if (
      !isRecord(asset)
      || asset.status !== 'ASSET_STATUS_ACTIVE'
      || typeof asset.tokenSymbol !== 'string'
      || asset.tokenSymbol.length === 0
    ) {
      continue;
    }

    const multiplier = parsePositiveNumber(asset.currentMultiplier);
    if (multiplier === null || !Array.isArray(asset.deployments)) continue;

    for (const deployment of asset.deployments) {
      if (
        !isRecord(deployment)
        || deployment.chainId !== ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID
        || typeof deployment.contractAddress !== 'string'
      ) {
        continue;
      }

      byAddress.set(deployment.contractAddress.toLowerCase(), {
        symbol: asset.tokenSymbol,
        multiplier
      });
    }
  }

  return byAddress;
}

async function getRobinhoodAssetIndex(): Promise<Map<string, RobinhoodAssetPriceInfo> | null> {
  const now = Date.now();
  if (robinhoodAssetCache && robinhoodAssetCache.expiresAt > now) {
    return robinhoodAssetCache.byAddress;
  }
  if (robinhoodAssetRequest) return robinhoodAssetRequest;

  robinhoodAssetRequest = (async () => {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(`${ROBINHOOD_API_BASE_URL}/assets`);
    if (!response.ok) return null;

    const byAddress = parseRobinhoodAssetIndex(await response.json());
    robinhoodAssetCache = {
      expiresAt: Date.now() + ROBINHOOD_ASSET_CACHE_MS,
      byAddress
    };
    return byAddress;
  })();

  try {
    return await robinhoodAssetRequest;
  } finally {
    robinhoodAssetRequest = null;
  }
}

export function getDexScreenerChainId(chain: Chain): DexScreenerChainId {
  return DEX_SCREENER_CHAIN_IDS[chain];
}

function getPairLiquidityUsd(pair: DexScreenerPair): number {
  const rawLiquidity = pair.liquidity?.usd;
  const liquidity = typeof rawLiquidity === 'number'
    ? rawLiquidity
    : typeof rawLiquidity === 'string'
      ? Number(rawLiquidity)
      : 0;
  return Number.isFinite(liquidity) ? liquidity : 0;
}

export function selectDexScreenerPair(
  pairs: unknown,
  chain: Chain
): DexScreenerPair | null {
  if (!Array.isArray(pairs)) return null;

  const expectedChainId = getDexScreenerChainId(chain);
  let selected: DexScreenerPair | null = null;

  for (const candidate of pairs) {
    if (
      !isRecord(candidate)
      || !('chainId' in candidate)
      || candidate.chainId !== expectedChainId
    ) {
      continue;
    }

    const pair = candidate as DexScreenerPair;
    if (selected === null || getPairLiquidityUsd(pair) > getPairLiquidityUsd(selected)) {
      selected = pair;
    }
  }

  return selected;
}

async function fetchDexScreenerPair(
  tokenMint: string,
  requestedChain?: Chain
): Promise<DexScreenerPair | null> {
  const { chain, raw: cleanMint } = resolveChainValue(tokenMint, requestedChain);
  const response = await fetchWithTimeout(`https://api.dexscreener.com/latest/dex/tokens/${cleanMint}`);
  if (!response.ok) return null;

  const data = await response.json() as { pairs?: unknown };
  return selectDexScreenerPair(data.pairs, chain);
}

export async function fetchDexScreenerPrice(
  tokenMint: string,
  requestedChain?: Chain
): Promise<number | null> {
  const resolved = resolveChainValue(tokenMint, requestedChain);
  try {
    const pair = await fetchDexScreenerPair(resolved.raw, resolved.chain);
    if (!pair) return null;

    const rawPrice = pair.priceUsd;
    const price = typeof rawPrice === 'number'
      ? rawPrice
      : typeof rawPrice === 'string'
        ? Number.parseFloat(rawPrice)
        : Number.NaN;
    return Number.isFinite(price) ? price : null;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[prices] DexScreener error for ${resolved.raw} on ${resolved.chain}:`, error);
    return null;
  }
}

export async function fetchDexScreenerLiquidity(
  tokenMint: string,
  requestedChain?: Chain
): Promise<number | null> {
  const resolved = resolveChainValue(tokenMint, requestedChain);
  try {
    const pair = await fetchDexScreenerPair(resolved.raw, resolved.chain);
    return pair ? getPairLiquidityUsd(pair) : null;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(
      `[prices] DexScreener liquidity error for ${resolved.raw} on ${resolved.chain}:`,
      error
    );
    return null;
  }
}

export async function fetchRobinhoodChainPrice(tokenMint: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const { raw: cleanMint } = resolveChainValue(tokenMint, 'robinhood-chain');
  try {
    const assetIndex = await getRobinhoodAssetIndex();
    const asset = assetIndex?.get(cleanMint);
    if (!asset) return null;

    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(
      `${ROBINHOOD_API_BASE_URL}/prices/${encodeURIComponent(asset.symbol)}`
    );
    if (!response.ok) return null;

    const data = await response.json() as unknown;
    if (!isRecord(data) || !Array.isArray(data.quotes)) return null;

    const quote = data.quotes.find((candidate) => (
      isRecord(candidate)
      && candidate.tokenSymbol === asset.symbol
      && candidate.isTradingHalt === false
      && hasRobinhoodDeployment(candidate.deployments, cleanMint)
    ));
    if (!isRecord(quote)) return null;

    const bid = parsePositiveNumber(quote.bid);
    const ask = parsePositiveNumber(quote.ask);
    if (bid === null || ask === null || typeof quote.generatedAt !== 'string') return null;

    const generatedAt = Date.parse(quote.generatedAt);
    const ageMs = Date.now() - generatedAt;
    if (
      !Number.isFinite(generatedAt)
      || ageMs < -30_000
      || ageMs > ROBINHOOD_PRICE_MAX_AGE_MS
    ) {
      return null;
    }

    const price = ((bid + ask) / 2) * asset.multiplier;
    return Number.isFinite(price) && price > 0 ? price : null;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[prices] Robinhood Chain price error for ${cleanMint}:`, error);
    return null;
  }
}

export async function fetchCoinGeckoPrice(
  tokenMint: string,
  chain: Exclude<Chain, 'robinhood-chain'> = 'solana'
): Promise<number | null> {
  const cleanMint = tokenMint.includes(':') ? tokenMint.split(':')[1] : tokenMint;
  const platform = chain === 'polygon' ? 'polygon-pos' : 'solana';
  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(`https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/token_price/${platform}?contract_addresses=${cleanMint}&vs_currencies=usd`);
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const data = await response.json() as any;
    
    const key = cleanMint.toLowerCase();
    if (data[key] && data[key].usd) {
      return data[key].usd;
    }
    if (data[cleanMint] && data[cleanMint].usd) {
      return data[cleanMint].usd;
    }
    return null;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[prices] CoinGecko error for ${cleanMint} on ${chain}:`, error);
    return null;
  }
}

export async function fetchJupiterPrice(tokenMint: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const cleanMint = tokenMint.includes(':') ? tokenMint.split(':')[1] : tokenMint;
  try {
    const response = await fetchWithTimeout(`https://lite-api.jup.ag/price/v3?ids=${cleanMint}`);
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const data = await response.json() as Record<string, { usdPrice?: number } | undefined>;
    const price = data?.[cleanMint]?.usdPrice;
    return typeof price === 'number' && Number.isFinite(price) ? price : null;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[prices] Jupiter error for ${cleanMint}:`, error);
    return null;
  }
}

export async function fetchTokenPriceUsd(tokenMint: string): Promise<number | null> {
  const { chain, raw: cleanMint } = resolveChainValue(tokenMint);

  if (chain === 'robinhood-chain') {
    const officialPrice = await fetchRobinhoodChainPrice(cleanMint);
    if (officialPrice !== null) return officialPrice;

    const dexPrice = await fetchDexScreenerPrice(cleanMint, chain);
    return dexPrice !== null && !isNaN(dexPrice) ? dexPrice : null;
  }

  // Try DexScreener first (supports all chains)
  let price = await fetchDexScreenerPrice(cleanMint, chain);
  if (price !== null && !isNaN(price)) {
    return price;
  }

  // Fallback to CoinGecko
  price = await fetchCoinGeckoPrice(cleanMint, chain);
  if (price !== null && !isNaN(price)) {
    return price;
  }

  // Fallback to Jupiter (Solana only)
  if (chain === 'solana') {
    price = await fetchJupiterPrice(cleanMint);
    if (price !== null && !isNaN(price)) {
      return price;
    }
  }

  return null;
}

export async function fetchTokenMetadata(tokenMint: string): Promise<{ name: string; symbol: string } | null> {
  const { chain, raw: cleanMint } = resolveChainValue(tokenMint);

  // 1. Try Helius DAS API getAsset (Solana only)
  if (chain === 'solana') {
    const HELIUS_API_KEY = process.env.HELIUS_API_KEY;
    if (HELIUS_API_KEY) {
      try {
        const rpcUrl = `https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=${HELIUS_API_KEY}`;
        const response = await fetch(rpcUrl, {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({
            jsonrpc: '2.0',
            id: 'token-metadata',
            method: 'getAsset',
            params: { id: cleanMint }
          })
        });
        if (response.ok) {
          const json = await response.json() as any;
          if (!json.error && json.result?.content?.metadata) {
            const name = json.result.content.metadata.name || 'Unknown';
            const symbol = json.result.content.metadata.symbol || 'UNKNOWN';
            return { name, symbol };
          }
        }
      } catch (error) {
        console.error(`[prices] Helius getAsset error for ${cleanMint}:`, error);
      }
    }
  }

  // 2. Fallback to DexScreener (supports all chains)
  try {
    const pair = await fetchDexScreenerPair(cleanMint, chain);
    const base = pair?.baseToken;
    if (base?.name && base?.symbol) {
      return { name: base.name, symbol: base.symbol };
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[prices] DexScreener metadata error for ${cleanMint} on ${chain}:`, error);
  }

  return null;
}
